exarchate-of-africa.t: The last Byzantine government of North Africa, a frontier exarchate at Carthage that launched Heraclius to the imperial throne.
exarchate-of-africa.o: Around 591 the emperor Maurice replaced the [[s:praetorian-prefecture-of-africa|Praetorian Prefecture of Africa]] with an exarchate, uniting civil and military authority in one governor at [[e:carthage|Carthage]] to face [[e:berbers|Berber]] pressure. The first known exarch was [[e:gennadius-exarch-of-africa|Gennadius]], who had defeated the Berber king [[e:garmul|Garmul]] in 578.
exarchate-of-africa.r: The exarchate covered the coast from [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] to [[s:septem|Septem]], with [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] and [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]], and drew wealth from grain and [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]]. In 608 the exarch [[e:heraclius-the-elder|Heraclius the Elder]] revolted against the emperor [[e:phocas|Phocas]], and his son [[e:heraclius|Heraclius]] sailed from [[e:carthage|Carthage]] to take [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 610. In 646 the exarch [[e:gregory-the-patrician|Gregory the Patrician]] declared himself emperor, but was killed by an Arab army at [[e:sufetula|Sufetula]] in 647.
exarchate-of-africa.e: Arab raids grew into conquest. [[e:carthage|Carthage]] fell to [[e:hassan-ibn-al-numan|Hassan ibn al-Numan]] in 695, was briefly retaken in 697 and fell for good in 698 to the [[s:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad Caliphate]]. The [[e:arabs|Arabs]] built up nearby [[e:tunis|Tunis]], an ancient town, as their base, and only [[s:septem|Septem]] held out until around 711.

erdini.t: People of north-western Ireland recorded by Ptolemy, usually placed around Lough Erne and linked by name with the Érainn.
erdini.o: The Erdini are named in [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150, placed inland in the north-west of Ireland, usually located around [[e:lough-erne|Lough Erne]] in modern [[e:county-fermanagh|Fermanagh]] and neighbouring parts of [[e:county-donegal|Donegal]]. Their name is often compared with Erne and with the [[s:iverni|Érainn]], a population group of early Irish genealogies.
erdini.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers, settlements or customs. The lakeland around [[e:lough-erne|Lough Erne]] was well suited to crannogs and [[e:cattle|cattle]] farming, and if the name link with the [[s:iverni|Érainn]] holds, they belonged to a widespread group that early Irish historians regarded as one of the ancient peoples of Ireland.
erdini.e: The Erdini do not reappear in any source. Their territory later fell within the lands of the [[s:kingdom-of-airgialla|Kingdom of Airgialla]] and the northern [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]].

empire-of-thessalonica.t: Short-lived Greek empire founded when Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus took Thessalonica in 1224 and claimed the Byzantine throne.
empire-of-thessalonica.o: [[e:theodore-komnenos-doukas|Theodore Komnenos Doukas]], ruler of the [[s:despotate-of-epirus|Despotate of Epirus]], steadily conquered the [[s:kingdom-of-thessalonica|Kingdom of Thessalonica]] and captured the city in 1224. Around 1227 he was crowned emperor by [[e:demetrios-chomatenos|Demetrios Chomatenos]], archbishop of [[e:ohrid|Ohrid]], challenging the [[s:empire-of-nicaea|Empire of Nicaea]] for leadership of the Byzantine world and preparing to march on [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]].
empire-of-thessalonica.r: Theodore ruled a realm stretching from the Adriatic to [[e:thrace|Thrace]], with Byzantine court titles and administration, and quarrelled with [[e:nicaea|Nicaea's]] patriarch over church authority. In 1230 he attacked [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] but was defeated and captured by [[e:ivan-asen-ii|Ivan Asen II]] at [[e:battle-of-klokotnitsa|Klokotnitsa]] and later blinded. His brother Manuel then ruled as a Bulgarian client.
empire-of-thessalonica.e: Theodore regained [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]] for his son John, who in 1242 had to accept the lesser title of despot from [[e:john-iii-doukas-vatatzes|John III Vatatzes]]. In 1246 Vatatzes took Thessalonica from John's brother [[e:demetrios-angelos-doukas|Demetrios]], annexing it to the [[s:empire-of-nicaea|Empire of Nicaea]].

emirate-of-nejd.t: The second Saudi state, which revived Al Saud rule from Riyadh after the destruction of Diriyah, until the Rashidis overthrew it.
emirate-of-nejd.o: Six years after the Ottoman-Egyptian destruction of the [[s:emirate-of-diriyah|Emirate of Diriyah]], [[e:turki-ibn-abdullah|Turki ibn Abdullah]], a grandson of [[e:muhammad-ibn-saud|Muhammad ibn Saud]], drove the Egyptian garrison from [[e:riyadh|Riyadh]] in 1824 and made it his capital. He restored Saudi rule over [[e:najd|Najd]] and [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Hasa]] and renewed the alliance with the Wahhabi scholars.
emirate-of-nejd.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] was smaller than its predecessor and avoided war with the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], leaving the holy cities alone. [[e:faisal-ibn-turki-al-saud|Faisal ibn Turki]], who ruled twice, consolidated it; between his reigns [[e:egypt|Egypt]] occupied [[e:riyadh|Riyadh]] again from 1838 to 1843. The state taxed oasis farmers and tribes and drew on [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]] trade through [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Hasa]] and [[e:qatif|Qatif]]. The [[s:emirate-of-jabal-shammar|Emirate of Jabal Shammar]] in the north was at first a loyal ally.
emirate-of-nejd.e: After Faisal died in 1865, his sons Abdullah and Saud fought a long civil war, and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] took [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Hasa]] in 1871. [[e:muhammad-ibn-rashid|Muhammad ibn Rashid]] of Ha'il took [[e:riyadh|Riyadh]] in 1887 and defeated the [[e:house-of-saud|Al Saud]] at [[e:battle-of-mulayda|Mulayda]] in 1891; the family fled to the [[s:sheikhdom-of-kuwait|Sheikhdom of Kuwait]].

electorate-of-cologne.t: The prince-archbishopric of Cologne, one of the seven electors, whose archbishops crowned German kings and ruled a long strip of the Rhineland.
electorate-of-cologne.o: [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] had been an archbishopric since the 8th century. In 953 [[e:otto-i-duke-of-bavaria|Otto I]] made his brother [[e:bruno-the-great|Bruno]] archbishop and also duke of [[s:duchy-of-lotharingia|Lotharingia]], founding the temporal power of the see. Grants of counties and, in 1180, the [[s:duchy-of-westphalia|Duchy of Westphalia]] after the fall of [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] made the archbishops major territorial princes.
electorate-of-cologne.r: The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] confirmed the archbishop as one of the seven [[e:prince-elector|electors]] and arch-chancellor of [[e:italy|Italy]]. After long conflicts with the citizens and the archbishop's defeat at the [[e:battle-of-worringen|Battle of Worringen]] in 1288, [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] became in effect a free city, and the electors moved to [[e:bonn|Bonn]]. The [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] family held the see from 1583 to 1761, building the palaces at [[e:bruhl-rhineland|Brühl]] and Bonn.
electorate-of-cologne.e: [[e:french-revolutionary-occupation-of-the-netherlands|French revolutionary armies]] took the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]] in 1794, and the electorate was dissolved in 1803; [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]] went to [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]] and other lands to [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]]. After 1815 the territories became Prussian. [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] Cathedral, begun in 1248, was completed in 1880.

estado-novo-portugal.t: Salazar's authoritarian New State, one of Europe's longest-lived dictatorships, which fought to keep Portugal's African empire.
estado-novo-portugal.o: The constitution of 1933, approved by plebiscite, turned the [[s:ditadura-nacional|Ditadura Nacional]] into a corporatist regime under prime minister [[e:antonio-de-oliveira-salazar|António de Oliveira Salazar]], inspired by Catholic social teaching and the idea of an organic nation.
estado-novo-portugal.r: The regime banned parties except the [[e:national-union-portugal|National Union]], censored the press and used the [[e:pide|PVDE]], later PIDE, secret police and the [[e:tarrafal-camp|Tarrafal]] prison camp against opponents. Portugal stayed neutral in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]], leased the [[e:azores|Azores]] to the [[e:allies|Allies]] and joined [[e:nato|NATO]] in 1949. Its economy remained poor, prompting mass emigration, while from 1961 it fought costly colonial wars in [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]], [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]] and [[e:guinea-bissau|Guinea-Bissau]].
estado-novo-portugal.e: [[e:marcelo-caetano|Marcelo Caetano]] succeeded [[e:antonio-de-oliveira-salazar|Salazar]] in 1968 but failed to end the wars. On 25 April 1974 the [[e:armed-forces-movement|Armed Forces Movement]] overthrew the regime in the [[e:carnation-revolution|Carnation Revolution]], founding the [[s:third-portuguese-republic|Third Portuguese Republic]].

electorate-of-baden.t: Baden's three years as an electorate, when the Napoleonic settlement doubled its territory and set it on the way to a grand duchy.
electorate-of-baden.o: Margrave [[e:charles-frederick-grand-duke-of-baden|Charles Frederick]] had united the two [[e:baden|Baden]] margraviates in 1771. In the [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Imperial Recess of 1803]] he gained the Palatinate's right-bank lands around [[e:heidelberg|Heidelberg]] and [[e:mannheim|Mannheim]], parts of the bishoprics of [[e:konstanz|Constance]], [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-strasbourg|Strasbourg]], and several imperial cities, and was raised to elector.
electorate-of-baden.r: [[e:charles-frederick-grand-duke-of-baden|Charles Frederick]] was a reforming ruler who had abolished [[e:serfdom|serfdom]] in 1783. As elector he integrated the new lands, whose Catholic and Protestant populations had to be combined, with a new administration and courts, and the [[e:heidelberg-university|University of Heidelberg]] was reorganised in 1803. [[e:baden|Baden]] allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] in the 1805 campaign.
electorate-of-baden.e: After the Peace of [[e:bratislava|Pressburg]] [[e:baden|Baden]] gained the [[e:breisgau|Breisgau]] from [[e:austria|Austria]]. In 1806 it joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] and [[e:charles-frederick-grand-duke-of-baden|Charles Frederick]] took the title of Grand Duke, forming the [[s:grand-duchy-of-baden|Grand Duchy of Baden]].

early-dynastic-egypt.t: The First and Second Dynasties, which turned a newly united Nile valley into the kingdom of the pharaohs.
early-dynastic-egypt.o: [[e:egypt|Egypt]] was united around 3100 BCE when the Thinite king [[e:narmer|Narmer]], followed by [[e:hor-aha|Hor-Aha]] (often identified with the legendary [[e:menes|Menes]]), brought the Delta under the southern kingship. A new capital, [[e:memphis-egypt|Memphis]], was founded where the [[e:nile|Nile]] valley meets the Delta, and the [[e:old-babylonian-empire|First Dynasty]] began, succeeding the [[s:proto-kingdom-of-thinis|Proto-kingdom of Thinis]].
early-dynastic-egypt.r: The kings of the First and Second Dynasties created the lasting institutions of pharaonic [[e:egypt|Egypt]]: a court and treasury, taxation recorded in hieroglyphs, the double crown and the royal titulary. Early [[e:old-babylonian-empire|First Dynasty]] kings were buried at [[s:abydos|Abydos]] with sacrificed retainers, while officials built great mastaba tombs at [[e:saqqara|Saqqara]]. Den first used the title 'King of Upper and [[e:lower-egypt|Lower Egypt]]', and expeditions reached Sinai and [[e:nubia|Nubia]] for [[e:copper|copper]] and stone.
early-dynastic-egypt.e: The [[e:second-dynasty-of-egypt|Second Dynasty]] saw unrest, with [[e:peribsen|Peribsen]] adopting [[e:seth|Seth]] rather than [[e:horus|Horus]] as his patron, before [[e:khasekhemwy|Khasekhemwy]] reunited the country. His successors of the [[e:third-dynasty-of-egypt|Third Dynasty]], from around 2686 BCE, opened the [[s:old-kingdom-of-egypt|Old Kingdom of Egypt]] and its age of pyramid building.

ezhimala-kingdom.t: The Mushika kingdom of northern Kerala around the coastal hill of Ezhimala, whose kings had their history written in a Sanskrit court epic.
ezhimala-kingdom.o: [[e:ezhimala|Ezhimala]], a hill on the coast north of [[e:kannur|Kannur]], was the seat of chiefs praised in [[e:sangam-literature|Sangam]] poetry, notably [[e:nannan|Nannan]], a powerful and sometimes ruthless ruler. In later centuries the region was ruled by the [[e:mushika-dynasty|Mushika dynasty]], whose land lay north of the [[e:chera-dynasty|Chera]] kingdom.
ezhimala-kingdom.r: The [[e:mushikavamsa|Mushikavamsa]], a [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] poem written by the court poet Atula in the 11th century, traces the dynasty's legendary origins and lists its kings, though its early chronology is unreliable. Inscriptions show the later Mushika kings ruling through local chiefs and endowing [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] temples. The coast traded [[e:pepper|pepper]] and other [[e:spice-trade|spices]] with Arab and Persian merchants.
ezhimala-kingdom.e: From the 12th century the Mushika realm became the kingdom of [[s:kolathunadu|Kolathunadu]] under the Kolathiri rajas, who ruled northern [[e:malabar-coast|Malabar]] until the 18th century and met [[e:vasco-da-gama|Vasco da Gama's]] successors.

eastern-zhou.t: The age of the Zhou kings at Luoyang, whose real power faded while the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods produced Confucius, Laozi and the Hundred Schools of Thought.
eastern-zhou.o: After the [[e:quanrong|Quanrong]] sacked [[e:haojing|Haojing]] in 771 BCE, [[e:king-ping-of-zhou|King Ping]] moved the court east to [[e:luoyang|Luoyi]] (Luoyang), under the protection of the [[s:state-of-jin|State of Jin]] and the [[s:state-of-zheng|State of Zheng]], beginning the Eastern Zhou.
eastern-zhou.r: The kings kept their ritual supremacy but lost real authority. In the Spring and Autumn period (770 to 476 BCE) hegemons such as the [[s:state-of-qi|State of Qi]] and the [[s:state-of-jin|State of Jin]] led the states in the king's name; in the [[e:warring-states-period|Warring States period]] the great states fought wars of annihilation. Iron tools, coinage, cities and bureaucracies spread, and thinkers from [[e:confucius|Confucius]] to [[e:han-fei|Han Feizi]] debated how to restore order.
eastern-zhou.e: The royal domain split into the [[s:duchy-of-western-zhou|Duchy of Western Zhou]] and the [[s:duchy-of-eastern-zhou|Duchy of Eastern Zhou]]. In 256 BCE the [[s:state-of-qin|State of Qin]] seized [[e:wangcheng|Wangcheng]] and [[e:king-nan-of-zhou|King Nan]], the last Zhou king, died. Its intellectual legacy shaped Chinese civilisation for the next two thousand years.
eastern-zhou.re: Zhou ancestral religion and worship of Heaven

emirate-of-afghanistan.t: The Barakzai state that reunited Afghanistan, fought two wars with Britain and had its borders fixed by the Great Game.
emirate-of-afghanistan.o: After the collapse of [[e:sadozai|Sadozai]] power, [[e:dost-mohammad-khan|Dost Mohammad Khan]] of the [[e:barakzai-dynasty|Barakzai]] clan took [[e:kabul|Kabul]] in 1826 and assumed the title emir in the mid-1830s, building on Barakzai control from 1823. He was deposed by a British invasion in 1839 during the [[e:first-anglo-afghan-war|First Anglo-Afghan War]] but returned in 1842 and later reunited [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]] and [[e:herat|Herat]].
emirate-of-afghanistan.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled a fragmented tribal society, with power resting on [[e:pashtuns|Pashtun]] tribal chiefs. After the [[e:second-anglo-afghan-war|Second Anglo-Afghan War]] of 1878 to 1880, [[e:abdur-rahman-khan|Abdur Rahman Khan]], the 'Iron Emir', centralised power, crushed revolts and annexed the [[e:hazarajat|Hazarajat]], while [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] controlled foreign policy. The [[e:durand-line|Durand Line]] of 1893 and Anglo-Russian agreements set the borders.
emirate-of-afghanistan.e: In 1919 [[e:amanullah-khan|Amanullah Khan]] fought the [[e:third-anglo-afghan-war|Third Anglo-Afghan War]] and won full independence. In 1926 he took the title king, turning the [[e:emirate|emirate]] into the [[s:kingdom-of-afghanistan|Kingdom of Afghanistan]].

eighth-dynasty-of-egypt.t: The last Memphite kings after the collapse of the Old Kingdom, a dynasty of many brief reigns at the start of the First Intermediate Period.
eighth-dynasty-of-egypt.o: After the long reign of [[e:pepi-ii|Pepi II]] and the end of the Sixth Dynasty, a line of kings at [[e:memphis-egypt|Memphis]] claimed to continue the [[s:old-kingdom-of-egypt|Old Kingdom of Egypt]] around 2181 BCE. [[e:manetho|Manetho's]] [[e:seventh-dynasty-of-egypt|Seventh Dynasty]], of 'seventy kings in seventy days', is now usually regarded as fictitious, and its kings are counted with the Eighth.
eighth-dynasty-of-egypt.r: The [[s:abydos|Abydos]] king list names around a dozen or more rulers in roughly twenty years, most known only by name. [[e:qakare-ibi|Qakare Ibi]] built a small pyramid at [[e:saqqara|Saqqara]] inscribed with [[e:pyramid-texts|Pyramid Texts]], and decrees of [[e:neferkauhor|Neferkauhor]] found at [[e:coptos|Coptos]] show royal favour granted to a powerful local family. Real power was passing to provincial governors, and [[e:nile|Nile]] floods appear to have been low.
eighth-dynasty-of-egypt.e: Around 2160 BCE the Memphite line was displaced by rulers from [[e:herakleopolis-magna|Herakleopolis]], who founded the [[s:herakleopolitan-kingdom|Herakleopolitan Kingdom]]. Its brief, obscure history marks the end of [[s:old-kingdom-of-egypt|Old Kingdom]] unity and the beginning of the [[e:first-intermediate-period|First Intermediate Period]].

ekiti-parapo.t: An alliance of Ekiti, Ijesha and other Yoruba states that fought Ibadan to a standstill in the Kiriji war, one of the longest wars of 19th-century Africa.
ekiti-parapo.o: From the 1850s [[s:ibadan|Ibadan]] dominated the [[e:ekiti-people|Ekiti]] and [[s:ijesha-kingdom|Ijesha]] towns of eastern [[e:yorubaland|Yorubaland]], collecting tribute through resident agents. In 1877-1878 these towns rose in revolt and formed the Ekiti Parapo, meaning Ekiti together, joining forces with the Ijesha general [[e:ogedengbe|Ogedengbe]] and allies from [[e:igbomina|Igbomina]] and [[s:ilorin-emirate|Ilorin]].
ekiti-parapo.r: The alliance had no single ruler; it was a military coalition of kings and war chiefs, led in the field by men such as [[e:ogedengbe|Ogedengbe]] and Fabunmi of Oke-Mesi. Its soldiers, including [[e:ekiti-people|Ekiti]] who had returned from [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]], used [[e:breech-loading-rifle|breech-loading rifles]] bought through the coast. The main armies faced [[s:ibadan|Ibadan]] for years in [[e:fortified-camp|fortified camps]] at Kiriji, near [[e:igbajo|Igbajo]].
ekiti-parapo.e: Missionaries and [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]] officials brokered a peace in 1886, but full settlement came only in 1893, when the Governor of the [[s:lagos-colony|Lagos Colony]], [[e:gilbert-carter|Gilbert Carter]], imposed terms. Soon afterwards the area came under British rule.

estado-novo-brazil.t: Getúlio Vargas's authoritarian New State, which built modern Brazil's labour laws and heavy industry and sent troops to fight in Europe.
estado-novo-brazil.o: On 10 November 1937 [[e:getulio-vargas|Getúlio Vargas]], president of the [[s:second-brazilian-republic|Second Brazilian Republic]], closed Congress with army support and imposed a new constitution modelled on European authoritarian regimes, creating the [[e:estado-novo-portugal|Estado Novo]], or New State. Elections planned for 1938 were cancelled.
estado-novo-brazil.r: [[e:getulio-vargas|Vargas]] ruled by decree, abolished political parties and censored the press through the [[e:departement|Department]] of Press and Propaganda. He centralised power, burning state flags in a public ceremony. He introduced a minimum wage in 1940 and the Consolidation of Labour Laws in 1943, winning working-class support. The state founded the National [[e:steel|Steel]] Company at [[e:volta-redonda|Volta Redonda]]. [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] joined the [[e:allies|Allies]] in 1942 and sent an expeditionary force to [[e:italy|Italy]] in 1944.
estado-novo-brazil.e: As the war ended, pressure for democracy grew, and the military deposed [[e:getulio-vargas|Vargas]] on 29 October 1945. Elections followed, and the constitution of 1946 created the [[s:fourth-brazilian-republic|Fourth Brazilian Republic]]. Vargas returned to power by election in 1951.

elisyces.t: Iberian-influenced people of the coastal plain around Narbonne, among the first inhabitants of Gaul named in Greek writing.
elisyces.o: Known only from a handful of Greek sources. [[e:hecataeus-of-miletus|Hecataeus of Miletus]] names them around 500 BCE, and [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] lists Elisyces among the [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] hired by [[e:carthage|Carthage]] for the Battle of [[s:himera|Himera]] in [[e:sicily|Sicily]] in 480 BCE. They held the [[e:languedoc|Languedoc]] coast between the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] and the [[e:herault-river|Hérault]], with [[e:montlaures|Naro]], the oppidum of Montlaurès beside [[s:viscounty-of-narbonne|Narbonne]], as their main centre.
elisyces.r: Archaeology suggests a mixed culture with strong Iberian features: Iberian script on pottery and lead tablets, fortified hilltop settlements such as [[e:enserune|Ensérune]], and busy exchange with Greek [[s:massalia|Massalia]] and [[s:emporion|Emporion]] in wine, painted pottery and metals.
elisyces.e: The name fades from the record by the 3rd century BCE, when Celtic [[e:volcae|Volcae]] dominated the region. In 118 BCE [[e:rome|Rome]] founded the colony of [[e:narbonne|Narbo Martius]] next to [[e:montlaures|Montlaurès]], which became the capital of [[e:gallia-narbonensis|Gallia Narbonensis]].

emirate-of-cyrenaica.t: A short-lived emirate proclaimed by Idris al-Senussi with British backing in 1949, the stepping stone to an independent united Libya.
emirate-of-cyrenaica.o: Idris, head of the [[s:senussi-order|Senussi Order]], had allied with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]]. On 1 June 1949, with British approval, he proclaimed [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] independent at Benghazi under the [[s:british-military-administration-of-libya|British Military Administration of Libya]], as the UN debated the future of the former Italian colony.
emirate-of-cyrenaica.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] had its own government and a constitution of 1949, with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] retaining control of foreign affairs and defence. It was based on the [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] tribes loyal to the [[s:senussi-order|Senussi]], and Benghazi served as its capital.
emirate-of-cyrenaica.e: Idris negotiated union with [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] and the [[s:sultanate-of-fezzan|Fezzan]], and on 24 December 1951 he became king of the federal [[s:kingdom-of-libya|Kingdom of Libya]], with [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] as one of its provinces.

eretria.t: Euboean city that helped found Greek colonies in Italy and the north Aegean, and whose support for the Ionian Revolt brought Persian destruction in 490 BCE.
eretria.o: Eretria grew on the south coast of [[e:euboea|Euboea]], facing [[e:attica|Attica]], in the 8th century BCE, possibly succeeding the earlier settlement at [[e:lefkandi|Lefkandi]]. With [[s:chalcis|Chalcis]] it was a pioneer of long-distance Greek trade, and their rivalry over the Lelantine plain became the [[e:lelantine-war|Lelantine War]].
eretria.r: Eretrians joined [[s:chalcis|Chalcis]] in founding [[e:pithekoussai|Pithekoussai]] and settled [[s:methone-pieria|Methone]] in [[e:macedonia-roman-province|Macedonia]] and, by tradition, [[s:corcyra|Corcyra]] before the Corinthians. It was ruled by aristocracies of horse-breeders. Eretria sent five ships to help [[s:miletus|Miletus]] in 499 BCE, sharing in the burning of [[e:sardis|Sardis]]. Its later [[e:theatre|theatre]] and [[e:gymnasium|gymnasium]] are among the best-preserved on [[e:euboea|Euboea]].
eretria.e: [[e:persia|Persia]] sacked Eretria in 490 BCE and deported its people. Rebuilt, it joined the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] and later hosted the philosopher [[e:menedemus-of-eretria|Menedemus]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] sacked it in 198 BCE, and it lost independence in 146 BCE.
eretria.re: Greek religion; cult of Apollo Daphnephoros

elis.t: City-state of the north-western Peloponnese that controlled the sanctuary of Olympia and organised the Olympic Games.
elis.o: Elis occupied the fertile lowlands of the [[e:pineios-elis|Peneios]] in the north-western [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]], settled by north-west Greek speakers in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. For centuries its people lived in villages; the Eleans won control of the sanctuary of [[e:olympia|Olympia]] from [[e:pisa|Pisa]] in the 6th century BCE, and the city of Elis was formed by synoecism in 471 BCE.
elis.r: Elis supervised the [[e:ancient-olympic-games|Olympic Games]] through officials called [[e:hellanodikai|Hellanodikai]], and its territory was regarded as sacred during the festival. It had an aristocracy and later a democracy, and its land produced horses and [[e:flax|flax]]. Elis produced the sophist [[e:hippias-of-elis|Hippias]] and the sceptic philosopher [[e:pyrrho|Pyrrho]].
elis.e: [[s:sparta|Sparta]] defeated Elis in a war c. 402 to 400 BCE and stripped it of [[e:triphylia|Triphylia]]. In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] Elis allied with the [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]] before joining the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]] in 191 BCE, and passed under [[e:rome|Rome]] in 146 BCE.
elis.re: Greek religion; cult of Olympian Zeus

estonian-soviet-socialist-republic.t: Soviet Estonia, imposed by annexation in 1940 and ended by the Singing Revolution and the restoration of independence in 1991.
estonian-soviet-socialist-republic.o: The [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] occupied the [[s:republic-of-estonia|Republic of Estonia]] in June 1940 under the [[e:molotov-ribbentrop-pact|Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact]]. After rigged elections, a puppet parliament asked to join the [[e:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], and [[e:estonia|Estonia]] was annexed in August 1940. German occupation followed in 1941-1944, and Soviet rule returned in 1944.
estonian-soviet-socialist-republic.r: Soviet rule brought nationalisation, collectivisation and [[e:deportation|mass deportations]], especially in June 1941 and March 1949, when over 20,000 people were sent to [[e:siberia|Siberia]]. Large-scale Russian-speaking immigration changed the population, and oil shale industry developed in the north-east. [[e:johannes-kabin|Johannes Käbin]] led the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Communist Party]] from 1950 to 1978. [[e:estonia|Estonia's]] access to Finnish television made it unusually open to Western influence.
estonian-soviet-socialist-republic.e: In the late 1980s the Singing Revolution mobilised mass protest. The Supreme Soviet declared Estonian [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] in 1988, and during the failed [[e:moscow|Moscow]] coup [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] declared full independence on 20 August 1991, restoring the Republic of [[e:estonia|Estonia]].

emirate-of-tbilisi.t: A Muslim emirate centred on Tbilisi that ruled the heart of eastern Georgia for nearly four centuries until David the Builder took the city in 1122.
emirate-of-tbilisi.o: Arab armies first took [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]] in the 640s, and around 736 the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] general [[e:marwan-ii|Marwan ibn Muhammad]] made it the seat of an emir governing Georgian lands. Under the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]] the [[e:emir|emirs]] turned the strategic city on the [[e:kura-river|Mtkvari]] into a largely self-governing state.
emirate-of-tbilisi.r: [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]] was a prosperous trading city of Muslims, Christians and [[e:jews|Jews]], with a mint, baths and markets. The [[e:emir|emirs]], notably the Jaffarid family, often defied [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]]: [[e:ishaq-ibn-ismail|Ishaq ibn Ismail's]] rebellion ended in 853 when the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid]] general [[e:bugha-the-elder|Bugha the Elder]] burned the city. Later the emir shared power with a council of leading citizens.
emirate-of-tbilisi.e: Weakened by Georgian pressure, the [[e:emirate|emirate]] fell under Seljuk control in the 1080s. In 1122 [[e:david-iv-of-georgia|David IV]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] captured [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]] after the [[e:battle-of-didgori|Battle of Didgori]] and made it his capital.

ezeritai.t: Slavic tribe of the lower Eurotas valley in Laconia, a tribute-paying neighbour of the Melingoi under Byzantine rule.
ezeritai.o: The Ezeritai, whose name probably comes from the Slavic word for lake, settled in the marshy plain of [[e:helos|Helos]] in southern [[e:laconia|Laconia]] during the Slavic migrations into the [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]] of the late 6th and 7th centuries. They first appear clearly in Byzantine sources of the 9th and 10th centuries.
ezeritai.r: Like the [[s:melingoi|Melingoi]], the Ezeritai kept their own leaders and paid a fixed tribute instead of regular taxes, recorded by [[e:constantine-vii|Constantine VII]] as 300 gold coins a year. They were subdued by [[e:theoktistos-bryennios|Theoktistos Bryennios]] in the 840s and rebelled again in the 920s under [[e:romanos-i-lekapenos|Romanos I]], after which their tribute was raised. Little else is recorded of their society.
ezeritai.e: They may have remained a distinct group into the period of Frankish rule in the 13th century. Over time they converted to [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox Christianity]] and merged into the Greek population of [[e:laconia|Laconia]], leaving place names as their main trace.
ezeritai.re: Slavic paganism, later Eastern Orthodox Christianity

emirate-of-multan.t: An Arab emirate of the upper Indus, first Sunni and later Ismaili, ruling the rich pilgrimage city of Multan until Mahmud of Ghazni took it.
emirate-of-multan.o: [[e:multan|Multan]] was conquered by [[e:muhammad-ibn-qasim|Muhammad ibn Qasim]] in 713. As Abbasid control of [[e:sindh|Sindh]] weakened, an Arab family, the [[e:banu-munabbih|Banu Munabbih]], claiming descent from the [[e:quraysh|Quraysh]], ruled it from around 855 as an autonomous [[e:emirate|emirate]] that recognised the Abbasid [[e:caliphate|caliph]].
emirate-of-multan.r: [[e:multan|Multan's]] famous Sun temple drew [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] pilgrims from across [[e:india|India]], and the [[e:emir|emirs]], according to al-Masudi, used its idol as a hostage against Hindu attack and drew revenue from the offerings. In the 950s [[e:ismailism|Ismaili]] missionaries of the [[s:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimid Caliphate]] won over the ruling class, and under the Ismaili ruler [[e:jalam-ibn-shayban|Jalam ibn Shayban]] the Sun temple was destroyed and a mosque built in its place. Multan traded with [[e:khorasan|Khorasan]] and [[e:sindh|Sindh]].
emirate-of-multan.e: [[e:mahmud-of-ghazni|Mahmud of Ghazni]] attacked the [[e:ismailism|Ismaili]] ruler [[e:abu-al-fath-dawud|Abu al-Fath Dawud]] in 1006 and annexed [[e:multan|Multan]] around 1010, persecuting the Ismailis. Multan became a province of the [[s:ghaznavid-empire|Ghaznavid Empire]] and later a centre of [[e:sufism|Sufism]].
emirate-of-multan.re: Sunni Islam, then Ismaili Shia Islam

early-le-dynasty.t: The short Vietnamese dynasty of Le Hoan, who repelled a Song Chinese invasion in 981 and sacked the Cham capital the following year.
early-le-dynasty.o: In 980, as the [[e:song-dynasty|Song dynasty]] prepared to invade [[s:dinh-dynasty|Dai Co Viet]] after the murder of [[e:dinh-tien-hoang|Dinh Tien Hoang]], the commander-in-chief [[e:le-dai-hanh|Le Hoan]] took the throne with the backing of the queen mother [[e:duong-van-nga|Duong Van Nga]]. He ruled as Le Dai Hanh from the old Dinh capital at [[e:hoa-lu|Hoa Lu]].
early-le-dynasty.r: [[e:le-dai-hanh|Le Dai Hanh]] defeated the [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] invasion at [[e:chi-lang-pass|Chi Lang]] and on the [[e:bach-dang-river|Bach Dang]] river in 981, then restored [[e:tributary-system|tributary relations]] with the Song. In 982 he attacked [[s:champa|Champa]] and sacked its capital at [[e:indrapura-champa|Indrapura]]. He promoted agriculture with a royal ploughing ceremony, built roads and canals, and relied on Buddhist monks as advisers and envoys.
early-le-dynasty.e: After [[e:le-dai-hanh|Le Dai Hanh's]] death in 1005 his sons fought over the succession. The last ruler, [[e:le-long-dinh|Le Long Dinh]], was remembered as cruel, and on his death in 1009 the court official [[e:ly-thai-to|Ly Cong Uan]] was chosen as king, founding the [[s:ly-dynasty|Ly dynasty]], which moved the capital to [[e:thang-long|Thang Long]].

emirate-of-asir.t: A highland emirate of south-western Arabia that resisted Egyptian and Ottoman armies for half a century from its base at Abha.
emirate-of-asir.o: [[e:asir|Asir]], the mountainous region between the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]] and [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]], had joined the [[s:emirate-of-diriyah|Emirate of Diriyah]] and fought hard against the Egyptian armies of [[e:muhammad-ali-of-egypt|Muhammad Ali]]. After [[e:diriyah|Diriyah]] fell in 1818, local leaders took charge, and from 1823 a series of [[e:emir|emirs]], from 1834 of the Al Aidh family, ruled the region from [[e:abha|Abha]].
emirate-of-asir.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] led a confederation of highland tribes, combining Wahhabi-influenced religious leadership with tribal warfare. They fought off Egyptian expeditions in the 1820s and 1830s and raided the [[e:tihama|Tihama]] coast and the Yemeni ports. Under A'id ibn Mar'i and his son Muhammad the [[e:emirate|emirate]] remained largely independent of the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] despite repeated campaigns.
emirate-of-asir.e: In 1871-1872 an Ottoman army took [[e:abha|Abha]], and [[e:muhammad-ibn-aid|Muhammad ibn A'id]] was killed. [[e:asir|Asir]] was incorporated into the [[s:yemen-vilayet|Yemen Vilayet]] as a sanjak, and later passed to the [[s:idrisid-emirate-of-asir|Idrisid Emirate of Asir]] and then to [[s:saudi-arabia|Saudi Arabia]].

estonian-self-administration.t: Estonian collaborationist administration under German occupation in 1941-1944, headed by Hjalmar Mäe within Reichskommissariat Ostland.
estonian-self-administration.o: German forces drove the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] out of [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] in summer 1941. The occupiers placed [[e:estonia|Estonia]] in the Generalkommissariat [[s:duchy-of-estonia-1561-1721|Estland]] within [[s:reichskommissariat-ostland|Reichskommissariat Ostland]], and in 1941 appointed a Directorate of [[e:estonians|Estonians]] led by [[e:hjalmar-mae|Hjalmar Mäe]] to handle local administration.
estonian-self-administration.r: The Self-Administration had limited powers under German control and could not restore independence. It ran local government, schools and the economy, and took part in German policies. Almost all of [[e:estonia|Estonia's]] [[e:jews|Jews]] who had not fled were murdered in 1941, and camps such as [[e:klooga-concentration-camp|Klooga]] held Jews deported from elsewhere. From 1943 Estonian men were conscripted into German units.
estonian-self-administration.e: As the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] advanced in September 1944 and the Germans withdrew, [[e:hjalmar-mae|Mäe]] left, and [[e:otto-tief|Otto Tief]] briefly formed a national government in [[s:reval|Tallinn]] on 18 September. Soviet forces took Tallinn on 22 September 1944, restoring the [[s:estonian-soviet-socialist-republic|Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic]].

emirate-of-bari.t: Short-lived Muslim emirate in Apulia, centred on the port of Bari, which raided southern Italy until Louis II took it in 871.
emirate-of-bari.o: Arab and [[e:berbers|Berber]] soldiers, some of them [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] hired by the warring [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] princes, seized [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]] around 847 under a leader named [[e:kalfun|Kalfun]]. From this base on the Adriatic coast they extended control over much of [[e:apulia|Apulia]].
emirate-of-bari.r: Under [[e:mufarraj-ibn-sallam|Mufarraj ibn Sallam]] and then [[e:sawdan|Sawdan]], the last emir, [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]] sought recognition from the Abbasid [[e:caliphate|caliph]] and became an [[e:emirate|emirate]] with a congregational mosque. It lived largely from raiding and the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]], attacking [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] and Byzantine territory and monasteries, though Sawdan also dealt diplomatically with Christian neighbours, and a Jewish chronicle recalls him as a figure of learning.
emirate-of-bari.e: The Carolingian emperor [[e:louis-ii-of-italy|Louis II]] besieged [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]] for several years with [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] allies and Byzantine naval help, taking the city in 871 and capturing [[e:sawdan|Sawdan]]. The [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] occupied [[e:bari|Bari]] in 876, and it became the capital of the [[s:theme-of-longobardia|Theme of Longobardia]].

essequibo.t: The oldest Dutch colony on the Guiana coast, founded as a trading post on the Essequibo river and later a plantation colony that became part of Guyana.
essequibo.o: [[e:dutch|Dutch]] traders from [[s:county-of-zeeland|Zeeland]] established a post on the Essequibo river around 1616, at the fort of [[e:kyk-over-al|Kyk-over-al]] on an island near the meeting of the Essequibo, [[e:mazaruni|Mazaruni]] and Cuyuni rivers. From 1621 the colony was run by the Zeeland chamber of the [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]].
essequibo.r: Early Essequibo traded with indigenous peoples for dyes and hardwoods, but [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] plantations worked by enslaved Africans gradually took over. The seat of government moved to [[e:fort-zeelandia-guyana|Fort Zeelandia]] on Fort Island in the 18th century. Commander [[e:laurens-storm-van-s-gravesande|Laurens Storm van 's Gravesande]], from 1743, opened the neighbouring [[s:demerara|Demerara]] river to settlement, which soon outgrew Essequibo, and many British planters settled there. Relations with indigenous peoples relied on gifts and alliances.
essequibo.e: The colony changed hands several times during wars, and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] occupied it from 1796. It was united with [[s:demerara|Demerara]] in 1812 as [[s:demerara-essequibo|Demerara-Essequibo]], formally ceded to [[e:britain|Britain]] in 1814, and merged into [[s:british-guiana|British Guiana]] in 1831. [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]] still claims the region west of the Essequibo.

erythrae.t: Ionian city on the peninsula facing Chios, home of a famous Sibyl and member of the twelve-city Ionian League.
erythrae.o: Erythrae stood on the coast of the peninsula opposite [[s:chios|Chios]], founded by tradition by Cnopus, a son of [[e:codrus|Codrus of Athens]], with mixed settlers c. 1000 BCE. It joined the [[s:ionian-league|Ionian League]] and, as an early rival of Chios, fought several wars with the island.
erythrae.r: The [[e:erythraean-sibyl|Erythraean Sibyl]], a prophetess of [[e:apollo|Apollo]], gave the city renown. Erythrae was governed by aristocracies and later oligarchies and democracies, and sent eight ships to the [[e:battle-of-lade|Battle of Lade]] in 494 BCE. An Athenian decree of the 450s BCE imposed a democratic constitution and garrison on it as a [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] member.
erythrae.e: Erythrae revolted from [[s:athens|Athens]] in 412 BCE and later swung between Persian, Athenian and Macedonian influence. In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] it was a free city, allied to [[e:rome|Rome]] from the war against [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]], and passed into the province of Asia after 133 BCE.

eburones.t: Belgic people between the Meuse and the Rhine who destroyed a Roman legion in 54 BCE and were wiped out by Caesar in revenge.
eburones.o: The Eburones lived between the [[e:meuse|Meuse]] and the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], in modern eastern [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] and the southern [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]]. [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] counts them among the [[e:germani-cisrhenani|Germani Cisrhenani]] and says they had paid tribute to the [[s:aduatuci|Aduatuci]].
eburones.r: They were ruled jointly by two kings, [[e:ambiorix|Ambiorix]] and the elderly [[e:catuvolcus|Catuvolcus]]. Their stronghold was [[e:atuatuca|Atuatuca]], where [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] stationed troops for the winter of 54 BCE.
eburones.e: In 54 BCE [[e:ambiorix|Ambiorix]] lured the legion and a half under [[e:quintus-titurius-sabinus|Sabinus]] and [[e:lucius-aurunculeius-cotta|Cotta]] out of [[e:atuatuca|Atuatuca]] and destroyed it. In 53 BCE [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] invited neighbouring peoples to plunder their land; [[e:catuvolcus|Catuvolcus]] poisoned himself with yew, while Ambiorix escaped. Their territory was later settled by the [[s:tungri|Tungri]].

electorate-of-trier.t: The ecclesiastical principality of the archbishops of Trier, one of the seven electors of the Holy Roman Empire, stretching along the Moselle and Rhine.
electorate-of-trier.o: [[e:trier|Trier]] had been an imperial capital in late Roman times and a bishopric since the 3rd century. In 898 King [[e:zwentibold|Zwentibold]] granted Archbishop [[e:radbod-of-trier|Ratbod]] immunity and comital rights over the city, the basis of the archbishops' temporal power. Over the following centuries they built a territory along the [[e:moselle|Moselle]] from Trier to [[e:koblenz|Koblenz]].
electorate-of-trier.r: Archbishop Baldwin of [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]], brother of [[e:henry-vii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry VII]], consolidated the territory between 1307 and 1354. The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] confirmed the archbishop as an elector and arch-chancellor for [[e:gaul|Gaul]] and [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]]. The [[e:prince-elector|electors]] moved their residence to [[e:koblenz|Koblenz]] and [[e:ehrenbreitstein-fortress|Ehrenbreitstein]], and [[e:trier|Trier]] kept the [[e:holy-robe|Holy Robe]] relic, exhibited to pilgrims.
electorate-of-trier.e: [[e:french-revolutionary-occupation-of-the-netherlands|French revolutionary armies]] occupied the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 1794. The last elector, [[e:clemens-wenceslaus-of-saxony|Clemens Wenceslaus of Saxony]], fled, and in 1803 the [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Reichsdeputationshauptschluss]] dissolved the electorate, its remaining eastern lands going to [[s:county-of-nassau-weilburg|Nassau-Weilburg]]. After 1815 most of it became Prussian.

emirate-of-cordoba.t: The independent Umayyad state in al-Andalus founded by a refugee prince in 756, which built the Great Mosque of Córdoba.
emirate-of-cordoba.o: After the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]] massacred the Umayyad family in 750, the prince Abd al-Rahman escaped to [[e:north-africa|North Africa]] and crossed to [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]] in 755. Backed by Umayyad clients and Syrian troops, he defeated the governor [[e:yusuf-al-fihri|Yusuf al-Fihri]] in 756 and became emir at [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]], independent of [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]].
emirate-of-cordoba.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] built a centralised state with a professional army, a bureaucracy and a coinage. [[e:abd-al-rahman-i|Abd al-Rahman I]] began the [[e:mosque-cathedral-of-cordoba|Great Mosque]] in 785. [[e:al-hakam-i|Al-Hakam I]] crushed the revolt of the suburb of [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] in 818, and [[e:abd-al-rahman-ii|Abd al-Rahman II]], patron of the musician [[e:ziryab|Ziryab]], brought eastern fashions and repelled the [[e:vikings|Vikings]] from [[e:seville|Seville]] in 844. Christians were steadily Arabised and converted.
emirate-of-cordoba.e: From the 880s revolts by muwallads such as [[e:umar-ibn-hafsun|Umar ibn Hafsun]] and local lords split the [[e:emirate|emirate]]. [[e:abd-al-rahman-iii|Abd al-Rahman III]] restored control from 912 and in 929 declared himself [[e:caliphate|caliph]], turning the emirate into the [[s:caliphate-of-cordoba|Caliphate of Córdoba]].

emirate-of-diriyah.t: The first Saudi state, born of an alliance between the Al Saud and the reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, which conquered most of Arabia.
emirate-of-diriyah.o: [[e:muhammad-ibn-saud|Muhammad ibn Saud]] became emir of the small oasis town of [[e:diriyah|Diriyah]] in [[e:najd|Najd]] in 1727. In 1744 he made a pact with [[e:muhammad-ibn-abd-al-wahhab|Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab]], a preacher calling for a return to strict [[e:monotheism|monotheism]]: the [[e:house-of-saud|Al Saud]] would support the reform movement, and the scholar would legitimise their rule.
emirate-of-diriyah.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] expanded by war and conversion, taking [[e:riyadh|Riyadh]] in 1773, defeating the [[s:banu-khalid-emirate|Banu Khalid Emirate]] and conquering [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Hasa]]. It collected [[e:zakat|zakat]] from subject towns and tribes and destroyed shrines seen as idolatrous. Under [[e:saud-ibn-abd-al-aziz|Saud ibn Abd al-Aziz]] its forces sacked Karbala in 1802 and took [[e:mecca|Mecca]] in 1803 and [[e:medina|Medina]] soon after, and raided [[e:iraq|Iraq]], [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[e:oman|Oman]].
emirate-of-diriyah.e: The [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] sent the army of [[s:egypt-under-muhammad-ali|Egypt under Muhammad Ali]]. [[e:ibrahim-pasha-of-egypt|Ibrahim Pasha]] besieged and destroyed [[e:diriyah|Diriyah]] in 1818; the last emir, [[e:abdullah-ibn-saud|Abdullah ibn Saud]], was executed in [[e:istanbul|Istanbul]]. The [[s:emirate-of-nejd|Emirate of Nejd]] revived Saudi rule in 1824. The ruins of [[e:at-turaif|al-Turaif]] are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

eastern-rumelia.t: Autonomous Ottoman province south of the Balkan mountains, created at Berlin to divide Bulgaria and absorbed into it by a bloodless coup in 1885.
eastern-rumelia.o: The [[e:treaty-of-san-stefano|Treaty of San Stefano]] in 1878 had created a large [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]], but the [[e:congress-of-berlin|Congress of Berlin]] split it, leaving the southern part as Eastern Rumelia, an autonomous province of the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]]. Its constitution, the [[e:regulamentul-organic|Organic Statute]], was drafted by an international commission, and [[e:plovdiv|Plovdiv]] became its capital.
eastern-rumelia.r: A Christian governor-general appointed by the sultan with the approval of the Great Powers headed the administration, first [[e:aleko-bogoridi|Aleko Bogoridi]] and then [[e:gavril-krastevich|Gavril Krastevich]], with an elected assembly. The majority population was Bulgarian, with Turkish, Greek and [[e:pomaks|Pomak]] minorities. Bulgarian became the dominant language of government and schools, and the province's militia was largely Bulgarian.
eastern-rumelia.e: On 6 September 1885 Bulgarian activists and militia in [[e:plovdiv|Plovdiv]] deposed the governor and proclaimed union with the [[s:principality-of-bulgaria|Principality of Bulgaria]]. [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] then defeated [[s:serbia|Serbia]], and in 1886 the sultan recognised the Bulgarian prince as governor-general, ending the province in practice.

emesene-dynasty.t: Emesa, an Arab priestly kingdom in central Syria whose descendants included the Roman empress Julia Domna and emperor Elagabalus.
emesene-dynasty.o: [[e:sampsigeramus-i|Sampsigeramus I]], an Arab chief, controlled the [[e:orontes-river|Orontes]] valley around [[e:homs|Emesa]], modern Homs, as the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]] collapsed. [[e:pompey|Pompey]] recognised him as a client ruler in 64 BCE, founding a dynasty that would last over a century.
emesene-dynasty.r: Its rulers were priests of the sun god [[e:elagabal|Elagabal]], worshipped as a black stone at [[e:homs|Emesa]]. They served [[e:rome|Rome]] with [[e:archery|archers]] and soldiers and grew wealthy on the caravan trade of the Syrian desert. [[e:iamblichus-i-of-emesa|Iamblichus I]] was executed by [[e:mark-antony|Mark Antony]], but the dynasty soon regained power under Augustus.
emesene-dynasty.e: After [[e:gaius-julius-sohaemus|Gaius Julius Sohaemus]], the kingdom was absorbed into Roman [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] around 72 CE. The priestly family survived, and [[e:julia-domna|Julia Domna]] married [[e:septimius-severus|Septimius Severus]]; her great-nephew [[e:elagabalus|Elagabalus]] became emperor in 218 CE.

emirate-of-dhala.t: The Amiri emirate on the highland frontier north of Aden, where the armed revolt against British rule in South Arabia began.
emirate-of-dhala.o: The Amiri family ruled the district of Dhala, a high plateau on the route between [[e:aden|Aden]] and the Yemeni highlands. They became independent of the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] in the 18th century. The Zaydi [[e:imam|imams]] and later the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] continued to claim the area.
emirate-of-dhala.r: The emir governed through tribal sheikhs and taxed the trade crossing the frontier. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] brought Dhala into the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]], and the Anglo-Ottoman boundary of 1904 left it on the British side. British political officers and troops were stationed there, and the [[e:emirate|emirate]] was a founding member of the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]] in 1959.
emirate-of-dhala.e: In 1963 tribesmen of the nearby Radfan mountains launched the armed struggle of the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] against the federation. When the NLF took over in 1967 the [[e:emirate|emirate]] was abolished and incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

emirate-of-adrar.t: A Hassani emirate on the Adrar plateau of Mauritania, controlling the caravan towns of Atar, Chinguetti and Ouadane and the salt of Ijil.
emirate-of-adrar.o: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] formed in the mid-18th century when a Hassani warrior lineage, the Awlad Yahya bin Uthman, established dominance over the Adrar plateau of central [[e:mauritania|Mauritania]]. It took over oases long settled by [[e:berbers|Berber]] scholarly and trading communities, with [[e:atar|Atar]] emerging as its main centre.
emirate-of-adrar.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] taxed the date oases and caravan towns such as [[e:chinguetti|Chinguetti]] and [[e:ouadane|Ouadane]], famous for their [[e:manuscript|manuscript]] libraries, and controlled the [[e:salt-trade|salt trade]] from the Ijil mines. Society was divided between Hassani warriors, [[e:zawaya|Zawaya]] scholars, tributaries and enslaved people. Succession disputes and feuds between branches of the ruling family were frequent.
emirate-of-adrar.e: French forces under [[e:henri-gouraud|Henri Gouraud]] occupied [[e:atar|Atar]] in 1909, overcoming resistance encouraged by the scholar [[e:ma-al-aynayn|Ma al-Aynayn]]. Adrar became part of [[s:french-mauritania|French Mauritania]], and the [[e:emirate|emirate]] was absorbed into colonial administration.

eastern-ganga-dynasty.t: The long-ruling dynasty of Odisha that built the Jagannath temple at Puri and the Sun Temple at Konark.
eastern-ganga-dynasty.o: The Eastern Gangas emerged in the late 5th century under [[e:indravarma|Indravarman]] I in [[s:kingdom-of-kalinga|Kalinga]], on the coast of modern [[e:odisha|Odisha]] and northern [[e:andhra-region|Andhra]], with their early capital at [[e:mukhalingam|Kalinganagara]], modern Mukhalingam. For centuries they were a regional power, at times subordinate to the [[s:eastern-chalukyas|Eastern Chalukyas]] and the [[s:somavamshi-dynasty|Somavamshi dynasty]].
eastern-ganga-dynasty.r: [[e:anantavarman-chodaganga|Anantavarman Chodaganga]], who ruled from 1078 to 1147, united the land from the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] to the Godavari, moved the capital to [[e:cuttack|Cuttack]] and began the [[e:jagannath|Jagannath]] temple at Puri, which became the centre of the state cult. [[e:narasimhadeva-i|Narasimhadeva I]] built the [[e:konark-sun-temple|Sun Temple]] at Konark around 1250 and fought the Muslim rulers of [[e:bengal|Bengal]]. Temple endowments, [[e:rice|rice]] farming and seaborne trade sustained the kingdom, and [[e:odia-language|Odia]] emerged as a written language.
eastern-ganga-dynasty.e: Weakened by attacks from the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] and the [[s:bengal-sultanate|Bengal Sultanate]], the last Ganga king was overthrown in 1434 by his minister [[e:kapilendra-deva|Kapilendra Deva]], who founded the Gajapati kingdom of the Suryavamshi dynasty.

ebusus.t: The Punic city of Ibiza, a Carthaginian stronghold whose vast necropolis and Tanit cult make it a key site for Phoenician civilisation in the West.
ebusus.o: [[e:phoenicians|Phoenicians]] had a small trading post at [[e:sa-caleta|Sa Caleta]] on Ibiza in the 7th century BCE. According to [[e:diodorus-siculus|Diodorus]], the city of Ebusus was founded in 654 BCE on the bay of modern Ibiza town, and it soon came under the influence of [[e:carthage|Carthage]].
ebusus.r: Ebusus became one of the most important Punic cities in the western [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]], producing wine, oil, salt, purple dye and pottery, and minting coins showing the god Bes. The [[e:puig-des-molins|Puig des Molins]] necropolis contains thousands of tombs, and the cave sanctuary of Es Culleram was dedicated to [[e:tanit|Tanit]]. It controlled trade with the [[s:balearic-islanders|Balearic Islanders]] and recruited their slingers.
ebusus.e: Ebusus stayed loyal to [[e:carthage|Carthage]] through the [[e:second-punic-war|Second Punic War]], but afterwards made a treaty with [[e:rome|Rome]]. After the Roman conquest of the [[e:balearic-islands|Balearics]] in 123 BCE it was increasingly integrated, becoming a Roman municipium under Vespasian while keeping Punic culture for centuries.

el-peru-waka.t: A Classic Maya city on the San Pedro Mártir river, a strategic ally of Calakmul whose royal tombs include that of the warrior queen Lady K'abel.
el-peru-waka.o: Waka' grew on an escarpment above the [[e:san-pedro-martir-river|San Pedro Mártir]] river in north-western [[e:peten|Petén]], a route linking the Gulf lowlands with the central Petén. Its dynasty is attested from about 350 CE, and in 378 it received the Teotihuacan-linked lord [[e:siyaj-kak|Sihyaj K'ahk']] before his arrival at [[s:tikal|Tikal]].
el-peru-waka.r: In the 7th century Waka' became a key client of the [[s:kingdom-of-kaan|Kingdom of Kaan]]. The Kaan princess [[e:lady-kabel|Lady K'abel]] married the king [[e:kinich-bahlam-ii|K'inich B'ahlam II]] and held the title of supreme warrior; her tomb was found in 2012. The city controlled river traffic in goods such as salt, [[e:cacao|cacao]] and obsidian.
el-peru-waka.e: [[s:tikal|Tikal]] defeated Waka' in 743, and the city declined with Calakmul's waning power. Activity faded around 800 CE. Looting of its stelae in the 1960s spurred protection efforts, and excavations since 2003 have revealed much of its history.

euzkadi-1936-1937.t: The first Basque autonomous government, formed during the Spanish Civil War and defeated within a year, after the bombing of Guernica.
euzkadi-1936-1937.o: After the outbreak of the [[e:spanish-civil-war|Spanish Civil War]], the [[s:second-spanish-republic|Second Spanish Republic]] granted the Basque Country a [[e:statute-of-autonomy-of-the-basque-country-1936|Statute of Autonomy]] in October 1936. [[e:jose-antonio-aguirre|José Antonio Aguirre]] of the [[e:basque-nationalist-party|Basque Nationalist Party]] was sworn in as first lehendakari under the oak of [[e:guernica|Guernica]] on 7 October 1936.
euzkadi-1936-1937.r: The government controlled only [[e:biscay|Biscay]] and part of [[e:gipuzkoa|Gipuzkoa]]. It raised its own army, issued money and passports, and protected the Catholic Church, unlike much of Republican [[e:spain|Spain]]. [[e:bilbao|Bilbao's]] industry and port were its base, defended by the fortified Iron Ring.
euzkadi-1936-1937.e: Franco's Army of the North attacked in 1937. German and Italian aircraft destroyed [[e:guernica|Guernica]] on 26 April 1937, and [[e:bilbao|Bilbao]] fell on 19 June. Basque troops surrendered to the Italians at [[e:santona|Santoña]] in August. The government went into exile, and Basque autonomy was restored only in 1979.

earldom-of-more.t: Coastal earldom of western Norway whose first great earl, Rognvald Eysteinsson, backed Harald Fairhair and founded the line of the earls of Orkney.
earldom-of-more.o: Møre, the coastal land between [[e:romsdal|Romsdal]] and the fjords to the south, was a petty kingdom in the 8th century. The sagas say that [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]], after conquering it, gave the region to his ally [[e:rognvald-eysteinsson|Rognvald Eysteinsson]] as earl in the late 9th century, joining North and [[e:sunnmore|South Møre]] under one lord.
earldom-of-more.r: The earls held power through their fleets, their great farms and their command of the sea lanes along the coast. [[e:rognvald-eysteinsson|Rognvald]]'s family spread overseas: his brother [[e:sigurd-eysteinsson|Sigurd]] became the first Earl of [[e:orkney|Orkney]], his son [[e:torf-einarr|Torf-Einarr]] later ruled there, and Icelandic saga tradition made [[e:rollo|Rollo]], founder of [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]], another son. The earls answered to the king but acted largely on their own.
earldom-of-more.e: [[e:rognvald-eysteinsson|Rognvald]] was killed, according to the sagas, when sons of [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] burned him in his hall. His descendants kept the earldom for a time, but by around 1000 Møre was governed directly by the kings of [[e:norway|Norway]] or by the earls of [[e:lade-trondheim|Lade]], and it became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]].

east-francia.t: The eastern Carolingian kingdom created at Verdun in 843, from which the Kingdom of Germany and the Holy Roman Empire developed.
east-francia.o: The [[e:treaty-of-verdun|Treaty of Verdun]] in 843 divided the Carolingian empire among the three sons of [[e:louis-the-pious|Louis the Pious]]. [[e:louis-the-german|Louis the German]] received the lands east of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], together with [[e:mainz|Mainz]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-worms|Worms]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]] on its west bank. He ruled them from palaces such as [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]] and [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]], and in 870 the [[e:treaty-of-meerssen|Treaty of Meerssen]] added much of [[s:duchy-of-lotharingia|Lotharingia]].
east-francia.r: East Francia combined [[s:franks|Franks]], [[s:saxons|Saxons]], [[e:bavarians|Bavarians]], Swabians and [[s:kingdom-of-the-thuringians|Thuringians]], each with strong regional identities that grew into stem duchies. Kings moved between palaces and relied on [[e:bishop|bishops]] and great abbeys. [[e:arnulf-of-carinthia|Arnulf of Carinthia]] defeated the [[e:vikings|Vikings]] on the [[e:dyle|Dyle]] in 891 and was crowned emperor in 896, but [[e:magyars|Magyar]] raids devastated the kingdom after 900.
east-francia.e: When the last Carolingian, [[e:louis-the-child|Louis the Child]], died in 911, the nobles elected Conrad I of [[e:franconia|Franconia]], then in 919 [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler of Saxony]]. [[e:prince-henry-the-navigator|Henry's]] son Otto I defeated the [[e:magyars|Magyars]] at the [[e:battle-of-lechfeld|Lechfeld]] in 955 and was crowned emperor in 962, a date usually taken as the start of the [[s:kingdom-of-germany|Kingdom of Germany]] within the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
east-francia.la: Old High German, Old Saxon, Latin

enchelei.t: Illyrian people around Lake Ohrid, linked by Greek legend to the hero Cadmus, among the earliest Illyrian groups named in Greek sources.
enchelei.o: Greek writers from [[e:hecataeus-of-miletus|Hecataeus]] and [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] onward place the Enchelei, the 'eel people', near [[e:lake-ohrid|Lake Ohrid]] and the [[e:drin|Drin]] valley. Myth said [[e:cadmus|Cadmus]] and [[e:harmonia|Harmonia]] came to rule them after leaving [[s:thebes|Thebes]], and that their descendants ruled the [[e:illyrians|Illyrians]]. Little beyond these mentions survives, and their origins are otherwise unknown.
enchelei.r: Known only from scattered Greek references, the Enchelei appear as a tribal people of the lake district around [[e:ohrid|Lychnidus]] (Ohrid), whose fisheries probably gave them their name. Later authors seem to treat the Sesarethii as the same or a successor people.
enchelei.e: By the 4th century BCE their name fades, and the region around [[e:lake-ohrid|Lake Ohrid]] appears under the [[e:dassaretae|Dassaretae]] and within the sphere of [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] and the [[s:illyrian-kingdom|Illyrian Kingdom]].

eastern-province.t: The self-governing Banda Oriental of José Artigas, which pioneered federalism and land reform before being overrun by Portugal.
eastern-province.o: The Banda Oriental, east of the [[s:oriental-republic-of-uruguay|Uruguay]] river, rose against Spanish [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]] in 1811 under [[e:jose-gervasio-artigas|José Gervasio Artigas]]. In 1813 a congress of the Eastern Province adopted the [[e:instructions-of-the-year-xiii|Instructions of the Year XIII]], demanding independence and a federal union with the other provinces of the [[s:united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|United Provinces of the Río de la Plata]].
eastern-province.r: [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] rejected the Instructions and captured [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]] from [[e:spain|Spain]] in 1814. [[e:jose-gervasio-artigas|Artigas]] broke with Buenos Aires and took Montevideo in 1815, governing through a cabildo while leading the wider [[s:federal-league|Federal League]]. His Provisional Regulation of 1815 distributed confiscated land to poor settlers, indigenous people and [[e:freedmen|freedmen]], one of the first agrarian reforms in the [[e:americas|Americas]].
eastern-province.e: Portuguese troops from [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] invaded in 1816 and occupied [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]] in January 1817. The province was annexed as [[s:cisplatina|Cisplatina]], while [[e:jose-gervasio-artigas|Artigas]] fought on until 1820. Artigas is honoured as the founder of Uruguayan nationhood.

ephesus.t: Ionian port city of the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders, and later the capital of Roman Asia.
ephesus.o: Ionian settlers led, by tradition, by [[e:androclus|Androclus]], son of [[e:codrus|Codrus of Athens]], founded Ephesus near the mouth of the [[e:cayster-river|Cayster]] c. 1000 BCE, beside a native cult of a mother goddess. The [[e:greeks|Greeks]] identified her with [[e:artemis|Artemis]], and her sanctuary became the city's focus. Ephesus was one of the twelve cities of the [[s:ionian-league|Ionian League]].
ephesus.r: Ephesus prospered from trade between the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] and inner [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. [[e:croesus|Croesus]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-lydia|Kingdom of Lydia]] took the city c. 560 BCE, ousting the tyrant Pindarus, and paid for columns of the great marble [[e:temple-of-artemis|Artemision]]. The philosopher [[e:heraclitus|Heraclitus]] lived there. Under the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] and then the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] it kept its temple economy, with the sanctuary acting as a bank and place of asylum.
ephesus.e: The temple burned in 356 BCE and was rebuilt in grander form. [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]] moved the city to a new site c. 290 BCE. After [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]], Ptolemaic and [[e:pergamenes|Pergamene]] rule, Ephesus passed to [[e:rome|Rome]] in 133 BCE and became the chief city of the province of Asia.
ephesus.re: Greek religion; cult of Artemis of Ephesus

eastern-liao.t: A Khitan kingdom in Manchuria founded by Yelü Liuge in revolt against the Jurchen, which survived as a Mongol vassal until 1269.
eastern-liao.o: In 1212, as Mongol attacks weakened the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234), the Khitan officer [[e:yelu-liuge|Yelü Liuge]] rebelled in [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]] and allied himself with [[e:genghis-khan|Genghis Khan]]. In 1213 he proclaimed himself king of [[e:liao-dynasty|Liao]], reviving the name of the fallen [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]], and defeated Jin armies sent against him.
eastern-liao.r: The kingdom drew on Khitan soldiers and settlers in [[e:manchuria|Manchuria]]. [[e:yelu-liuge|Yelü Liuge]] chose loyalty to the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] over full independence, submitting in person to [[e:genghis-khan|Genghis Khan]] in 1215. Some of his followers rejected this, set up a rival regime, and fled into [[s:goryeo|Goryeo]], where Mongol and Korean forces destroyed them in 1219.
eastern-liao.e: After [[e:yelu-liuge|Yelü Liuge's]] death in 1220 his widow and son [[e:yelu-xuedu|Yelü Xuedu]] governed as hereditary [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:mongol-empire|Mongol Empire]]. The kingdom was gradually reduced and was abolished in 1269 under [[e:kublai-khan|Kublai]], its lands absorbed into Yuan administration.

emirate-of-beihan.t: A frontier emirate in Wadi Bayhan, ancient heart of Qataban, whose sharifs were staunch British allies against Yemen.
emirate-of-beihan.o: [[e:wadi-bayhan|Wadi Bayhan]], once the core of the [[s:kingdom-of-qataban|Kingdom of Qataban]], was by the 19th century divided between local tribes and a family of sharifs, descendants of the Prophet, who emerged as [[e:emir|emirs]] around 1800 with their seat at Suq Abdullah.
emirate-of-beihan.r: Beihan lay on the disputed border between the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]] and the [[e:imam|imams]]' [[s:mutawakkilite-kingdom-of-yemen|Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen]], and clashes there were frequent in the 1950s. Its ruling sharif, [[e:husayn-ibn-ahmad-al-habili|Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Habili]], was one of [[e:britain|Britain's]] firmest allies and a founding figure of the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]] in 1959. Agriculture depended on seasonal floods.
emirate-of-beihan.e: In 1967 the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over the region and the [[e:emirate|emirate]] was incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]]; its ruling family went into exile.

emirate-of-brakna.t: A Hassani emirate on the north bank of the Senegal River, a major partner of French traders in the Atlantic gum arabic trade.
emirate-of-brakna.o: The Brakna [[e:emirate|emirate]] emerged in the 17th century in south-central [[e:mauritania|Mauritania]], as [[e:banu-hassan|Hassani Arab]] warrior groups established dominance over [[e:berbers|Berber]] scholarly tribes after the Char Bouba war of the 1670s. Its territory lay around [[e:aleg|Aleg]] and along the right bank of the [[e:senegal-river|Senegal River]].
emirate-of-brakna.r: The emir ruled a hierarchical society of Hassani warriors, [[e:zawaya|Zawaya]] scholarly tribes, tributaries and enslaved people. Wealth came from livestock and especially from gum arabic, sold to French and other European traders at river trading posts in exchange for cloth, guns and customs payments. The [[e:emir|emirs]] fought frequently with the [[s:emirate-of-trarza|Emirate of Trarza]] and with the [[s:imamate-of-futa-toro|Imamate of Futa Toro]] across the river.
emirate-of-brakna.e: Succession disputes weakened the [[e:emirate|emirate]] in the 19th century. In 1903 [[e:france|France]], under [[e:xavier-coppolani|Xavier Coppolani's]] policy of peaceful penetration, made Brakna a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]], and it became part of [[s:french-mauritania|French Mauritania]].

eastern-wei.t: The eastern half of the divided Northern Wei, a puppet state of the general Gao Huan at Ye, which his son turned into the Northern Qi in 550.
eastern-wei.o: After the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] emperor [[e:emperor-xiaowu-of-northern-wei|Xiaowu]] fled from [[e:gao-huan|Gao Huan's]] control to [[e:yuwen-tai|Yuwen Tai]] at [[e:changan|Chang'an]] in 534, [[e:gao|Gao]] Huan installed the boy [[e:emperor-xiaojing-of-eastern-wei|Yuan Shanjian]] as Emperor Xiaojing and moved the court from [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]] to Ye. The Wei realm was thus divided between Eastern Wei and [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]].
eastern-wei.r: Eastern Wei held the richer and more populous [[e:north-china-plain|North China Plain]], and real power lay with [[e:gao-huan|Gao Huan]], based at [[e:jinyang|Jinyang]] with his [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] armies. [[e:gao|Gao]] Huan balanced [[e:xianbei|Xianbei]] soldiers and Chinese aristocrats and fought repeated wars with [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]], suffering defeat at [[e:battle-of-shayuan|Shayuan]] in 537 and failing to take [[e:battle-of-yubi|Yubi]] in 546.
eastern-wei.e: After [[e:gao-huan|Gao Huan's]] death in 547 his general [[e:hou-jing|Hou Jing]] defected to the south, and his son [[e:gao-cheng|Gao Cheng]] was assassinated in 549. Another son, [[e:emperor-wenxuan-of-northern-qi|Gao Yang]], forced [[e:emperor-xiaojing-of-eastern-wei|Emperor Xiaojing]] to abdicate in 550 and founded the [[s:northern-qi|Northern Qi]].

earldom-of-ormond.t: The great Butler lordship of Kilkenny and Tipperary, for four centuries one of Ireland's most powerful Anglo-Irish dynasties and a loyal crown ally.
earldom-of-ormond.o: The [[e:butler-dynasty|Butlers]] descended from [[e:theobald-walter|Theobald Walter]], who came to Ireland with Prince John in 1185 and held the hereditary office of butler of Ireland. In 1328 [[e:james-butler-1st-earl-of-ormond|James Butler]] became the first Earl of Ormond and was granted palatine rights over [[e:county-tipperary|Tipperary]].
earldom-of-ormond.r: The earls ruled their palatinate from [[e:kilkenny-castle|Kilkenny Castle]], bought in 1391, and [[e:carrick-on-suir|Carrick-on-Suir]], with their own courts. Generally loyal to the crown, they were rivals of the [[e:kildare|Kildare]] and [[s:earldom-of-desmond|Desmond FitzGeralds]]. [[e:thomas-butler-10th-earl-of-ormond|Thomas Butler]], the 10th Earl, helped crush the Desmond rebellions; [[e:james-butler-1st-duke-of-ormonde|James Butler, 1st Duke of Ormonde]], was Lord Lieutenant under [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]].
earldom-of-ormond.e: [[e:james-butler-1st-earl-of-ormond|James Butler]], 2nd Duke, joined the [[e:jacobitism|Jacobites]] and was attainted in 1715, and the [[e:county-tipperary|Tipperary]] palatinate was abolished in 1716. The [[e:butler-dynasty|Butlers]] kept [[e:kilkenny-castle|Kilkenny Castle]] until 1967.

exarchate-of-ravenna.t: Byzantine province ruling what remained of imperial Italy from Ravenna, under an exarch combining military and civil power, until the Lombards took Ravenna in 751.
exarchate-of-ravenna.o: After the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] invasion of 568 broke Byzantine [[e:italy|Italy]] into scattered territories, Emperor Maurice concentrated civil and military authority in a single governor, the exarch, based at [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]]. The office is first attested in 584. It was a new form of government designed for a frontier under constant attack.
exarchate-of-ravenna.r: The exarch governed [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]], the [[e:pentapolis-italy|Pentapolis]], the [[s:duchy-of-rome|Duchy of Rome]], [[e:naples|Naples]], [[e:venetia|Venetia]] and other fragments, commanding local garrisons whose officers became a landed aristocracy. Relations with the popes were often tense, especially over [[e:monothelitism|Monothelitism]] and [[e:byzantine-iconoclasm|Iconoclasm]]. Several exarchs rebelled, among them [[e:eleutherius-exarch|Eleutherius]] in 619 and [[e:olympius-exarch|Olympius]] in 649. Ravenna remained a centre of Greek-[[e:latin|Latin]] culture, its churches adorned with mosaics.
exarchate-of-ravenna.e: [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] pressure grew in the 8th century; King [[e:aistulf|Aistulf]] captured [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] in 751, killing or expelling the last exarch, [[e:eutychius-exarch|Eutychius]]. When [[e:pepin-the-short|Pepin the Short]] defeated Aistulf, he gave the exarchate's lands to the pope in 756, forming the core of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].

electorate-of-mainz.t: The most powerful church state of the Holy Roman Empire, whose archbishop was arch-chancellor of Germany and convened the elections of kings.
electorate-of-mainz.o: The see of [[e:mainz|Mainz]] was raised to an archbishopric around 780 to 782, building on the work of [[e:saint-boniface|Saint Boniface]], archbishop there from 746. Its province became the largest in [[e:latin-christendom|Latin Christendom]]. Royal grants from the [[e:ottonian-dynasty|Ottonians]] onwards gave the archbishops temporal lordship over Mainz and scattered lands along the Main, the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], in [[e:hesse|Hesse]] and the [[e:eichsfeld|Eichsfeld]].
electorate-of-mainz.r: From 965 the archbishop held the title of arch-chancellor of [[e:germany|Germany]], and the [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] confirmed him as first among the seven prince-[[e:prince-elector|electors]], presiding over imperial elections. [[e:mainz|Mainz]] was governed by its cathedral chapter and archbishop. [[e:johannes-gutenberg|Gutenberg]] invented [[e:printing-press|printing]] there in the 1450s, and the university was founded in 1477.
electorate-of-mainz.e: [[e:france|France]] occupied the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] during the [[e:french-revolutionary-wars|Revolutionary Wars]], and the short-lived [[s:republic-of-mainz|Republic of Mainz]] was proclaimed in 1793. The [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Reichsdeputationshauptschluss]] of 1803 dissolved the electorate; its last elector, [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Karl Theodor von Dalberg]], kept a state centred on [[e:aschaffenburg|Aschaffenburg]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]].

eastern-hungarian-kingdom.t: Rival Hungarian kingdom of John Zápolya and his son, backed by the Ottomans, which became the seed of the Principality of Transylvania.
eastern-hungarian-kingdom.o: After King [[e:louis-ii-of-hungary|Louis II]] died at [[e:battle-of-mohacs|Mohács]] in 1526, the Hungarian nobility split. A diet at [[e:szekesfehervar|Székesfehérvár]] crowned [[e:john-zapolya|John Zápolya]], voivode of [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]], in November 1526, while a rival diet chose [[e:ferdinand-i-holy-roman-emperor|Ferdinand of Habsburg]]. Driven out by Ferdinand in 1527, Zápolya accepted the protection of [[e:suleiman-the-magnificent|Sultan Suleiman]], who restored him to [[e:buda|Buda]] in 1529.
eastern-hungarian-kingdom.r: The kingdom held the eastern half of [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] under Ottoman suzerainty. After [[e:john-zapolya|Zápolya]]'s death in 1540, his widow [[e:isabella-jagiellon|Isabella Jagiellon]] and the [[e:bishop|bishop]] [[e:george-martinuzzi|George Martinuzzi]] governed for the infant [[e:john-sigismund-zapolya|John Sigismund]]. When Suleiman seized [[e:buda|Buda]] in 1541, the court moved to [[e:alba-iulia|Gyulafehérvár]]. The [[e:edict-of-torda|Diet of Torda]] in 1568 proclaimed broad religious freedom.
eastern-hungarian-kingdom.e: By the Treaty of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]] in 1570, [[e:john-sigismund-zapolya|John Sigismund]] gave up the title of king and was recognised as [[e:prince-of-transylvania|Prince of Transylvania]], turning the realm into the [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Principality of Transylvania]]. The division between [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1526-1867|Royal Hungary]], [[e:ottoman-hungary|Ottoman Hungary]] and [[e:transylvania|Transylvania]] lasted until the late 17th century.

egypt-under-muhammad-ali.t: Egypt transformed by Muhammad Ali and his heirs into a modernising, expansionist power, nominally Ottoman but effectively independent.
egypt-under-muhammad-ali.o: [[e:muhammad-ali-of-egypt|Muhammad Ali]], an Albanian officer sent to fight the French, exploited the chaos after the [[s:french-occupation-of-egypt|French occupation of Egypt]] and was recognised as Ottoman governor in 1805. He destroyed the [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] leadership in the [[e:cairo-citadel|Cairo Citadel]] massacre of 1811.
egypt-under-muhammad-ali.r: He built a [[e:conscription|conscript]] army and navy, factories and schools, sent students to [[e:france|France]] and made [[e:cotton|cotton]] a state-controlled export. His armies fought the [[e:wahhabism|Wahhabis]] in [[e:arabia|Arabia]], conquered [[e:sudan|Sudan]] in 1820 to 1821 and, under his son Ibrahim, invaded [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] in 1831. The European powers forced him back in 1840 but granted his family hereditary rule. [[e:said-pasha|Said Pasha]] granted the [[e:suez-canal|Suez Canal]] concession in 1854.
egypt-under-muhammad-ali.e: In 1867 the Ottoman sultan granted [[e:isma-il-pasha|Ismail Pasha]] the title of khedive, turning the province into the [[s:khedivate-of-egypt|Khedivate of Egypt]]. The dynasty ruled [[e:egypt|Egypt]] until 1953, and [[e:muhammad-ali-of-egypt|Muhammad Ali]]'s reforms laid the foundations of the modern Egyptian state, army and administration.

emar.t: Emar, a Syrian trading city at the great bend of the Euphrates whose Late Bronze Age tablets show daily life and ritual under Hittite overlordship.
emar.o: Emar is named in the archives of [[s:ebla|Ebla]] and [[s:mari|Mari]] as a market town where caravans from [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] met boats on the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]]. Its position at the river's westward bend made it a key stage on the route between [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]] and the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] from the mid-3rd millennium BCE.
emar.r: In the 14th century BCE the city was rebuilt on a new site as the capital of the land of Ashtata, governed by local kings and a council of elders under the [[s:viceroyalty-of-carchemish|Viceroyalty of Carchemish]] and the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]]. Over a thousand Akkadian tablets record land sales, adoptions, wills and the festivals of the god [[e:dagan|Dagan]].
emar.e: Emar was destroyed c. 1185 BCE in the wave of violence that ended the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]]. Its site at Meskene was partly flooded by [[e:lake-assad|Lake Assad]] after the [[e:tabqa-dam|Tabqa Dam]], and French salvage excavations in the 1970s recovered its archives.
