early-duchy-of-aquitaine.t: Independent duchy of south-western Gaul whose dukes defied the Franks and fought the Umayyad advance in the 8th century.
early-duchy-of-aquitaine.o: As Merovingian power weakened in the mid 7th century, the region south of the [[e:loire|Loire]] came under semi-independent dukes. [[e:felix-of-aquitaine|Felix]], a nobleman of [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]], is recorded around 660, followed by [[e:lupus-i-of-aquitaine|Lupus]] and then [[e:odo-the-great|Odo]], called the Great, who ruled [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] and [[e:gascony|Gascony]] from around 700.
early-duchy-of-aquitaine.r: The duchy kept a strong Gallo-Roman identity and [[e:roman-law|Roman law]]. [[e:odo-the-great|Odo]] defeated an [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] army besieging [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]] in 721, one of the first checks on the Muslim advance, but was routed near [[e:bordeaux|Bordeaux]] in 732 and had to seek help from [[e:charles-martel|Charles Martel]], joining him at the battle near [[e:tours|Tours]].
early-duchy-of-aquitaine.e: [[e:odo-the-great|Odo]]'s son [[e:hunald-i-of-aquitaine|Hunald]] and grandson [[e:waiofar|Waiofar]] resisted the [[e:carolingian-empire|Carolingians]], but [[e:pepin-the-short|Pippin the Short]] waged yearly wars against Waiofar until his murder in 768. A last rising under a second Hunald was crushed by [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] in 769, and [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]].

el-tajin.t: The leading city of north-central Veracruz, renowned for the Pyramid of the Niches and for its many ballcourts carved with scenes of sacrifice.
el-tajin.o: El Tajín grew in the hills of north-central [[e:veracruz|Veracruz]], in a region of rich rainfall and tropical farming. It became a significant centre from about 600 CE and reached its greatest size after the decline of [[s:teotihuacan|Teotihuacan]], dominating the [[e:gulf-coast-of-mexico|Gulf Coast]] region later known as [[s:totonac-state-of-cempoala|Totonacapan]].
el-tajin.r: The [[e:pyramid-of-the-niches|Pyramid of the Niches]], with 365 recesses, and the Tajín Chico palace area display a distinctive style of stepped frets and flying cornices. At least 17 ballcourts have been found; panels in the South Ballcourt show players, sacrifice and the gods. A ruler named 13 Rabbit appears on columns of the Building of the Columns. The economy probably relied on [[e:maize|maize]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and vanilla.
el-tajin.e: El Tajín declined and was largely abandoned around 1200, possibly after burning. The [[e:totonacs|Totonac]] people later dominated the region. It was rediscovered in 1785 and declared a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1992.

emirate-of-bohtan.t: A Kurdish emirate at Cizre on the Tigris, setting of the epic Mem u Zin and seat of Bedir Khan, whose revolt shaped modern Kurdish nationalism.
emirate-of-bohtan.o: The Azizan family, which claimed descent from the Arab general [[e:khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]], ruled [[e:cizre|Jazirat ibn Umar]] (Cizre) and the Bohtan region on the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] from the late [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]], their power predating the arrival of the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].
emirate-of-bohtan.r: After 1514 the [[e:emirate|emirate]] accepted Ottoman suzerainty and kept hereditary rule. [[e:cizre|Cizre]] was a centre of Kurdish learning: the poet [[e:ahmad-khani|Ahmad Khani]] set his epic [[e:mem-and-zin|Mem u Zin]] of 1692 at its court. In the 1840s [[e:bedir-khan-beg|Bedir Khan Beg]] extended his power across the region, and his forces massacred Assyrian Christians of Hakkari in 1843 and 1846.
emirate-of-bohtan.e: Ottoman troops defeated [[e:bedir-khan-beg|Bedir Khan]] in 1847 and exiled him to [[e:crete|Crete]], ending the [[e:emirate|emirate]]. His descendants, the Bedirxan family, became leading Kurdish nationalists, publishing the first Kurdish newspaper, [[e:kurdistan|Kurdistan]], in 1898.

eshnunna.t: An Amorite-era kingdom in the Diyala valley whose law code is one of the oldest in the world and whose kings rivalled Hammurabi of Babylon.
eshnunna.o: Eshnunna, modern Tell Asmar, had been a city since the [[e:early-dynastic-period|Early Dynastic period]] and a province of the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]]. As Ur collapsed around 2028 BCE its governor [[e:ilshu-iliya|Ilshu-iliya]] declared independence, and the city became the centre of a kingdom controlling the [[e:diyala-river|Diyala]] valley and the routes from [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]] into the [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]].
eshnunna.r: Its god was [[e:tishpak|Tishpak]], and its rulers styled themselves his servants before claiming full kingship. Under [[e:ipiq-adad-ii|Ipiq-Adad II]], [[e:naram-sin|Naram-Sin]] and [[e:dadusha|Dadusha]] in the 19th and early 18th centuries BCE it expanded to the middle [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] and [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]]. The [[e:laws-of-eshnunna|Laws of Eshnunna]], found at [[e:tell-harmal|Tell Harmal]] (ancient Shaduppum), set prices, wages and penalties in Akkadian and predate [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi's]] code. [[e:oriental-institute|Oriental Institute]] excavations in the 1930s also found the Tell Asmar hoard of praying statues.
eshnunna.e: Eshnunna fought [[s:mari|Mari]], [[e:elam|Elam]] and [[e:babylon|Babylon]] for supremacy. In 1762 BCE [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi]] defeated it and it became part of the [[s:babylonian-empire|Babylonian Empire]]; a later year name of his records the destruction of Eshnunna by flood waters.

epidii.t: People of Kintyre in western Scotland recorded by Ptolemy, whose name means 'horse people' and whose land later became the heart of Dál Riata.
epidii.o: [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 places the Epidii in the [[e:kintyre|Kintyre]] peninsula and neighbouring islands of [[e:argyll|Argyll]], with the [[e:mull-of-kintyre|Mull of Kintyre]] named Epidion Akron after them. Their name comes from the Brittonic word for horse, suggesting a people who honoured horses or a horse deity.
epidii.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or institutions. [[e:kintyre|Kintyre]] and the islands were a land of duns, crannogs and small forts, with the sea as the main highway. The peninsula lies only about 20 kilometres from [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]], and contact with Ireland was constant across the [[e:north-channel|North Channel]].
epidii.e: The Epidii disappear from the record after Ptolemy. By the 6th century their region was ruled by the Gaelic kings of [[s:dal-riata|Dál Riata]], whose territory spanned [[e:argyll|Argyll]] and north [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]], and [[e:kintyre|Kintyre]] was held by its leading kindred, the [[s:cenel-ngabrain|Cenél nGabráin]].

empire-of-nicaea.t: The largest Byzantine successor state after 1204, which rebuilt Byzantine power in Anatolia and recaptured Constantinople in 1261.
empire-of-nicaea.o: As the [[e:fourth-crusade|Fourth Crusade]] took [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 1204, [[e:theodore-i-laskaris|Theodore Laskaris]], son-in-law of [[e:alexios-iii-angelos|Alexios III]], gathered refugees and troops in [[s:kingdom-of-bithynia|Bithynia]]. With [[e:nicaea|Nicaea]] as his base he fought off the [[e:latins|Latins]] and the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]], and in 1208 had himself crowned emperor by a newly elected patriarch, giving his state the strongest claim to Byzantine legitimacy.
empire-of-nicaea.r: The [[e:laskarid-dynasty|Laskarid]] emperors governed through a Byzantine-style court and bureaucracy, with the patriarch residing at [[e:nicaea|Nicaea]] and the court often at [[e:nymphaion|Nymphaion]]. [[e:john-iii-doukas-vatatzes|John III Vatatzes]] promoted agricultural self-sufficiency, restricted luxury imports, founded charities and expanded into [[e:europe|Europe]], taking [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]] in 1246. Scholarship flourished under [[e:nikephoros-blemmydes|Nikephoros Blemmydes]] and [[e:theodore-ii-laskaris|Theodore II Laskaris]].
empire-of-nicaea.e: [[e:michael-viii-palaiologos|Michael VIII Palaiologos]] seized power from the boy emperor [[e:john-iv-laskaris|John IV]], defeated the [[e:latin|Latins]] and Epirotes at [[e:battle-of-pelagonia|Pelagonia]] in 1259 and took [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in July 1261, restoring the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]]. Neglect of the Anatolian frontier after the move opened the way to Turkish expansion.

edom.t: Edom, a kingdom of the arid highlands south of the Dead Sea, rich in copper and the incense trade, rival of Judah.
edom.o: The Edomites lived in the mountains east of the [[e:arabah|Arabah]] valley, mentioned in Egyptian texts from the 13th century BCE. In the 10th century BCE large-scale [[e:copper|copper]] smelting at [[e:faynan|Faynan]], such as [[e:khirbat-en-nahas|Khirbat en-Nahas]], supported an emerging elite, and a kingdom with its capital at [[e:bozrah|Bozrah]] formed by the 8th century BCE.
edom.r: Edomite kings worshipped the god Qos and drew revenue from [[e:copper|copper]] and from [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] carrying Arabian [[e:incense|incense]] to [[s:gaza|Gaza]]. The Bible records wars with the [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Kingdom of Judah]]. Edom became a loyal [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], and kings such as [[e:qaus-gabri|Qaus-gabri]] sent tribute and workers.
edom.e: Edom survived the fall of [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] but lost its independence to [[e:nabonidus|Nabonidus]] of the [[s:chaldean-empire|Chaldean Empire]], who campaigned there c. 552 BCE. Edomites later settled in southern [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Judah]], which became [[e:idumaea|Idumaea]], while Arab groups and the [[s:nabataean-kingdom|Nabataean Kingdom]] took their old lands.

eleutherna.t: Hill city of western Crete on the slopes of Mount Ida whose Orthi Petra cemetery has revealed rich warrior burials of the early Iron Age.
eleutherna.o: Eleutherna occupied a long ridge on the north-west slopes of [[e:mount-ida-crete|Mount Ida]], inhabited since the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]]. It grew into a city in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], and by the 7th century BCE it was one of the important [[e:polis|poleis]] of [[e:crete|Crete]].
eleutherna.r: Excavations at the Orthi [[e:petra|Petra]] necropolis since 1985 have found rich burials of the 9th to 7th centuries BCE, including warriors and elite women with gold jewellery. Like other Cretan cities, Eleutherna had [[e:kosmoi|kosmoi]] magistrates and aristocratic institutions. It minted coins showing [[e:apollo|Apollo]] and took part in Hellenistic alliances and the [[s:cretan-koinon|Cretan Koinon]].
eleutherna.e: [[e:quintus-caecilius-metellus-creticus|Metellus]] captured Eleutherna during the Roman conquest of [[e:crete|Crete]] in 68 or 67 BCE. It continued as a Roman and early Byzantine town before being abandoned, probably after an earthquake in the 7th century CE.

earldom-of-bamburgh.t: The English lordship that survived the Viking conquest of York, ruling northern Northumbria from the fortress of Bamburgh.
earldom-of-bamburgh.o: When the [[e:great-heathen-army|Great Heathen Army]] took York in 867, the northern part of the [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Kingdom of Northumbria]] between the [[e:river-tees|Tees]] and the [[e:river-tweed|Tweed]] remained under English rulers based at Bamburgh. Its leaders, such as Eadwulf and his descendants, styled themselves high-reeves or even kings of the northern English.
earldom-of-bamburgh.r: Bamburgh's lords protected the community of [[e:saint-cuthbert|Saint Cuthbert]], which moved with its relics to [[e:chester-le-street|Chester-le-Street]] and then [[e:durham-england|Durham]]. They recognised [[e:wessex|West Saxon]] kings from Aethelstan onwards, while defending [[e:lothian|Lothian]] against Scottish attack. [[e:uhtred-the-bold|Uhtred the Bold]] defeated the Scots at Durham in 1006 and held the whole earldom of [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]].
earldom-of-bamburgh.e: Feuds and Danish rule weakened the house. In 1041 [[e:siward-earl-of-northumbria|Earl Siward]] killed Eadwulf, the last of the line, and united [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]] under his own authority as part of the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]]. [[e:lothian|Lothian]] had already passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]].

earldom-of-desmond.t: The FitzGerald lordship of Munster that became more Gaelic than the Gaels, destroyed in the Desmond Rebellions of the 1570s and 1580s.
earldom-of-desmond.o: The [[e:fitzgerald-dynasty|FitzGeralds]] descended from [[e:maurice-fitzgerald-lord-of-lanstephan|Maurice FitzGerald]], one of the first Cambro-Norman invaders of 1169. [[e:maurice-fitzthomas-fitzgerald-1st-earl-of-desmond|Maurice FitzThomas FitzGerald]] was created Earl of Desmond in 1329 with palatine rights over [[s:ciarraige-luachra|Kerry]].
earldom-of-desmond.r: The Desmond earls ruled much of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]] from castles such as [[e:askeaton|Askeaton]] and [[e:newcastle-west|Newcastle West]], adopting Irish language, law and patronage of poets. [[e:gerald-fitzgerald-3rd-earl-of-desmond|Gerald, the 3rd Earl]], was a noted Irish poet. They were often at odds with the [[e:butler-dynasty|Butler]] earls of the [[s:earldom-of-ormond|Earldom of Ormond]] and with the [[e:dublin|Dublin]] government.
earldom-of-desmond.e: [[e:gerald-fitzgerald-14th-earl-of-desmond|Gerald FitzGerald]], the 15th Earl, rebelled against [[e:elizabeth-i|Elizabeth I]] in the [[e:desmond-rebellions|Desmond Rebellions]]. He was killed in 1583, and his vast lands were confiscated and granted to English settlers in the Plantation of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]].

erie-nation.t: An Iroquoian people of the south shore of Lake Erie, which takes their name, destroyed by the Iroquois Confederacy in the 1650s.
erie-nation.o: The Erie lived in what is now western [[e:new-york|New York]], north-western [[e:pennsylvania|Pennsylvania]] and north-eastern [[e:ohio|Ohio]]. Little is known of their early history; they appear in French sources mainly through [[s:huron-confederacy|Huron]] informants, who called them the Cat People, perhaps after the panther, and they are known almost entirely from the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] Relations.
erie-nation.r: Like other Iroquoian peoples they lived in palisaded villages of longhouses and grew [[e:maize|maize]], beans and squash. They were said to be numerous and skilled with poisoned arrows, and to have had little direct contact with Europeans, so they lacked firearms. After 1649 refugees from the [[s:huron-confederacy|Huron Confederacy]] joined them, raising tensions with the [[s:seneca-nation|Seneca]].
erie-nation.e: In 1654, after a quarrel in which [[s:seneca-nation|Seneca]] envoys were killed, the [[s:iroquois-confederacy|Iroquois Confederacy]] invaded, and by 1656 the Erie had been defeated. Survivors were absorbed by the Seneca, and some may have moved south to become the [[e:westo|Westo]].

eastern-chalukyas.t: A Chalukya branch that ruled coastal Andhra from Vengi for over four centuries and presided over the birth of Telugu literature.
eastern-chalukyas.o: In 624 [[e:pulakeshin-ii|Pulakeshin II]] of the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]], having conquered the [[s:vishnukundina-dynasty|Vishnukundina dynasty]], made his younger brother [[e:kubja-vishnuvardhana|Kubja Vishnuvardhana]] [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] of the [[e:vengi|Vengi]] region between the [[e:krishna-river|Krishna]] and Godavari rivers. [[e:vishnuvardhana|Vishnuvardhana]] soon became independent, founding a separate line that outlived the [[e:badami|Badami]] branch.
eastern-chalukyas.r: The Eastern Chalukyas fought long wars with the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]] for control of the [[e:deccan|Deccan]]; [[e:vijayaditya-iii|Vijayaditya III]] campaigned as far as the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] according to his records. Their [[e:telugu-language|Telugu]] inscriptions are among the earliest, and under [[e:rajaraja-narendra|Rajaraja Narendra]] the poet [[e:nannaya|Nannaya]] began the [[e:andhra-mahabharatam|Telugu Mahabharata]], the founding work of Telugu literature. The fertile delta and coastal trade supported the state, and temples flourished at [[e:draksharama|Draksharama]] and [[e:bhimavaram|Bhimavaram]].
eastern-chalukyas.e: From the late 10th century the [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] dominated [[e:vengi|Vengi]] through marriage alliances. In 1070 the Eastern Chalukya prince Rajendra became [[e:chola-empire|Chola]] emperor as [[e:kulottunga-i|Kulottunga I]], and Vengi was merged into the Chola realm, the last [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]] ruling until about 1075.

egba-united-government.t: The Egba state of Abeokuta, a Yoruba refugee city that became a centre of missions and returned Saro, and stayed formally independent of Britain until 1914.
egba-united-government.o: The Egba lost their towns in the wars that followed the decline of the [[s:oyo-empire|Oyo Empire]]. Around 1830 survivors under the war leader [[e:sodeke|Sodeke]] founded [[e:abeokuta|Abeokuta]] beneath the [[e:olumo-rock|Olumo]] rock. The new city united many Egba townships, each keeping its own chiefs, and in 1854 [[e:okukenu|Okukenu]] was installed as [[e:alake-of-egbaland|Alake]], paramount ruler.
egba-united-government.r: Returned freed slaves from [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]], known as Saro, and missionaries such as [[e:henry-townsend|Henry Townsend]] and [[e:samuel-ajayi-crowther|Samuel Ajayi Crowther]] made [[e:abeokuta|Abeokuta]] a centre of [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and Western education. The Egba twice repelled sieges by the [[s:kingdom-of-dahomey|Kingdom of Dahomey]], in 1851 and 1864. In 1865 the Saro [[e:george-william-johnson|George William Johnson]] organised the [[e:egba-united-board-of-management|Egba United Board of Management]], and in 1898 a reformed Egba United Government ran a treasury, courts and roads under [[e:alake-of-egbaland|Alake]] [[e:gbadebo-i|Gbadebo I]].
egba-united-government.e: A treaty of 1893 recognised Egba independence, but British influence grew. After unrest in 1914 the Egba government lost its independence, and [[e:abeokuta|Abeokuta]] was absorbed into [[s:colonial-nigeria|Colonial Nigeria]], where the [[e:alake-of-egbaland|Alake]] remained a leading traditional ruler.

eritrea-federation.t: Eritrea's decade as an autonomous unit federated with Ethiopia, whose dismantling by Haile Selassie set off a 30-year war for independence.
eritrea-federation.o: Following a UN resolution of December 1950, [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] was federated with [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]] under the Ethiopian Crown in September 1952. It received its own constitution, an elected assembly in [[e:asmara|Asmara]], an executive and official languages, [[e:tigrinya-language|Tigrinya]] and Arabic, while [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]] controlled defence, foreign affairs, currency and trade.
eritrea-federation.r: The federation was unequal from the start. [[e:haile-selassie|Haile Selassie's]] representative steadily curtailed Eritrean autonomy: political parties and independent newspapers were suppressed, [[e:amharic|Amharic]] was imposed, and the Eritrean flag was replaced by [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia's]] in 1958. Nationalists organised the [[e:eritrean-liberation-movement|Eritrean Liberation Movement]] in 1958 and the [[e:eritrean-liberation-front|Eritrean Liberation Front]] in 1960, whose fighters under [[e:hamid-idris-awate|Hamid Idris Awate]] began armed struggle in September 1961.
eritrea-federation.e: In November 1962 the Eritrean assembly, under pressure, voted to dissolve itself, and [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] was annexed as a province of the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]]. The war that followed ended with independence as the State of [[e:eritrea|Eritrea]] in 1993.

erivan-khanate.t: The Persian-ruled khanate around Yerevan and the Ararat plain, whose conquest by Russia in 1827-1828 began modern Armenia's territorial history.
erivan-khanate.o: The [[e:yerevan|Erivan]] province had been an Iranian administrative unit since Safavid times. After the death of [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah]] in 1747, its governors acted as autonomous khans of the [[e:mount-ararat|Ararat]] plain and the area around [[e:lake-sevan|Lake Sevan]], while recognising Persian overlordship whenever a strong shah ruled.
erivan-khanate.r: The khans ruled from the fortress of [[e:yerevan|Erivan]] over a mixed population of Muslims and [[e:armenians|Armenians]], with [[e:etchmiadzin-cathedral|Etchmiadzin]], seat of the Armenian Catholicos, within the khanate. Irrigated farming of [[e:cotton|cotton]], [[e:rice|rice]] and fruit sustained it. The khanate paid tribute to the [[s:zand-empire|Zand Empire]] and to [[e:erekle-ii|Erekle II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti|Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti]] before [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]] restored control. [[e:hosein-qoli-khan-qajar|Hosein Qoli Khan Qajar]], governor from 1807, built the [[e:sardar|Sardar's]] Palace.
erivan-khanate.e: Russian troops under [[e:ivan-paskevich|Ivan Paskevich]] captured [[e:yerevan|Erivan]] in 1827, and the [[e:treaty-of-turkmenchay|Treaty of Turkmenchay]] in 1828 ceded the khanate to the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]]. Combined with [[e:nakhchivan|Nakhichevan]], it became the [[e:armenian-oblast|Armenian Oblast]], and many [[e:armenians|Armenians]] from [[e:iran|Iran]] settled there.

emirate-of-granada.t: The last Muslim state in Iberia, ruled by the Nasrid dynasty for over 250 years and builder of the Alhambra.
emirate-of-granada.o: In 1232 [[e:muhammad-i-of-granada|Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn Nasr]], known as Ibn al-Ahmar, proclaimed himself ruler at [[e:arjona|Arjona]] amid the collapse of [[e:almohad-caliphate|Almohad]] power. He took [[e:granada|Granada]] in 1237-1238 and in 1246 accepted [[e:vassal|vassalage]] to [[e:ferdinand-iii-of-castile|Ferdinand III of Castile]], ceding [[e:jaen|Jaén]] and paying tribute to survive.
emirate-of-granada.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] covered the mountains and coasts from [[e:almeria|Almería]] to [[s:gibraltar|Gibraltar]], dense with refugees from lost Andalusi cities. [[e:silk|Silk]], [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and dried fruit were exported through Málaga, often by Genoese merchants. Yusuf I and [[e:muhammad-v-of-granada|Muhammad V]] built the finest parts of the [[e:alhambra|Alhambra]], and poets such as [[e:ibn-zamrak|Ibn Zamrak]] and the [[e:vizier|vizier]] [[e:ibn-al-khatib|Ibn al-Khatib]] served the court.
emirate-of-granada.e: Weakened by dynastic feuds, [[e:granada|Granada]] fell in the war of 1482-1492. [[e:muhammad-xii-of-granada|Muhammad XII]], Boabdil, surrendered the city to Isabella I and [[e:ferdinand-ii-of-aragon|Ferdinand II]] on 2 January 1492. Its Muslims later faced forced conversion and, as [[e:moriscos|Moriscos]], expulsion.

edetani.t: An Iberian people of the Valencian plain, centred on Edeta near Llíria, whose leader Edeco was among the first to join Rome.
edetani.o: The Edetani occupied the coastal plain and hills of the modern province of [[e:valencia|Valencia]], between the [[e:jucar|Júcar]] and the [[e:mijares|Mijares]], from about the 5th century BCE. Their capital, [[e:edeta|Edeta]], stood on the hill of Tossal de Sant Miquel above [[e:lliria|Llíria]].
edetani.r: [[e:edeta|Edeta's]] excavated houses have yielded famous painted pottery showing warriors, dancers and hunting scenes, with Iberian inscriptions. The Edetani lived from farming, crafts and trade along the coast, and their leaders controlled networks of villages and watchtowers. In 209 BCE their prince [[e:edeco|Edeco]] went over to [[e:scipio-africanus|Scipio]] after the fall of [[e:carthago-nova|Carthago Nova]], recovering his family held hostage there.
edetani.e: The Edetani joined [[e:rome|Rome]] during the [[e:second-punic-war|Second Punic War]] and were absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]]. In 138 BCE the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] founded [[e:valencia|Valentia]], modern Valencia, in their territory, and [[e:edeta|Edeta]] itself was later abandoned in favour of a Roman town on the plain.

electorate-of-bavaria.t: Bavaria as one of the great electoral principalities of the Empire, a Catholic power whose dukes twice sought the imperial crown.
electorate-of-bavaria.o: [[e:maximilian-i-elector-of-bavaria|Duke Maximilian]] I, head of the [[e:catholic-league|Catholic League]], helped crush the Bohemian revolt at the [[e:battle-of-white-mountain|White Mountain]] in 1620. As a reward [[e:ferdinand-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Ferdinand II]] transferred the electoral dignity of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] to him in 1623 and gave him the [[s:upper-palatinate|Upper Palatinate]] in 1628, gains confirmed at the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648.
electorate-of-bavaria.r: The electorate was firmly Catholic, with strong ties to the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] and a rich baroque church culture. The [[e:prince-elector|electors]] built [[e:nymphenburg-palace|Nymphenburg]] and [[e:schleissheim-palace|Schleissheim]] palaces in and near [[e:munich|Munich]]. [[e:maximilian-ii-emanuel-elector-of-bavaria|Max Emanuel]] allied with [[e:france|France]] in the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]] and lost his lands after [[e:battle-of-blenheim|Blenheim]] in 1704, and [[e:charles-vii-holy-roman-emperor|Charles Albert]] was elected Emperor Charles VII in 1742 during the [[e:war-of-the-austrian-succession|Austrian Succession]] war.
electorate-of-bavaria.e: In 1777 the Bavarian [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbachs]] died out and the electorate passed to [[e:charles-theodore-elector-of-bavaria|Charles Theodore]] of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]]. Allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], [[e:maximilian-i-joseph-of-bavaria|Elector Maximilian IV Joseph]] gained large territories and became King of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] on 1 January 1806.

emirate-of-tarsus.t: The great frontier fortress of Cilicia, a base for holy war against Byzantium that drew volunteer fighters from across the Islamic world.
emirate-of-tarsus.o: [[e:tarsus|Tarsus]] lay abandoned in the frontier zone until the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]] rebuilt and garrisoned it in the late 8th century, a project completed under [[e:harun-al-rashid|Harun al-Rashid]]. It became the chief city of the Cilician thughur, the line of fortified towns on the Byzantine border.
emirate-of-tarsus.r: The city was governed by appointees of [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]] and later of the [[s:tulunid-emirate|Tulunids]], [[s:ikhshidid-emirate|Ikhshidids]] and [[e:hamdanid-dynasty|Hamdanids]], but its garrison and civic leaders acted largely independently. Volunteers came from [[e:khorasan|Khurasan]], [[e:iraq|Iraq]] and [[e:egypt|Egypt]] to live in [[e:ribat|ribats]], fortified hostels, and join the annual raids. Commanders such as [[e:yazaman-al-khadim|Yazaman al-Khadim]] and [[e:thamal-al-dulafi|Thamal al-Dulafi]] led land and naval raids into [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] and the [[e:aegean|Aegean]], and prisoner exchanges with [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] were held on the nearby [[e:lamos-river|Lamos]] river.
emirate-of-tarsus.e: In 965 the Byzantine emperor [[e:nikephoros-ii-phokas|Nikephoros II Phokas]] captured [[e:tarsus|Tarsus]] after a long [[e:naval-blockade|blockade]]. Its Muslim inhabitants were allowed to leave and the city was resettled with Christians, ending more than two centuries of Muslim rule in [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]].

epirote-league.t: Federal republic of the peoples of Epirus that replaced the Aeacid monarchy and ended in mass enslavement by Rome in 167 BCE.
epirote-league.o: Around 232 BCE the last of the royal [[e:aeacidae|Aeacid]] family, [[e:deidamia-ii-of-epirus|Deidamia]], was killed and the [[e:molossians|Molossians]], [[e:chaonians|Chaonians]] and [[e:thesprotians|Thesprotians]] abolished the monarchy of the [[s:kingdom-of-epirus|Kingdom of Epirus]]. They formed a federal state, the Koinon of the Epirotes, whose meetings were often held at [[e:phoenice|Phoenice]] in [[e:chaonia|Chaonia]], near the Ionian coast.
epirote-league.r: The league was led by annually elected generals and a federal assembly, and minted coins showing [[e:zeus|Zeus]] and [[e:dione|Dione of Dodona]]. Its regions remained distinct, and wealth came from herding and trade with [[e:italy|Italy]]. Illyrian raiders under Queen [[e:teuta|Teuta]] sacked [[e:phoenice|Phoenice]] in 230 BCE. The [[e:peace-of-phoenice|Peace of Phoenice]], ending the [[e:first-macedonian-war|First Macedonian War]] in 205 BCE, was signed there.
epirote-league.e: In the [[e:third-macedonian-war|Third Macedonian War]] the [[e:molossians|Molossians]] sided with [[e:perseus-of-macedon|Perseus]] while other Epirotes supported [[e:rome|Rome]]. In 167 BCE the [[s:commune-of-rome|Roman Senate]] ordered [[e:lucius-aemilius-paullus-macedonicus|Lucius Aemilius Paullus]] to punish [[e:epirus|Epirus]]: seventy towns were plundered and about 150,000 people enslaved, ending the league.
epirote-league.re: Ancient Greek religion (cult of Zeus at Dodona)

elisu-sultanate.t: A small Tsakhur sultanate in the foothills of north-western Azerbaijan whose last sultan defected from Russia to join Imam Shamil.
elisu-sultanate.o: The Elisu Sultanate took shape around 1604 among the [[e:tsakhurs|Tsakhur]] people of the southern slopes of the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]], centred on the village of [[e:ilisu|Ilisu]]. Its rulers, who took the title sultan, emerged as the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]] reasserted control over the region after wars with the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].
elisu-sultanate.r: The sultans ruled [[e:tsakhurs|Tsakhur]], Azerbaijani and Georgian-speaking [[e:ingiloys|Ingiloy]] villages, collecting tribute and leading raids into [[s:kingdom-of-kakheti|Kakheti]]. The land lived by herding, orchards and [[e:silk|silk]]. Its rulers balanced between the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]], the khanates of [[e:shaki-azerbaijan|Shaki]] and [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvan]], the [[e:lezgins|Lezgin]] free communities of Jar and [[e:balakan|Belokan]] and later [[e:russia|Russia]].
elisu-sultanate.e: The sultanate accepted Russian protection in 1803. In 1844 [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:daniyal-bek|Daniyal Bek]], though a Russian major general, joined [[e:imam-shamil|Imam Shamil's]] [[s:caucasian-imamate|Caucasian Imamate]], and the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] abolished the sultanate. Daniyal [[e:bek|Bek]] became one of Shamil's naibs and later made peace with [[e:russia|Russia]].

etowah-chiefdom.t: A Mississippian mound centre in northern Georgia whose temple mounds, copper plates and marble statues make it one of the richest sites of the ancient South-East.
etowah-chiefdom.o: Farming villages on the [[e:etowah-river|Etowah River]] near modern [[e:cartersville-georgia|Cartersville, Georgia]], were occupied from around 1000, and mound building began in the following century. The site was abandoned and reoccupied more than once, reaching its height between about 1250 and 1375, when a palisade and ditch enclosed the town and its plazas.
etowah-chiefdom.r: Etowah was ruled by a hereditary chiefly elite who lived on and were buried in its platform mounds; the largest, Mound A, rises some 19 metres. Burials in Mound C held embossed [[e:copper|copper]] plates, shell gorgets, ceremonial stone axes and a pair of painted marble figures, classic objects of the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex. [[e:maize|Maize]], beans and squash fed the population, and long-distance exchange brought copper from the [[e:great-lakes|Great Lakes]] and shell from the Gulf coast.
etowah-chiefdom.e: By the 1500s Etowah was a smaller town, probably the Itaba visited by [[e:hernando-de-soto|Hernando de Soto]] in 1540 and then subject to the [[s:coosa-chiefdom|Coosa chiefdom]]. Epidemics and the collapse of Mississippian chiefdoms left it deserted, and later [[e:muscogee|Muscogee]] and [[e:cherokee|Cherokee peoples]] lived in the region.

emirate-of-chefchaouen.t: A mountain emirate in the Rif founded as a base for holy war against Portuguese Ceuta, a refuge for exiles from Granada.
emirate-of-chefchaouen.o: [[e:chefchaouen|Chefchaouen]] was founded in 1471 by [[e:ali-ibn-rashid|Ali ibn Rashid]], a sharif of the Banu Rashid, as a fortified base for raids against the Portuguese enclaves of [[s:portuguese-morocco|Portuguese Morocco]] around [[e:ceuta|Ceuta]] and [[e:ksar-es-seghir|Ksar es-Seghir]]. Muslim and Jewish refugees from [[e:granada|Granada]] swelled the town after 1492.
emirate-of-chefchaouen.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled the western Rif and [[e:jbala|Jbala]] hills semi-independently, nominally recognising the [[s:wattasid-sultanate|Wattasid Sultanate]] in [[e:fez|Fez]]. Andalusi settlers gave the town its whitewashed houses and craft traditions. Ali's daughter [[e:sayyida-al-hurra|Sayyida al-Hurra]] married the lord of [[e:tetouan|Tetouan]] and later governed that city herself, linking the two states.
emirate-of-chefchaouen.e: The [[s:saadi-sultanate|Saadi Sultanate]] subdued the [[e:emirate|emirate]] around 1561, ending Banu Rashid rule. [[e:chefchaouen|Chefchaouen]] remained a closed holy town, rarely visited by Europeans before the 20th century, and is today a well-known Moroccan city.

early-cheras.t: The Sangam-age Chera kings of the south-west coast, who sold pepper to the Roman world through the port of Muziris.
early-cheras.o: The [[e:chera-dynasty|Cheras]] were one of the three crowned dynasties of ancient [[e:tamilakam|Tamilakam]], with the [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]] and the [[s:chola-empire|Cholas]]. [[e:ashoka|Ashoka's]] edicts in the 3rd century BCE name the Keralaputras among independent peoples beyond his empire. Their territory covered the [[e:malabar-coast|Malabar]] coast and the [[e:kongu-nadu|Kongu]] country inland; their capital [[e:vanchi|Vanchi]] is identified with [[e:karur|Karur]] in [[e:tamil-nadu|Tamil Nadu]] by most historians.
early-cheras.r: [[e:chera-dynasty|Chera]] power rested on trade: [[e:pepper|pepper]], [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and gems were shipped from [[e:muziris|Muziris]] and other ports to [[s:roman-egypt|Roman Egypt]], as recorded in the [[e:periplus-of-the-erythraean-sea|Periplus of the Erythraean Sea]] and the Muziris [[e:papyrus|papyrus]]. The [[e:patirruppattu|Pathitrupathu]], a [[e:sangam-literature|Sangam]] anthology, praises a succession of Chera kings, among them [[e:imayavaramban-nedunceralatan|Imayavaramban Nedunceralatan]] and [[e:senguttuvan|Senguttuvan]], who also appears in the epic [[e:silappatikaram|Silappatikaram]]. [[e:tamil-brahmi|Tamil-Brahmi]] inscriptions at [[e:pugalur|Pugalur]] name kings of the Irumporai branch.
early-cheras.e: After the 3rd century the [[e:chera-dynasty|Cheras]] fade from view during the poorly documented age of the [[s:kalabhra-dynasty|Kalabhra dynasty]]. A later Chera state, the [[s:chera-perumals-of-makotai|Chera Perumals of Makotai]], arose on the [[e:kerala|Kerala]] coast in the 9th century and claimed their legacy.
early-cheras.re: Tamil folk religion, Vedic religion, Jainism

ekron.t: Ekron, a Philistine city that grew into the largest olive-oil producer of the ancient Near East under Assyrian rule.
ekron.o: Ekron, at Tel Miqne, was refounded in the 12th century BCE by newcomers whose pottery, hearths and diet show roots in the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] world. They built a planned town that formed one of the five cities of the [[s:philistine-pentapolis|Philistine Pentapolis]].
ekron.r: Ekron shrank in the 10th century BCE, then boomed in the 7th as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], with over a hundred olive presses producing oil for export. A dedication inscription found in 1996 names [[e:ikausu|Ikausu]] son of [[e:padi|Padi]] as king and the goddess Ptgyh, confirming the city's identity.
ekron.e: In 701 BCE [[e:padi|Padi]] was handed to [[e:hezekiah|Hezekiah]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Kingdom of Judah]] by rebels, then restored by [[e:sennacherib|Sennacherib]]. [[e:nebuchadnezzar-ii|Nebuchadnezzar II]] of the [[s:chaldean-empire|Chaldean Empire]] destroyed Ekron in 604 BCE, ending the city.

emirate-of-kish.t: A seafaring island emirate in the Persian Gulf that dominated trade between Iraq, India and Arabia in the 12th century.
emirate-of-kish.o: As the port of [[e:siraf|Siraf]] declined after its 10th-century earthquake, merchants and sea captains on the island of [[s:kish|Kish]], called [[e:qays|Qays]] in Arabic, took over its trade. By around 1100 a local dynasty, the Banu Qaysar, ruled an independent [[e:emirate|emirate]] there.
emirate-of-kish.r: [[s:kish|Kish]] lived from maritime commerce and from levying ships passing through the [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]], and it maintained a fleet that raided rival ports and even attacked [[e:aden|Aden]] in 1135. It controlled the pearl fisheries and at times the [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] islands. Geographers such as [[e:yaqut-al-hamawi|Yaqut]] describe its markets and its rulers' wealth, but its internal history is poorly recorded.
emirate-of-kish.e: In 1229 the island was conquered by the [[e:salghurids|Salghurid]] atabegs of [[e:fars|Fars]] with help from the [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Kingdom of Ormus]], which then inherited much of its trade.

etruscan-league.t: Federation of twelve Etruscan city-states that met yearly at the sanctuary of Voltumna, more a religious union than a military alliance.
etruscan-league.o: By the 6th century BCE the leading cities of [[e:etruria|Etruria]] formed a group known to the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] as the twelve peoples of Etruria. Its focus was the [[e:fanum-voltumnae|Fanum Voltumnae]], a federal sanctuary near [[s:volsinii|Volsinii]], possibly at [[e:campo-della-fiera|Campo della Fiera]] below [[s:commune-of-orvieto|Orvieto]], where delegates met each spring.
etruscan-league.r: The list of members changed over time but usually included [[s:veii|Veii]], [[s:caere|Caere]], [[s:tarquinii|Tarquinii]], [[s:vulci|Vulci]], [[s:volsinii|Volsinii]], [[s:clusium|Clusium]], [[s:perusia|Perusia]], [[s:cortona|Cortona]], [[s:arretium|Arretium]], [[s:volaterrae|Volaterrae]], [[s:vetulonia|Vetulonia]] or [[s:rusellae|Rusellae]], and [[s:populonia|Populonia]]. The annual gathering combined sacrifices, games and markets with political councils, and chose a federal leader whose powers were mainly ceremonial. It rarely acted together in war: [[e:livy|Livy]] says it refused to help Veii against [[e:rome|Rome]].
etruscan-league.e: As [[e:rome|Rome]] conquered the Etruscan cities one by one, the League lost all political weight, ending with the destruction of [[s:volsinii|Volsinii]] in 264 BCE. Under the Empire a ceremonial league of fifteen peoples was revived with a praetor of [[e:etruria|Etruria]], and the festival was still held in the 4th century CE.

early-pandyas.t: The Pandya kings of Madurai in the Sangam age, masters of the pearl fisheries of the far south and patrons of early Tamil poetry.
early-pandyas.o: The [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]] were one of the three crowned dynasties of ancient [[e:tamilakam|Tamilakam]], with the [[e:chera-dynasty|Cheras]] and the [[s:chola-empire|Cholas]]. [[e:megasthenes|Megasthenes]] heard of them around 300 BCE, and [[e:ashoka|Ashoka's]] edicts in the 3rd century BCE name the [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandyas]] as independent neighbours beyond his empire. Their heartland was the Vaigai valley around [[e:madurai|Madurai]] and the coast near [[e:korkai|Korkai]].
early-pandyas.r: [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandya]] wealth came from pearls and conch shells from the [[e:gulf-of-mannar|Gulf of Mannar]], traded with the Roman world through ports such as [[e:korkai|Korkai]], and from [[e:rice|rice]] farming. Tamil tradition places the [[e:sangam-literature|Sangam]] literary academies at [[e:madurai|Madurai]] under Pandya patronage, and Sangam poems praise kings such as [[e:nedunjeliyan-ii|Nedunjeliyan]], victor at the battle of [[e:battle-of-talaiyalanganam|Talaiyalanganam]] over the [[e:chera-dynasty|Cheras]] and [[s:chola-empire|Cholas]]. [[e:tamil-brahmi|Tamil-Brahmi]] inscriptions record gifts to [[e:jainism|Jain]] monks.
early-pandyas.e: Around the 3rd century the [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]], like their neighbours, were displaced by the [[s:kalabhra-dynasty|Kalabhra dynasty]], whose rule is poorly documented. The dynasty revived in the late 6th century as the [[s:first-pandyan-empire|First Pandyan Empire]] under [[e:kadungon|Kadungon]].
early-pandyas.re: Tamil folk religion, Vedic religion, Jainism

electoral-palatinate.t: The Rhineland electorate of the Wittelsbach counts palatine, centre of German Calvinism, whose elector's Bohemian adventure began the Thirty Years' War.
electoral-palatinate.o: The counts palatine of [[s:duchy-of-lotharingia|Lotharingia]], royal deputies in the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]], moved their power to the middle [[e:rhine|Rhine]]; around 1085 to 1087 [[e:henry-of-laach|Henry of Laach]] is first called count palatine of the Rhine. Under the [[e:hohenstaufen|Staufer]] and from 1214 the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbachs]], the Palatinate grew around [[e:heidelberg|Heidelberg]], [[e:alzey|Alzey]] and the upper Rhine.
electoral-palatinate.r: The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] made the count palatine an elector and imperial vicar. [[e:rupert-i-elector-palatine|Rupert I]] founded the [[e:heidelberg-university|University of Heidelberg]] in 1386, and [[e:rupert-of-germany|Rupert III]] became King of the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] in 1400. [[e:frederick-iii-elector-palatine|Elector Frederick III]] adopted [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]] and sponsored the [[e:heidelberg-catechism|Heidelberg Catechism]] of 1563, making the Palatinate the leading Reformed state of the Empire.
electoral-palatinate.e: [[e:frederick-v-of-the-palatinate|Frederick V]] accepted the Bohemian crown in 1619 and lost his lands and electoral vote. The Palatinate was devastated in [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years' War and again by [[e:france|France]] in 1689. France annexed the left bank in 1797, and in 1803 the remaining lands went to [[e:baden|Baden]] and others.

empire-of-kitara.t: A semi-legendary kingdom of the Great Lakes, associated with the Chwezi dynasty and the great earthworks of Bigo in western Uganda.
empire-of-kitara.o: Oral traditions of [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Bunyoro]], [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Ankole]] and neighbouring kingdoms speak of Kitara, a vast realm ruled by the [[e:chwezi|Chwezi]], demigod kings remembered as bringers of [[e:cattle|cattle]] culture and new crafts. Archaeologists link these memories with large settlements of the 13th to 15th centuries at [[e:ntusi|Ntusi]] and [[e:bigo-bya-mugenyi|Bigo bya Mugenyi]], where kilometres of ditches enclosed cattle and dwellings.
empire-of-kitara.r: Kitara appears to have been a [[e:cattle|cattle]]-centred state, with herders and farmers living side by side and the ruler's power resting on cattle wealth and spiritual authority. The [[e:chwezi|Chwezi]] are remembered as founders of a spirit cult, kubandwa, still practised in the region. How large or centralised the state really was is uncertain.
empire-of-kitara.e: Traditions say the [[e:chwezi|Chwezi]] vanished mysteriously and were succeeded by the [[e:babiito-dynasty|Babito]], Luo-speaking newcomers from the north, who founded the [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Kingdom of Bunyoro]] around 1500. Bunyoro and the [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Kingdom of Ankole]] both claimed Kitara's heritage.

euboean-league.t: Federation of the cities of Euboea, born from the island's revolt against Athens in 411 BCE and revived repeatedly under Macedonian and Roman patrons.
euboean-league.o: [[e:euboea|Euboea]] was vital to [[s:athens|Athens]], supplying food and pasture. In 411 BCE, after a Spartan naval victory off [[s:eretria|Eretria]], its cities revolted and formed a league, building a bridge across the [[e:euripus-strait|Euripus]] to link [[s:chalcis|Chalcis]] with the mainland. Federal coins inscribed for the Euboeans appear from about this time.
euboean-league.r: The league joined [[s:chalcis|Chalcis]], [[s:eretria|Eretria]], [[e:histiaea|Histiaea]] and [[s:karystos|Carystus]] with a federal council and coinage, though the larger cities often pursued their own policies. Its history was one of shifting allegiances: members joined the [[s:second-athenian-league|Second Athenian League]], while [[e:callias-of-chalcis|Callias of Chalcis]] revived the federation in the 340s BCE in a contest between [[s:athens|Athens]] and [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] for the island.
euboean-league.e: Under the Hellenistic kings, [[s:chalcis|Chalcis]] was one of [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon's]] 'fetters of [[e:greece|Greece]]'. After [[e:titus-quinctius-flamininus|Flamininus]] proclaimed the freedom of the [[e:greeks|Greeks]] in 196 BCE the league was refounded under Roman patronage. It lost its independence after the [[e:achaean-war|Achaean War]] of 146 BCE, when [[e:chalcis|Chalcis]] was punished for supporting the [[e:achaeans-achaea|Achaeans]].

emirate-of-nekor.t: The first Islamic principality in Morocco, ruled by an Arab dynasty on the Rif coast for three centuries.
emirate-of-nekor.o: Around 710 the [[s:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad Caliphate]] granted the coastal region of the Rif to [[e:salih-ibn-mansur|Salih ibn Mansur]], an Arab of Himyarite descent who preached [[e:islam|Islam]] to the local [[e:berbers|Berber]] tribes. His descendants, the [[s:salihids|Salihids]], ruled the [[e:emirate|emirate]], and his grandson [[e:said-ibn-idris|Said ibn Idris]] built the capital [[e:nekor|Nekor]] near modern [[e:al-hoceima|Al Hoceima]].
emirate-of-nekor.r: [[e:nekor|Nekor]] was a small [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] [[e:emirate|emirate]] following the [[e:maliki-school|Maliki school]], based on farming in the Nekor valley and trade across the sea with [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]]. It suffered a [[e:vikings|Viking]] raid around 859 and the Fatimid sack of the city in 917, after which the [[s:salihids|Salihids]] returned with Andalusian help. They recognised the [[s:caliphate-of-cordoba|Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba]] as overlord in the 10th century.
emirate-of-nekor.e: By the early 11th century the [[e:emirate|emirate]] had lost its independence amid [[e:zanata-berbers|Zenata Berber]] wars, and the [[e:almoravid-empire|Almoravids]] destroyed [[e:nekor|Nekor]] in 1080. Its role as the Rif's main port passed to other towns.

eastern-kara-khanid-khanate.t: The eastern branch of the Kara-Khanid dynasty, ruling Kashgar and the Tarim cities, whose khan received Yusuf Balasaguni's Kutadgu Bilig, a classic of Turkic literature.
eastern-kara-khanid-khanate.o: Around 1042 the [[s:kara-khanid-khanate|Kara-Khanid Khanate]] split into two rival branches. The eastern khanate, under the Hasanid line descended from [[e:hasan-bughra-khan|Hasan Bughra Khan]], held [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]], [[e:balasagun|Balasagun]], the Ili valley and the western [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]], while the [[s:western-kara-khanid-khanate|Western Kara-Khanid Khanate]], ruled by the descendants of Ali ibn Musa, held [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]].
eastern-kara-khanid-khanate.r: The eastern khans ruled Turkic tribes and oasis towns, continuing the spread of [[e:islam|Islam]] in the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim Basin]] and facing the Buddhist [[s:kingdom-of-qocho|Kingdom of Qocho]] to the east. [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]] became a centre of Turkic Islamic culture: [[e:yusuf-balasaguni|Yusuf Balasaguni]] presented his mirror for princes, the [[e:kutadgu-bilig|Kutadgu Bilig]], to the [[e:kashgar|Kashgar]] khan around 1069.
eastern-kara-khanid-khanate.e: In the 1130s the [[s:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]] took [[e:balasagun|Balasagun]] and reduced the eastern khans to [[e:vassal|vassals]] ruling [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]]. The line ended around 1211, in the turmoil after [[e:kuchlug|Kuchlug]], the Naiman prince who had seized the [[e:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]] throne, took over [[e:kashgar|Kashgar]], shortly before the Mongol conquest.

emirate-of-liptako.t: A Fulbe emirate in northern Burkina Faso centred on Dori, created by jihad in 1810 and the westernmost outpost of the Sokoto Caliphate.
emirate-of-liptako.o: [[e:fula|Fulbe]] herders had settled in Liptako under the rule of [[e:gurma-people|Gurma]] chiefs. Around 1810, inspired by the [[e:jihad|jihad]] of [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]], the Fulbe rose under [[e:brahima-saydu|Brahima Saydu]], defeated the Gurma and founded an [[e:emirate|emirate]] with its capital at [[e:dori|Dori]]. Its rulers accepted the authority of the [[s:gwandu-emirate|Gwandu Emirate]], which supervised the western emirates of the [[e:caliphate|caliphate]].
emirate-of-liptako.r: Liptako was a pastoral [[e:emirate|emirate]] in the [[e:sahel|Sahel]], where [[e:fula|Fulbe]] [[e:cattle|cattle]] owners ruled over farming communities and slaves. Its [[e:emir|emirs]] governed with Muslim scholars and lineage heads, and were often weakened by succession disputes. The emirate fought [[e:gurma-people|Gurma]] and [[e:tuareg|Tuareg]] neighbours for grazing land and [[e:well|wells]]. [[e:heinrich-barth|Heinrich Barth]] passed through [[e:dori|Dori]] in 1853 and described the town.
emirate-of-liptako.e: French columns reached [[e:dori|Dori]] in the 1890s, and Liptako came under French rule in 1897. It became part of [[s:french-sudan|French Sudan]] and later of [[s:french-upper-volta|French Upper Volta]], and Dori remains the main town of the region.

epidaurus.t: Argolid city-state whose sanctuary of Asclepius became the most famous healing centre of the Greek world, with its magnificent theatre.
epidaurus.o: Epidaurus lay on a small peninsula on the east coast of the [[e:argolid|Argolid]]. In the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] Dorian settlers from [[s:argos|Argos]] made it an independent city; tradition held that Epidaurians in turn settled [[s:aegina|Aegina]]. Its sanctuary of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] Maleatas inland gradually gave way to the cult of his son [[e:asclepius|Asclepius]].
epidaurus.r: Epidaurus was governed by an oligarchy of 180 citizens. From the late 5th century BCE the [[e:sanctuary-of-asclepius-at-epidaurus|Asclepieion]] attracted sick pilgrims who slept in the sanctuary hoping for healing dreams, and inscriptions record their cures. The 4th century BCE [[e:theatre|theatre]], attributed to [[e:polykleitos-the-younger|Polykleitos the Younger]], seats about 13,000. Epidaurus was a loyal member of the [[s:peloponnesian-league|Peloponnesian League]].
epidaurus.e: Epidaurus joined the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]] in 243 BCE and passed under [[e:rome|Rome]] in 146 BCE. [[e:sulla|Sulla]] plundered the sanctuary in 87 BCE, but it recovered and flourished in Roman times; its [[e:theatre|theatre]] still hosts performances.

eshrefids.t: A short-lived beylik on Lake Beysehir whose wooden-columned Eshrefoglu Mosque is a World Heritage Site.
eshrefids.o: The Eshrefids descended from Eshref, a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] commander serving the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]]. In the 1280s [[e:sayf-al-din-suleyman-bey|Sayf al-Din Suleyman Bey]] made [[e:beysehir|Beysehir]] on the lake of the same name the centre of a principality as Seljuk power waned.
eshrefids.r: The [[e:beylik|beylik]] held [[e:beysehir|Beysehir]], [[e:seydisehir|Seydisehir]] and [[e:aksehir|Aksehir]] at times. [[e:sayf-al-din-suleyman-bey|Suleyman Bey]] built the [[e:esrefoglu-mosque|Eshrefoglu Mosque]] in 1296-1299, whose interior has a forest of carved cedar columns and painted wooden ceilings, among the finest surviving wooden mosques; it was listed with other Anatolian wooden mosques as a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]] in 2023. The beylik had little political weight among its neighbours.
eshrefids.e: In 1326 the Ilkhanid governor of [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], [[e:timurtash-chupanid|Timurtash]], executed its last ruler, [[e:suleyman-ii-of-eshref|Suleyman II]], and the lands passed to the [[s:hamidids|Hamidids]].

east-africa-protectorate.t: The British protectorate that became Kenya, defined by the Uganda Railway and the arrival of European settlers in the highlands.
east-africa-protectorate.o: In 1895 the British government took over the territory between the coast and the [[e:east-african-rift|Rift Valley]] from the [[s:imperial-british-east-africa-company|Imperial British East Africa Company]]. The ten-mile coastal strip remained nominally part of the [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Sultanate of Zanzibar]]. The administration was based at [[s:mombasa|Mombasa]] until 1905, when the capital moved to Nairobi, a railway depot.
east-africa-protectorate.r: The [[e:uganda-railway|Uganda Railway]], built from 1896 to 1901 largely by Indian indentured workers, opened the interior. Commissioner [[e:charles-eliot-diplomat|Charles Eliot]] encouraged white settlement in the fertile highlands, which were reserved for Europeans, while [[e:maasai-people|Maasai]] and [[e:kikuyu-people|Kikuyu]] lost land and Africans were taxed and pressed into labour. Military expeditions subdued resisting peoples such as the Nandi.
east-africa-protectorate.e: In 1920 the interior was annexed as [[s:kenya-colony|Kenya Colony]] and the coastal strip became the Kenya [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]]. The settler-dominated order set up in these years shaped Kenyan politics up to the [[e:mau-mau-rebellion|Mau Mau uprising]] and independence.

electorate-of-saxony.t: The Wettin electorate on the Elbe that cradled the Lutheran Reformation and, under Augustus the Strong, made Dresden a Baroque capital.
electorate-of-saxony.o: The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] made the Ascanian dukes of the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg|Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg]] prince-[[e:prince-elector|electors]]. When their line ended in 1422, [[e:sigismund-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Sigismund]] granted the electorate to [[e:frederick-i-elector-of-saxony|Frederick the Warlike]], Margrave of [[e:meissen|Meissen]], joining it to the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettin]] lands of Meissen and [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]]. In 1485 the brothers Ernest and Albert divided these lands, and the electoral dignity went to the Ernestine line.
electorate-of-saxony.r: [[e:silver|Silver]] mining in the [[e:ore-mountains|Erzgebirge]] made [[e:saxony|Saxony]] rich. Elector [[e:frederick-iii-elector-of-saxony|Frederick the Wise]] founded [[e:university-of-wittenberg|Wittenberg University]] and protected [[e:martin-luther|Martin Luther]], and Saxony became the leading Lutheran state. After the [[e:schmalkaldic-war|Schmalkaldic War]] of 1547 the electorate passed to the Albertine [[e:maurice-elector-of-saxony|Maurice]], with [[e:dresden|Dresden]] as capital. [[e:augustus-ii-the-strong|Augustus the Strong]], king of [[e:poland|Poland]] from 1697, built the [[e:zwinger-dresden|Zwinger]] and founded the [[e:meissen|Meissen]] [[e:porcelain|porcelain]] works.
electorate-of-saxony.e: [[e:saxony|Saxony]] was badly weakened by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in the [[e:seven-years-war|Seven Years' War]]. Allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], Elector Frederick [[e:augustus-iii|Augustus III]] took the title of king in 1806, turning the electorate into the [[s:kingdom-of-saxony|Kingdom of Saxony]], which lost much of its territory to Prussia in 1815.

emirate-of-tagant.t: The emirate of the Idaw Aish in central Mauritania, ruled from Tijikja, where French colonial expansion met fierce resistance in 1905.
emirate-of-tagant.o: The Idaw Aish, a group of [[e:berbers|Berber]] origin that adopted the warrior way of life of the Hassani, rose to dominance in the Tagant plateau of central [[e:mauritania|Mauritania]] in the 18th century. By around 1760 their chiefs ruled as [[e:emir|emirs]], with [[e:tijikja|Tijikja]] as a main centre.
emirate-of-tagant.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled over warrior lineages, scholarly tribes, tributaries and enslaved oasis cultivators, taxing date palms, herds and caravans. Tagant was frequently torn by feuds between rival branches of the ruling family and wars with the [[s:emirate-of-brakna|Emirate of Brakna]] and other neighbours. Emir [[e:bakar-ould-soueid-ahmed|Bakkar ould Swayd Ahmad]], whose reign spanned much of the 19th century, was its most famous ruler.
emirate-of-tagant.e: [[e:france|France's]] [[e:xavier-coppolani|Xavier Coppolani]] occupied [[e:tijikja|Tijikja]] in 1905 and was assassinated there the same year. [[e:bakar-ould-soueid-ahmed|Bakkar]], then very old, was killed fighting the French in 1905, and Tagant was absorbed into [[s:french-mauritania|French Mauritania]].

east-jersey.t: The northern half of colonial New Jersey, owned by Carteret's heirs and later by a board of Scottish and Quaker proprietors, with its capital at Perth Amboy.
east-jersey.o: When [[e:john-berkeley-1st-baron-berkeley-of-stratton|Lord Berkeley]] sold his share of [[e:new-jersey|New Jersey]] in 1674, [[e:george-carteret|Sir George Carteret]] kept the eastern part, and the [[e:quintipartite-deed|Quintipartite Deed]] of 1676 fixed the line dividing East [[s:bailiwick-of-jersey|Jersey]] from [[s:west-jersey|West Jersey]]. After Carteret's death his heirs sold the colony in 1682 to 24 proprietors, many of them [[e:quakers|Quakers]] and Scots, including [[e:william-penn|William Penn]] and [[e:robert-barclay|Robert Barclay]].
east-jersey.r: Governor [[e:philip-carteret|Philip Carteret]], a cousin of the founder, ruled from [[e:elizabeth-new-jersey|Elizabethtown]] through the 1670s, and frequently clashed with the [[s:province-of-new-york|Province of New York]] over customs and authority. The Scottish proprietors founded [[e:perth-amboy|Perth Amboy]] as their capital, and [[e:robert-barclay|Barclay]] served as absentee governor from 1682 to 1688. Settlers from [[e:new-england|New England]], [[e:scotland|Scotland]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] farmed and resisted quitrents. In 1688 the colony was added to the [[s:dominion-of-new-england|Dominion of New England]].
east-jersey.e: Disorder over land titles led the proprietors to surrender government to the Crown in 1702, when East and [[s:west-jersey|West Jersey]] were reunited as the royal [[s:province-of-new-jersey|Province of New Jersey]]. The [[e:board-of-proprietors-of-east-jersey|Board of Proprietors of East Jersey]] kept its land rights for centuries.

emishi.t: The peoples of northern Honshu who resisted the Japanese court for two centuries until defeated in the wars of the late 8th and early 9th centuries.
emishi.o: Emishi was the court's term for the inhabitants of the northeast, beyond the frontier of the [[s:yamato|Yamato]] state, in the regions later called [[e:mutsu-province|Mutsu]] and Dewa. They were not a single nation but many communities; whether they were related to the [[e:ainu|Ainu]], or were Japanese speakers who simply lived outside the state, is still debated.
emishi.r: The Emishi lived by hunting, fishing, farming and [[e:horse-breeding|horse breeding]], and were famed as [[e:mounted-archer|mounted archers]]. Local chiefs led bands rather than a central government. The court built fortresses such as [[e:taga-castle|Taga-jo]] and [[e:isawa-castle|Isawa]] and settled colonists, while some Emishi accepted court titles and others raided frontier posts.
emishi.e: During the Thirty-Eight Years' War of 774 to 811, the leader Aterui surrendered to [[e:sakanoue-no-tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] in 802 and was executed. The campaigns ended in 811, and many Emishi were resettled across [[e:japan|Japan]], while their northern descendants later supported the [[e:abe-clan-of-mutsu|Abe]] and [[s:northern-fujiwara|Northern Fujiwara]].

espana-boba.t: The period of restored but neglectful Spanish rule over Santo Domingo, nicknamed 'Foolish Spain', which ended with a brief declaration of independence.
espana-boba.o: Dominican [[e:criollo-people|creoles]] led by [[e:juan-sanchez-ramirez|Juan Sánchez Ramírez]] expelled the French from [[e:santo-domingo|Santo Domingo]] in 1809, with British help, and voluntarily returned the colony to [[e:spain|Spain]]. Spain itself was then fighting [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], and the restored colony received little money, troops or attention.
espana-boba.r: [[e:juan-sanchez-ramirez|Sánchez Ramírez]] governed until his death in 1811, followed by captains general such as [[e:carlos-de-urrutia|Carlos de Urrutia]], mocked as 'Carlos Conuco' for making soldiers farm, and [[e:sebastian-kindelan|Sebastián Kindelán]]. The economy, already ruined by war and emigration, depended on [[e:cattle|cattle]], tobacco and mahogany, and [[e:paper-money|paper money]] lost value. Conspiracies included the so-called Italian plot of 1810 and a slave revolt plan of 1812, both harshly suppressed. [[e:spain|Spain's]] liberal constitution of 1812 was briefly applied.
espana-boba.e: Disillusioned with [[e:spain|Spain]], the lawyer [[e:jose-nunez-de-caceres|José Núñez de Cáceres]] proclaimed independence on 1 December 1821 as the [[s:republic-of-spanish-haiti|Republic of Spanish Haiti]]. The colony's weakness made the Haitian occupation of 1822 easy.

earldom-of-lade.t: Dynasty of earls based near Trondheim who rivalled the descendants of Harald Fairhair and ruled Norway for long periods around 1000.
earldom-of-lade.o: The earls took their name from [[e:lade-trondheim|Lade]], a farm near modern [[e:trondheim|Trondheim]] in Trøndelag. [[e:hakon-grjotgardsson|Håkon Grjotgardsson]], whose family came from [[s:halogaland|Hålogaland]], allied with [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] in the late 9th century and was made earl of the Trøndelag region, founding a powerful line.
earldom-of-lade.r: The jarls of [[e:lade-trondheim|Lade]] drew strength from the rich farming districts and assemblies of Trøndelag and from the northern [[e:fur-trade|fur trade]]. [[e:hakon-sigurdsson|Håkon Sigurdsson]], known as Haakon Jarl, ruled most of [[e:norway|Norway]] from about 975 to 995 under the overlordship of [[e:harald-bluetooth|Harald Bluetooth]] of [[e:denmark|Denmark]] and was a champion of the pagan cults. After the [[e:battle-of-svolder|Battle of Svolder]] in 1000, his sons Eric and [[e:sweyn-haakonsson|Sweyn]] governed Norway for the kings of Denmark and [[e:sweden|Sweden]].
earldom-of-lade.e: [[e:olaf-ii-of-norway|Olaf Haraldsson]] drove out the earls in 1015. [[e:cnut-the-great|Cnut the Great]] restored [[e:hakon-eiriksson|Håkon Eiriksson]] as his regent in [[e:norway|Norway]] in 1028, but Håkon drowned around 1030 and the line ended. Trøndelag passed fully to the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]], and [[e:trondheim|Trondheim]] (Nidaros) became its religious centre.

emirate-of-derbent.t: An Arab frontier emirate at the great Caspian gate of Derbent, guarding Islam's northern border against the Khazars and mountain peoples.
emirate-of-derbent.o: [[e:derbent|Derbent]], called Bab al-Abwab, the Gate of Gates, by the [[e:arabs|Arabs]], had been fortified by the [[e:sasanian-empire|Sasanians]] with walls running from the Caspian into the mountains. In 869, as [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid]] authority faded, the local Arab governor [[e:hashim-ibn-suraqa|Hashim ibn Suraqa]] founded a hereditary dynasty, the [[e:hashimids-of-derbent|Hashimids]].
emirate-of-derbent.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] was a frontier city-state that drew warriors for holy war against the [[s:khazar-khaganate|Khazar Khaganate]] and the peoples of the mountains, and grew rich on Caspian and caravan trade in slaves, [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and textiles. [[e:emir|Emirs]] shared power with an assembly of leading citizens and often fought or allied with the [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvanshah State]], which at times ruled the city.
emirate-of-derbent.e: Weakened by quarrels between [[e:emir|emirs]] and townsmen and by raids from the mountains, the [[e:emirate|emirate]] was taken by the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]] in 1075. The city later passed among regional powers, keeping its walls as the gateway to the [[e:north-caucasus|North Caucasus]].

emirate-of-abdelkader.t: The Algerian state built by Emir Abdelkader to resist French conquest, a symbol of national resistance in modern Algeria.
emirate-of-abdelkader.o: After [[e:france|France]] conquered [[e:algiers|Algiers]] and the [[s:beylik-of-the-west|Beylik of the West]] collapsed, the tribes of western [[e:algeria|Algeria]] chose the young [[e:sufism|Sufi]] scholar [[e:emir-abdelkader|Abdelkader]] as their emir near [[e:mascara-algeria|Mascara]] in 1832. He fought the French and won recognition in the [[e:treaty-of-desmichels|Treaty of Desmichels]] of 1834 and the [[e:treaty-of-tafna|Treaty of Tafna]] of 1837.
emirate-of-abdelkader.r: [[e:emir-abdelkader|Abdelkader]] built a state with provincial governors, Islamic courts, regular taxes, a standing army and arsenals, moving his capital to [[e:tagdemt|Tagdemt]]. At its height in the late 1830s, his authority covered most of western and central [[e:algeria|Algeria]]. He drew legitimacy from [[e:islam|Islam]] and from resistance to the invaders.
emirate-of-abdelkader.e: War resumed in 1839, and [[e:thomas-robert-bugeaud|Bugeaud]]'s scorched-earth campaigns destroyed [[e:emir-abdelkader|Abdelkader]]'s towns; his mobile camp was captured in 1843. [[e:morocco|Morocco's]] defeat at [[e:battle-of-isly|Isly]] in 1844 cost him support, and he surrendered in 1847. Exiled to [[e:damascus|Damascus]], he protected Christians during the 1860 massacres.

esuvii.t: Little-known Gallic people of lower Normandy subdued by Caesar's legate Crassus during the conquest of Armorica.
esuvii.o: Caesar mentions the Esuvii among the Armorican peoples brought under Roman control by [[e:publius-licinius-crassus|Publius Crassus]] in 57 BCE, and notes that a legion wintered in their territory in 54 BCE. Their exact location is debated, but most scholars place them in the [[e:orne-river|Orne]] region around [[e:sees|Sées]] or [[e:exmes|Exmes]].
esuvii.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or institutions; their name may be linked to the Gallic god [[e:esus|Esus]].
esuvii.e: After the conquest they disappear from the record, and their land seems to have been absorbed into the civitas of the Sagii, whose town became [[e:sees|Sées]].

eastern-jin.t: The Jin dynasty in exile at Jiankang, where northern aristocrats preserved Chinese court culture and turned back the Former Qin at the Fei River in 383.
eastern-jin.o: As the [[s:western-jin|Western Jin]] collapsed in the north, [[e:emperor-yuan-of-jin|Sima Rui]], a Jin prince stationed at [[e:jiankang|Jianye]] (renamed Jiankang, modern [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]]), was proclaimed emperor in 318 with the support of the Wang family led by [[e:wang-dao|Wang Dao]]. Hundreds of thousands of northern refugees followed, settling in the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] region.
eastern-jin.r: The emperors were often weak, and power lay with great families such as the Wang, Xie and Huan, who fought for control of armies and the court. [[e:huan-wen|Huan Wen]] took [[s:cheng-han|Cheng Han]] in 347, and [[e:xie-an|Xie An]] and [[e:xie-xuan|Xie Xuan]] defeated [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]] at the [[e:battle-of-fei-river|Fei River]] in 383. The era produced the calligrapher [[e:wang-xizhi|Wang Xizhi]], the painter [[e:gu-kaizhi|Gu Kaizhi]], the poet [[e:tao-yuanming|Tao Yuanming]] and the spread of [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] in the south.
eastern-jin.e: Revolts by [[e:sun-en|Sun En]] and the usurpation of [[e:huan-xuan|Huan Xuan]], who briefly founded [[s:huan-chu|Huan Chu]], weakened the throne. The general [[e:emperor-wu-of-liu-song|Liu Yu]] restored it, conquered [[s:southern-yan|Southern Yan]] and [[s:later-qin|Later Qin]], then deposed the last Jin emperor in 420 and founded the [[s:liu-song|Liu Song]].

early-ly-dynasty.t: The first native Vietnamese dynasty to break from Chinese rule, founded by Ly Bi, who declared himself emperor of Van Xuan in 544.
early-ly-dynasty.o: In 541 [[e:ly-nam-de|Ly Bi]], a local landowner of mixed Chinese and Vietnamese descent, led a revolt against the [[s:liang-dynasty|Liang dynasty]]'s governor of [[e:jiao-province|Jiaozhou]]. By 544 he had driven out [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]] officials and proclaimed himself Ly Nam De, emperor of the south, naming the state Van Xuan, 'ten thousand springs'.
early-ly-dynasty.r: [[e:ly-nam-de|Ly Nam De]] set up a court on Chinese lines, with an era name and officials, and built the [[e:tran-quoc-pagoda|Khai Quoc]] pagoda near [[e:long-bien|Long Bien]]. [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]] forces under [[e:emperor-wu-of-chen|Chen Baxian]] defeated him in 545, but resistance continued under [[e:trieu-quang-phuc|Trieu Quang Phuc]] and later [[e:ly-phat-tu|Ly Phat Tu]], who held the delta for decades through a mix of [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] warfare and negotiation.
early-ly-dynasty.e: In 602 the [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui dynasty]] sent an army under [[e:liu-fang|Liu Fang]], and [[e:ly-phat-tu|Ly Phat Tu]] surrendered, returning the region to Chinese control. [[e:ly-nam-de|Ly Bi]]'s revolt is celebrated in [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] as an early assertion of independence, and Van Xuan was the first name for the country chosen by its own rulers.

ek-balam.t: A walled Maya city in north-eastern Yucatán whose acropolis held the superb stucco tomb of its king Ukit Kan Le'k Tok'.
ek-balam.o: Ek' Balam, anciently Talol, was settled from the Preclassic period. It became the capital of a kingdom in the 8th century and reached its height after the ruler [[e:ukit-kan-lek-tok|Ukit Kan Le'k Tok']] arrived and took power in 770.
ek-balam.r: The city is enclosed by stone walls, with causeways leading out from gateways. Its great Acropolis contains the tomb of [[e:ukit-kan-lek-tok|Ukit Kan Le'k Tok']], who died around 801, with a doorway modelled as a monster's jaws and winged stucco figures. Painted capstones and murals carry many hieroglyphic texts, making Ek' Balam an important source on northern Maya kingship.
ek-balam.e: Royal activity at Ek' Balam faded after about 850, and the region came under the influence of [[s:chichen-itza|Chichen Itza]]. The stucco facade was uncovered in the late 1990s.
