emirate-of-nejd-and-hasa.t: The third Saudi state in its first phase, begun when Ibn Saud recaptured Riyadh in 1902, which defeated the Rashidis and took al-Hasa.
emirate-of-nejd-and-hasa.o: In January 1902 the young [[e:ibn-saud|Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud]], living in exile in the [[s:sheikhdom-of-kuwait|Sheikhdom of Kuwait]], captured [[e:riyadh|Riyadh's]] [[e:masmak-fort|Masmak fort]] from the Rashidi governor with a small band of followers. He gradually reclaimed southern [[e:najd|Najd]] from the [[s:emirate-of-jabal-shammar|Emirate of Jabal Shammar]], defeating its emir at [[e:battle-of-rawdat-muhanna|Rawdat Muhanna]] in 1906.
emirate-of-nejd-and-hasa.r: [[e:ibn-saud|Ibn Saud]] combined tribal diplomacy, marriage alliances and the Wahhabi religious establishment. From about 1912 he settled [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] in agricultural communities called hijras, creating the Ikhwan, a militant religious force. In 1913 he took [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Hasa]] from the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], gaining the [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]] coast. The [[e:treaty-of-darin|Treaty of Darin]] in 1915 made him a British protégé with a subsidy.
emirate-of-nejd-and-hasa.e: In 1921 [[e:ibn-saud|Ibn Saud]] conquered Ha'il, ending the Rashidi state, and took the title [[e:sultan|Sultan]] of [[e:najd|Nejd]] and its Dependencies, beginning the [[s:sultanate-of-nejd|Sultanate of Nejd]].

ellipi.t: A kingdom of the central Zagros, an Assyrian ally and vassal until a disputed succession drew in Sargon II and Sennacherib.
ellipi.o: Ellipi lay in the central [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]], in the [[e:kermanshah|Kermanshah]] and northern Luristan region of western [[e:iran|Iran]], between Media to the north and [[e:elam|Elam]] to the south. It appears in Assyrian sources from the 9th century BCE as a kingdom with fortified towns, its royal seat at Marubishtu.
ellipi.r: Ellipi's kings controlled valuable [[e:horse-breeding|horse-breeding]] lands and routes from [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]] to the plateau. Its best-known king, [[e:dalta|Dalta]], was a loyal [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]]. When Dalta died in 708 BCE, his sons Nibe and [[e:ishpabara|Ishpabara]] fought for the throne; Nibe called on [[e:elam|Elam]] and Ishpabara on [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]], which sent troops to install him. Some scholars associate the region with the Luristan bronzes, though this is debated.
ellipi.e: [[e:ishpabara|Ishpabara]] later turned against [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]], and in 702 BCE [[e:sennacherib|Sennacherib]] sacked Marubishtu and annexed part of Ellipi. The rest of the kingdom fades from the record by the early 7th century BCE, absorbed into the Median sphere.

eretnids.t: The successor state to Mongol rule in central Anatolia, founded by an Uyghur officer who made himself sultan in Sivas and Kayseri.
eretnids.o: [[e:eretna|Eretna]] was an [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] commander who served the Ilkhanid governor of [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], [[e:timurtash-chupanid|Timurtash]]. After the death of the last strong [[e:ilkhan|Ilkhan]], [[e:abu-said-bahadur-khan|Abu Sa'id]], in 1335, he governed central Anatolia on his own account, first in the name of rival Mongol princes and from 1341 as sultan, minting coins in his own name.
eretnids.r: In 1343 [[e:eretna|Eretna]] defeated a Chobanid army at [[e:battle-of-karanbuk|Karanbuk]], securing his state. His realm included [[e:sivas|Sivas]], [[e:kayseri|Kayseri]], [[e:tokat|Tokat]], [[e:amasya|Amasya]] and [[e:erzincan|Erzincan]], with a Mongol and [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] military elite and Persian administration in the Seljuk tradition. After his death in 1352 his son Mehmed and grandson [[e:ala-al-din-ali|Ala al-Din Ali]] faced revolts by [[e:emir|emirs]] and Turkmen chiefs.
eretnids.e: Real power passed to the [[e:vizier|vizier]] and judge [[e:kadi-burhan-al-din|Kadi Burhan al-Din]], who after [[e:ala-al-din-ali|Ala al-Din Ali's]] death in 1380 took the throne in 1381, ending the dynasty.

electorate-of-wurttemberg.t: Württemberg's brief rank as an electorate between the duchy and the kingdom, a step in Frederick I's rise under Napoleon.
electorate-of-wurttemberg.o: Duke [[e:frederick-i-of-wurttemberg|Frederick II of Württemberg]] lost his lands at [[s:county-of-montbeliard|Montbéliard]] to [[e:france|France]] but gained secularised church lands and imperial cities in the [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Imperial Recess of 1803]]. As part of the same settlement he was made an elector of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
electorate-of-wurttemberg.r: Frederick used his new rank to centralise power, overriding the traditional estates, which had long limited the dukes. He added former imperial cities such as [[s:free-imperial-city-of-heilbronn|Heilbronn]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-reutlingen|Reutlingen]] and Catholic lands like [[e:ellwangen|Ellwangen]], which made the Protestant state more mixed in religion. He allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] in 1805 and sent troops to the [[e:battle-of-austerlitz|Austerlitz]] campaign.
electorate-of-wurttemberg.e: The [[e:peace-of-pressburg-1805|Peace of Pressburg]] rewarded Frederick with further territory and recognition as a sovereign king. On 1 January 1806 he proclaimed himself King of Württemberg, and the electorate gave way to the [[s:kingdom-of-wurttemberg|Kingdom of Württemberg]].

ebla.t: Ebla, a Bronze Age kingdom in northern Syria whose palace archive of thousands of clay tablets revealed an early Semitic state rivalling Mari and Mesopotamia.
ebla.o: Ebla grew from a settlement at Tell Mardikh, south-west of modern [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]], into a walled city by the middle of the 3rd millennium BCE. By c. 2400 BCE it controlled a large territory of farming villages and pasture in western [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and dealt as an equal with [[s:mari|Mari]], [[s:nagar|Nagar]] and distant powers along the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]].
ebla.r: Its kings governed with a council of elders and powerful officials such as the [[e:vizier|vizier]] [[e:ibrium|Ibrium]], recorded in the archive of Palace G, found by Italian excavators under [[e:paolo-matthiae|Paolo Matthiae]] in 1974 and 1975. The tablets, in Sumerian [[e:cuneiform|cuneiform]] and the Semitic Eblaite language, record textiles, metals, flocks of sheep, treaties and offerings to gods such as [[e:kura-god|Kura]] and [[e:hadad|Hadda]].
ebla.e: Palace G burned c. 2300 BCE, probably at the hands of [[e:sargon-of-akkad|Sargon]] or [[e:naram-sin|Naram-Sin]] of the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]]. Ebla revived twice, the last time as an Amorite city allied to [[s:yamhad|Yamhad]], until a Hittite king destroyed it c. 1600 BCE. Its archive remains one of the oldest bodies of written Semitic texts.

esan-chiefdoms.t: A cluster of small Edo-speaking kingdoms north-east of Benin City, each ruled by an Onojie under the influence of the Benin Empire.
esan-chiefdoms.o: Esan tradition links the founding of most chiefdoms to the 15th century, when people left [[e:benin-city|Benin City]] during the reign of [[e:oba-dynasty|Oba]] [[e:ewuare-the-great|Ewuare]] and settled in the forest to the north-east. Princes and nobles from [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] became [[e:onojie|Enijie]] (singular Onojie), founding chiefdoms such as [[e:uromi|Uromi]], [[e:ekpoma|Ekpoma]], [[e:irrua|Irrua]] and [[e:ubiaja|Ubiaja]].
esan-chiefdoms.r: Each chiefdom had its own [[e:onojie|Onojie]], chiefs and age grades, and ruled villages of yam and palm farmers. The Enijie owed allegiance to the [[e:oba-dynasty|Oba of Benin]], sent tribute and took part in [[e:benin-empire|Benin's]] wars, but fought one another frequently. Esan shared much of Edo religion and court culture.
esan-chiefdoms.e: After the British conquest of [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] in 1897, the Esan chiefdoms were occupied; [[e:uromi|Uromi]] under [[e:onojie|Onojie]] Okolo resisted until 1901. They became part of [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Southern Nigeria]], and the Enijie remain traditional rulers in [[e:edo-state|Edo State]].

emirate-of-erzincan.t: The principality of Mutahharten, lord of Erzincan, an ally of Timur on the upper Euphrates.
emirate-of-erzincan.o: [[e:mutahharten|Mutahharten]] was a governor of [[e:erzincan|Erzincan]] under the [[s:eretnids|Eretnids]]. As that dynasty collapsed in the late 1370s, he made the city and its fertile plain an independent [[e:emirate|emirate]], competing with [[e:kadi-burhan-al-din|Kadi Burhan al-Din]] of [[e:sivas|Sivas]].
emirate-of-erzincan.r: [[e:mutahharten|Mutahharten]] ruled a mixed population of Turks, [[e:armenians|Armenians]] and [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and kept close ties with the [[s:empire-of-trebizond|Empire of Trebizond]]. Threatened by [[e:kadi-burhan-al-din|Kadi Burhan al-Din]] and by [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]], he accepted [[e:timur|Timur's]] overlordship and helped provoke the conflict between Timur and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. The Castilian envoy [[e:ruy-gonzalez-de-clavijo|Ruy Gonzalez de Clavijo]] passed through [[e:erzincan|Erzincan]] in 1404 on his way to [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]].
emirate-of-erzincan.e: [[e:mutahharten|Mutahharten]] died around 1403. His successors could not hold out, and the [[s:qara-qoyunlu|Qara Qoyunlu]] took [[e:erzincan|Erzincan]] in 1410.

emirate-of-jabal-shammar.t: The Rashidi emirate of Ha'il, which overthrew the second Saudi state and dominated northern Arabia before losing to Ibn Saud.
emirate-of-jabal-shammar.o: In 1836 [[e:abdullah-ibn-rashid|Abdullah ibn Rashid]] took control of Ha'il, the main town of the Jabal Shammar mountains, with the backing of the Saudi ruler [[e:faisal-ibn-turki-al-saud|Faisal ibn Turki]]. His family, leaders of the Shammar tribal confederation, at first ruled as allies of the [[s:emirate-of-nejd|Emirate of Nejd]].
emirate-of-jabal-shammar.r: Ha'il prospered on the pilgrim route from [[e:iraq|Iraq]] and [[e:persia|Persia]] to [[e:mecca|Mecca]] and on the [[e:camel|camel]] and horse trade. [[e:talal-ibn-rashid|Talal ibn Rashid]] encouraged merchants and building. [[e:muhammad-ibn-rashid|Muhammad ibn Rashid]], emir from 1869 to 1897, intervened in the Saudi civil war, took [[e:riyadh|Riyadh]] in 1887 and won at [[e:battle-of-mulayda|Mulayda]] in 1891, becoming master of central [[e:arabia|Arabia]]. The [[e:rashidi-dynasty|Rashidis]] allied with the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]].
emirate-of-jabal-shammar.e: [[e:ibn-saud|Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud]] recaptured [[e:riyadh|Riyadh]] in 1902 and the [[s:emirate-of-nejd-and-hasa|Emirate of Nejd and Hasa]] steadily pushed back the [[e:rashidi-dynasty|Rashidis]], killing [[e:abd-al-aziz-ibn-mutib-al-rashid|Abd al-Aziz ibn Mutib]] in 1906. Weakened by assassinations and the Ottoman defeat, Ha'il surrendered to Ibn Saud in 1921 and joined the [[s:sultanate-of-nejd|Sultanate of Nejd]].

emporion.t: The Greek trading city of Empúries in Catalonia, founded from Massalia, where the Romans first landed in Iberia in 218 BCE.
emporion.o: Around 575 BCE [[e:phocaea|Phocaean Greeks]] from [[s:massalia|Massalia]] (Marseille) set up a trading post on a small island at the mouth of the [[e:fluvia|Fluvià]], now [[e:sant-marti-dempuries|Sant Martí d'Empúries]]. Its name means 'market'. A larger new town, the [[s:neapolis|Neapolis]], soon grew on the mainland shore beside a native settlement of the [[s:indigetes|Indigetes]].
emporion.r: Emporion was a self-governing Greek polis trading wine, oil and fine pottery for grain, metals and textiles from the Iberian interior. It coexisted closely with its Indigetan neighbours, and from the 5th century BCE minted [[e:silver|silver]] drachms, later with a Pegasus design that Iberian mints copied. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] notes a temple of [[e:artemis-of-ephesus|Ephesian Artemis]], and a famous statue of [[e:asclepius|Asclepius]] was found in its sanctuary.
emporion.e: Allied with [[e:rome|Rome]], Emporion was the landing point of [[e:gnaeus-cornelius-scipio-calvus|Gnaeus Scipio]] in 218 BCE and of [[e:cato-the-elder|Cato]] in 195 BCE, when he crushed the revolt of the north-east. A Roman town grew beside it, and under Augustus the two merged as the municipium of Emporiae.

eldiguzids.t: A Turkic dynasty of atabegs who, from Nakhchivan and Tabriz, controlled the late Seljuk sultans and dominated north-western Iran and Arran.
eldiguzids.o: [[e:shams-al-din-eldiguz|Shams al-Din Eldiguz]], a former [[e:kipchaks|Kipchak]] slave, rose in the service of the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]] and around 1136 was made governor of [[s:caucasian-albania|Arran]] and atabeg, or guardian, of the prince [[e:arslan-shah-ibn-toghrul|Arslan Shah]]. After placing Arslan Shah on the throne of the [[s:seljuk-sultanate-of-iraq|Seljuk Sultanate of Iraq]] in 1160, he became the real power behind it.
eldiguzids.r: The atabegs ruled [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]], [[s:caucasian-albania|Arran]] and much of western [[e:iran|Iran]] from [[e:nakhchivan|Nakhchivan]], [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] and [[e:hamadan|Hamadan]], making and unmaking sultans. [[e:jahan-pahlavan|Jahan Pahlavan]] and [[e:qizil-arslan|Qizil Arslan]] continued their father's dominance. Their court patronised Persian poetry, including [[e:nizami-ganjavi|Nizami Ganjavi]], and the architect Ajami Nakhchivani built the Momine Khatun mausoleum in Nakhchivan in 1186.
eldiguzids.e: The [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] defeated the atabeg [[e:nusrat-al-din-abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] at [[e:battle-of-shamkor|Shamkor]] in 1195, and Mongol raids further weakened [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]], the last ruler. In 1225 [[e:jalal-al-din-mangburni|Jalal al-Din]] of the [[s:khwarazmian-empire|Khwarazmian Empire]] took [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]], ending the dynasty.

elusates.t: Aquitanian people of the Armagnac whose town Elusa, modern Eauze, became a provincial capital of late Roman Gaul.
elusates.o: The Elusates lived in the north-west of the modern [[e:gers|Gers]], in the [[s:county-of-armagnac|Armagnac]] hills. Caesar names them among the Aquitanian peoples who surrendered to [[e:publius-licinius-crassus|Publius Crassus]] in 56 BCE.
elusates.r: Nothing is known of their pre-Roman government. They belonged to the [[e:aquitani|Aquitani]], whose language was related to Basque.
elusates.e: Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:elusa|Elusa]] grew into a prosperous town, and in the late 3rd century it became the capital of the province of [[e:novempopulania|Novempopulana]]. The [[e:eauze|Eauze]] treasure, a hoard of nearly 28,000 coins and jewellery buried in the 3rd century, shows its wealth.

empire-of-china-1915-1916.t: Yuan Shikai's attempt to make himself emperor of China, which lasted only 83 days and plunged the country into the warlord era.
empire-of-china-1915-1916.o: [[e:yuan-shikai|Yuan Shikai]], president of the [[s:republic-of-china|Republic of China]], had dissolved parliament and concentrated power. Encouraged by supporters who argued that [[e:china|China]] needed a monarchy, and after staged petitions from provincial assemblies, he accepted the throne in December 1915 and adopted the reign title Hongxian from 1 January 1916.
empire-of-china-1915-1916.r: The monarchy changed little in practice, as government continued through the existing ministries of the [[s:beiyang-government|Beiyang government]]. It was deeply unpopular: Yuan's acceptance of most of [[e:japan|Japan's]] Twenty-One Demands in 1915 had already damaged him, and Japan and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] disapproved of the restoration.
empire-of-china-1915-1916.e: In December 1915 Cai E and [[s:later-tang|Tang]] Jiyao rose in [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]] in the National Protection War, and other southern provinces declared independence. Losing the support of his own generals, Yuan abandoned the monarchy on 22 March 1916 and died in June, leaving the warlords to divide [[e:china|China]].

elea.t: Greek city on the Cilento coast founded by refugees from Phocaea, home of the philosophers Parmenides and Zeno and of the Eleatic school.
elea.o: Around 540 BCE [[e:phocaea|Phocaean Greeks]], who had fled their city in [[e:asia-minor|Asia Minor]] before the [[e:persians|Persians]] and then lost much of their fleet at the battle of [[e:alalia|Alalia]] off [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]], founded Elea (later Roman Velia) on a headland south of [[s:poseidonia|Poseidonia]] with help from [[s:rhegion|Rhegion]].
elea.r: Elea lived by the sea: fishing, trade and shipping rather than farming, as its hilly territory was poor. It is best known for philosophy: [[e:parmenides|Parmenides]], said to have written the city's laws, and his pupil [[e:zeno-of-elea|Zeno]] founded the Eleatic school, which shaped Greek thinking about being and change. The [[e:porta-rosa|Porta Rosa]], a 4th-century BCE arched gateway, is an early true arch in a Greek city. Elea resisted Lucanian pressure while other Greek cities fell.
elea.e: Elea allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] in the early 3rd century BCE and supplied ships in the [[e:punic-wars|Punic Wars]]; Rome recruited priestesses of [[e:ceres|Ceres]] from Velia. It kept Greek speech and became a Roman municipium after 89 BCE. Silting of its harbour led to decline, and its remains are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

emirate-of-sicily.t: Muslim Sicily, ruled from Palermo for over two centuries, which transformed the island's farming, cities and language before the Norman conquest.
emirate-of-sicily.o: In 827 the [[e:aghlabid-dynasty|Aghlabids of Ifriqiya]] invaded [[e:sicily|Sicily]] at the invitation of the rebel Byzantine commander [[e:euphemius|Euphemius]]. [[e:palermo|Palermo]] fell in 831 and became the capital, but the conquest was slow: [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]] fell in 878, [[e:taormina|Taormina]] in 902 and [[e:rometta|Rometta]] in 965. [[e:malta|Malta]] was taken in 870.
emirate-of-sicily.r: After Fatimid takeover in 909, the [[e:kalbid-dynasty|Kalbid]] family ruled as [[e:emir|emirs]] from 948, beginning with [[e:hasan-al-kalbi|Hasan al-Kalbi]]. [[e:palermo|Palermo]] grew into one of the largest [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] cities; [[e:ibn-hawqal|Ibn Hawqal]] counted some 300 mosques. The [[e:arabs|Arabs]] introduced citrus, [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] cane, [[e:cotton|cotton]] and new irrigation techniques. Christians and [[e:jews|Jews]] lived as protected subjects, and [[e:siculo-arabic|Siculo-Arabic]], the ancestor of [[e:maltese-language|Maltese]], spread widely.
emirate-of-sicily.e: From the 1040s the [[e:emirate|emirate]] split among rival lords. One of them, [[e:ibn-al-thumna|Ibn al-Thumna]], invited the Normans, and Roger I took [[e:messina|Messina]] in 1061 and [[e:palermo|Palermo]] in 1072; [[e:noto-sicily|Noto]], the last Muslim stronghold, fell in 1091. Arab-Norman culture flourished under the Norman kings.

emirate-of-trarza.t: The emirate of south-western Mauritania whose rulers controlled the gum trade with Europeans and resisted French expansion on the Senegal River.
emirate-of-trarza.o: The Trarza [[e:emirate|emirate]] took shape in the 17th century among [[e:banu-hassan|Hassani Arab]] groups of south-western [[e:mauritania|Mauritania]], ruled by the Awlad Ahmed min [[e:daman|Daman]] lineage. It consolidated after the Char Bouba war of the 1670s, in which Hassani warriors defeated the [[e:berbers|Berber]] [[e:zawaya|Zawaya]] led by [[e:nasir-al-din-mauritanian-cleric|Nasir al-Din]].
emirate-of-trarza.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled a nomadic society of warriors, scholarly tribes, tributaries and enslaved labourers. Gum arabic, sold to the French at [[e:senegal-river|Senegal River]] posts and to the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and English at [[e:portendick|Portendick]], was their main source of wealth. [[e:ali-shandora|Ali Shandora]] in the early 18th century made Trarza a regional power, and the emirs dominated the [[s:waalo|Waalo]] kingdom.
emirate-of-trarza.e: [[e:emir|Emir]] [[e:muhammad-al-habib-of-trarza|Muhammad al-Habib]] fought the French governor [[e:louis-faidherbe|Faidherbe]] in the 1850s, losing control over [[s:waalo|Waalo]]. Trarza accepted a French [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1902 to 1903, and was absorbed into [[s:french-mauritania|French Mauritania]].

emirate-of-melitene.t: A Muslim frontier emirate at Malatya on the upper Euphrates that waged two centuries of raiding warfare against Byzantium.
emirate-of-melitene.o: [[e:malatya|Melitene]] was taken by the [[e:arabs|Arabs]] in the 7th century and changed hands repeatedly. In the 750s the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]] resettled and refortified it as a key fortress of the thughur, the frontier zone facing [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], and over time its governors, drawn from the local Arab tribe of [[e:banu-sulaym|Sulaym]], became a hereditary dynasty only loosely bound to [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]].
emirate-of-melitene.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] lived by war. Its garrison and volunteer fighters launched seasonal raids across the [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]] into Byzantine [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. Its most famous ruler, [[e:umar-al-aqta|Umar al-Aqta]], raided deep into [[e:asia-minor|Asia Minor]], allied with the [[s:paulician-state|Paulicians of Tephrike]] and in 863 sacked [[s:amisos|Amisos]] on the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] before being killed at the [[e:battle-of-lalakaon|battle of Lalakaon]]. The town also had a large Christian population and [[e:syriac|Syriac]] monasteries.
emirate-of-melitene.e: As [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] went on the offensive in the 10th century, [[e:malatya|Melitene]] was repeatedly besieged. In 934 the general [[e:john-kourkouas|John Kourkouas]] captured it and expelled Muslims who refused to convert, opening the way for Byzantine expansion to the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]].

euesperides.t: The westernmost Greek city of Cyrenaica, on the site of modern Benghazi, later refounded as Berenice.
euesperides.o: Euesperides was founded on the shore of a lagoon near modern Benghazi, probably in the early 6th century BCE, by settlers from the [[s:kingdom-of-cyrene|Kingdom of Cyrene]]. Its name recalls the [[e:garden-of-the-hesperides|Garden of the Hesperides]], placed nearby by Greek legend. [[e:arcesilaus-iv|Arcesilaus IV of Cyrene]] sent new colonists there in the 460s BCE.
euesperides.r: It was a self-governing Greek city with a mixed farming and trading economy, producing grain and [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] and exporting through its harbour. Excavations have found houses, pottery and coins. [[e:thucydides|Thucydides]] records that in 414 BCE the Spartan general [[e:gylippus|Gylippus]], sailing to [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]], helped the city lift a siege by Libyan tribes.
euesperides.e: Euesperides passed to the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]] in 322 BCE. In the mid-3rd century BCE its population moved to a new site, refounded as Berenice in honour of the wife of [[e:ptolemy-iii-euergetes|Ptolemy III]]. Berenice later grew into the city of Benghazi.

emirate-of-crete.t: Muslim emirate founded by Andalusian exiles that held Crete for over a century and made it a base for raiding the Byzantine Aegean.
emirate-of-crete.o: After a failed revolt in [[e:cordoba|Cordoba]] in 818, thousands of Andalusians were expelled from the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] [[e:emirate|Emirate]]. Many reached [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]], which they held for some years before being forced out. Led by [[e:abu-hafs-umar-al-iqritishi|Abu Hafs Umar]], they landed on Byzantine [[e:crete|Crete]] in the 820s, conquered the island and founded a fortified capital, [[e:heraklion|Chandax]], on the site of modern Heraklion.
emirate-of-crete.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled as a hereditary dynasty, nominally recognising the Abbasid [[e:caliphate|caliphs]], and Arabic and [[e:islam|Islam]] spread among part of the population. The [[e:emirate|emirate]] grew rich from raiding [[e:aegean|Aegean]] coasts, the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] and commerce with [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], and minted its own coins. It repelled several Byzantine expeditions, including those of 843, 911 and 949.
emirate-of-crete.e: In 960 the general [[e:nikephoros-ii-phokas|Nikephoros Phokas]] landed a great army and took [[e:heraklion|Chandax]] after a winter siege in March 961. The last emir, [[e:abd-al-aziz-ibn-shuayb|Abd al-Aziz ibn Shu'ayb]], was taken to [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]]. [[e:crete|Crete]] returned to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] and was re-Christianised.

eastern-turkic-khaganate.t: The eastern half of the first Turkic empire, which ruled Mongolia and dominated northern China until Tang Taizong crushed it in 630.
eastern-turkic-khaganate.o: When the [[e:first-turkic-khaganate|First Turkic Khaganate]] split around 603, the eastern [[e:khagan|khagans]] of the [[e:ashina-clan|Ashina clan]] held the Mongolian steppe, with their sacred centre at Otuken in the Khangai mountains. The [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui dynasty]] had encouraged the division, and the khagan [[e:qimin-khagan|Qimin]] was a Sui ally.
eastern-turkic-khaganate.r: The [[e:khagan|khagans]] led a confederation of Turkic and [[e:tiele|Tiele]] tribes, extracting [[e:silk|silk]] and tribute from the Chinese states. During the collapse of the [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]], [[e:shibi-khagan|Shibi Khagan]] besieged [[e:emperor-yang-of-sui|Emperor Yang]] at [[e:siege-of-yanmen|Yanmen]] in 615, and his successors backed Chinese rebels and threatened the new [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang dynasty]], reaching the [[e:wei-river|Wei River]] near [[e:changan|Chang'an]] in 626.
eastern-turkic-khaganate.e: Rebellion by the [[s:xueyantuo|Xueyantuo]] and other [[e:tiele|Tiele]] tribes and a severe winter weakened [[e:illig-qaghan|Illig Khagan]], and in 630 a [[s:later-tang|Tang]] army under [[e:li-jing|Li Jing]] captured him. The Turks were settled under Tang rule for fifty years until the [[s:second-turkic-khaganate|Second Turkic Khaganate]] revived their state in 682.

east-timor.t: Young South-East Asian republic that won independence in 2002 after Portuguese rule and a brutal Indonesian occupation.
east-timor.o: After Portugal withdrew from [[s:portuguese-timor|Portuguese Timor]], [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]] invaded in December 1975 and annexed the territory. Its occupation cost an estimated 100,000 or more lives through killing, famine and disease. Resistance led by [[e:fretilin|Fretilin]] and [[e:xanana-gusmao|Xanana Gusmao]] continued, and the [[e:santa-cruz-massacre|Santa Cruz massacre]] of 1991 drew world attention. In a UN-run referendum in August 1999, 78.5 per cent voted for independence.
east-timor.r: Pro-Indonesian militias then devastated the country until the Australian-led [[e:international-force-east-timor|INTERFET]] force arrived. After UN administration, the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste became independent on 20 May 2002, with [[e:xanana-gusmao|Gusmao]] as president. It is a semi-presidential democracy, overwhelmingly Catholic, with [[e:tetum-language|Tetum]] and Portuguese as official languages.
east-timor.e: The state survived a political crisis in 2006 and assassination attempts on its leaders in 2008. It depends heavily on offshore oil and gas revenue held in a petroleum fund, and joined [[e:association-of-southeast-asian-nations|ASEAN]] in 2025.

cr.a: See File history, below, for details.

empire-of-trebizond.t: A Byzantine successor state on the Black Sea, ruled by the Grand Komnenoi for over 250 years and the last Byzantine realm to fall.
empire-of-trebizond.o: In April 1204, just before the [[e:fourth-crusade|Fourth Crusade]] took [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]], Alexios and [[e:david-komnenos|David Komnenos]], grandsons of the emperor Andronikos I, seized [[e:trabzon|Trebizond]] with troops supplied by their relative [[e:tamar-of-georgia|Queen Tamar]] of [[s:georgia|Georgia]]. [[e:alexios-i-of-trebizond|Alexios I]] took the imperial title, founding the dynasty of the Grand Komnenoi.
empire-of-trebizond.r: [[e:trabzon|Trebizond]] controlled a narrow coastal strip backed by the Pontic mountains and grew rich as a terminus of the trade route from [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]], with Venetian and Genoese colonies in the city. Its rulers survived by paying tribute to [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]] and [[e:mongols|Mongols]] and marrying daughters to [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] princes, while [[e:alexios-iii-of-trebizond|Alexios III]] built churches and the [[e:sumela-monastery|Sumela]] monastery prospered. Greek scholarship flourished; the future cardinal [[e:bessarion|Bessarion]] was born there.
empire-of-trebizond.e: [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] besieged [[e:trabzon|Trebizond]] in 1461, eight years after the fall of [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]], and the emperor [[e:david-of-trebizond|David]] surrendered in August. He and most of his family were executed in 1463.

eastern-xia.t: A breakaway Jurchen state in eastern Manchuria founded by the Jin general Puxian Wannu, which held out between Jin, Mongols and Goryeo until 1233.
eastern-xia.o: [[e:puxian-wannu|Puxian Wannu]], a [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234) commander in [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]], was sent against the rebel [[e:yelu-liuge|Yelü Liuge]] of [[s:eastern-liao|Eastern Liao]] but was defeated. In 1215 he rebelled himself and proclaimed the kingdom of Great Zhen, later called Eastern Xia, moving north-east into the old [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] [[e:bantustan|homeland]] along the [[e:tumen|Tumen]] and Ussuri rivers.
eastern-xia.r: The state was organised on Jin lines, with [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] military units and walled towns such as its capital near modern [[e:yanji|Yanji]]. [[e:puxian-wannu|Puxian Wannu]] submitted to the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1216 and sent a son as hostage, but acted independently whenever possible, raiding and trading with [[s:goryeo|Goryeo]].
eastern-xia.e: Once the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] were ready to finish the Jin, they turned on Eastern Xia. In 1233 a Mongol army under [[e:guyuk-khan|Güyük]] captured [[e:puxian-wannu|Puxian Wannu]], and the state was absorbed into the [[s:mongol-empire|Mongol Empire]].

edzna.t: A Maya city in western Campeche known for its five-storey palace pyramid and an extensive system of canals and reservoirs.
edzna.o: Edzná occupied a flood-prone valley in [[e:campeche|Campeche]]. It was settled in the Preclassic, when inhabitants dug a large network of canals and a moat, and became an important centre in the [[e:late-classic-period|Late Classic]] from about 600 CE.
edzna.r: Its Great Acropolis carries the Building of the Five Storeys, combining a pyramid and palace rooms on each level. The city's architecture blends southern [[e:peten|Petén]] styles with the later [[e:puuc|Puuc]] and [[e:chenes|Chenes]] styles of the north. Hieroglyphic stairways and stelae record its rulers, though their history is only partly understood. Water management supported farming in the valley through the dry season.
edzna.e: Monument building at Edzná ended around 900 CE, and the city declined, though some Postclassic occupation continued. It is now a protected archaeological site in [[e:campeche|Campeche]].

emirate-of-hakkari.t: A Kurdish emirate in the mountains south-east of Lake Van, ruling Kurds and Assyrian Christians for nearly five centuries.
emirate-of-hakkari.o: The Hakkari mountains had long been held by Kurdish lords. In the late 14th century a dynasty based at [[e:julamerk|Julamerk]] (Colemerik) emerged; its emir [[e:izz-al-din-shir|Izz al-Din Shir]] submitted to [[e:timur|Timur]] and kept his lands, and his family ruled the region thereafter.
emirate-of-hakkari.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled a remote mountain land of Kurdish tribes and semi-autonomous Assyrian Christian tribes whose patriarch lived at [[e:qudshanis|Qudshanis]]. After 1514 they became Ottoman [[e:vassal|vassals]] with hereditary rule, sometimes switching to the [[e:safavid-empire|Safavids]]. Revenues came from flocks, tribute and the roads between Van and [[e:mosul|Mosul]].
emirate-of-hakkari.e: In the 19th century Ottoman centralisation and the revolt of the neighbouring emir [[e:bedir-khan-beg|Bedir Khan of Bohtan]], in which Hakkari's emir [[e:nurullah-bey|Nurullah Bey]] took part, led to the [[e:emirate|emirate]]'s abolition in the mid 1840s.

el-mirador.t: The greatest Preclassic Maya city, in the northern Petén forest, with some of the largest pyramids ever built and causeways linking it to neighbouring centres.
el-mirador.o: Settlement at El Mirador expanded from about 600 BCE in the [[e:mirador-basin|Mirador Basin]] of northern [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]]. Fertile swamp soils, carried up to build raised gardens, supported a population large enough for monumental building on a scale unmatched in later Maya history.
el-mirador.r: The La [[s:danta-state|Danta]] and El [[s:tigray|Tigre]] complexes are among the largest structures of the ancient world by volume. Stucco masks of deities decorated platform façades, and raised causeways (sakbeob) linked El Mirador with [[e:nakbe|Nakbe]], [[e:el-tintal|Tintal]] and other sites, suggesting a regional state. Some scholars connect it with the later snake-head emblem of the [[s:kingdom-of-kaan|Kingdom of Kaan]], but this remains debated.
el-mirador.e: El Mirador was largely abandoned around 150 CE, possibly through environmental degradation, drought or political collapse, a crisis shared across the basin. A smaller [[e:late-classic-period|Late Classic]] reoccupation followed. Its rediscovery showed that Maya civilisation reached great complexity centuries earlier than once thought.

empire-of-vietnam.t: The short-lived Japanese-backed Vietnamese state proclaimed by Emperor Bao Dai after Japan ousted the French in March 1945.
empire-of-vietnam.o: On 9 March 1945 Japanese forces overthrew the French administration across [[s:french-indochina|French Indochina]]. On 11 March Emperor [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]], at [[e:japan|Japan's]] urging, declared the treaties of protection with [[e:france|France]] void and proclaimed the independence of the Empire of [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]], covering [[s:french-protectorate-of-annam|Annam]] and [[s:french-protectorate-of-tonkin|Tonkin]].
empire-of-vietnam.r: [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]] appointed a cabinet of non-communist intellectuals under the historian [[e:tran-trong-kim|Tran Trong Kim]], which reintroduced Vietnamese as the language of administration, revised school curricula and negotiated the return of [[s:french-cochinchina|Cochinchina]] and the cities of [[e:hanoi|Hanoi]], [[e:haiphong|Haiphong]] and [[e:da-nang|Da Nang]] from Japanese control. Its power was limited by the Japanese military and by the famine then devastating the north.
empire-of-vietnam.e: After [[e:japan|Japan's]] surrender, the [[e:viet-minh|Viet Minh]] launched the [[e:august-revolution|August Revolution]] and seized [[e:hanoi|Hanoi]]. [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]] announced his abdication on 25 August 1945 and handed his seal and sword to Viet Minh representatives on 30 August; on 2 September [[e:ho-chi-minh|Ho Chi Minh]] declared the [[s:democratic-republic-of-vietnam|Democratic Republic of Vietnam]].

eastern-wu.t: The Three Kingdoms state of the Sun family in the lower Yangtze, which held the south with river fleets for six decades and laid the base of Nanjing as a capital.
eastern-wu.o: [[e:sun-ce|Sun Ce]], son of [[e:sun-jian|Sun Jian]], a general against the [[e:yellow-turban-rebellion|Yellow Turbans]], conquered the region south of the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] in the 190s. Sun Ce's brother [[e:sun-quan|Sun Quan]] defeated [[e:cao-cao|Cao Cao]] at [[e:battle-of-red-cliffs|Red Cliffs]] with [[e:liu-bei|Liu Bei]] in 208, took Jing province from [[e:guan-yu|Guan Yu]] in 219 and beat Liu Bei at [[e:battle-of-xiaoting|Yiling]] in 222. He declared himself emperor in 229, with his capital at [[e:jiankang|Jianye]] ([[e:nanjing|Nanjing]]).
eastern-wu.r: Wu relied on powerful southern clans and large navies, with [[e:military-colony|military colonies]] developing the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] delta and the far south. [[e:sun-quan|Sun Quan]] sent fleets to the island of Yizhou and envoys such as [[e:zhu-ying|Zhu Ying]] and [[e:kang-tai|Kang Tai]] to [[s:funan|Funan]] in South-[[e:east-asia|East Asia]]. Northern refugees and settlers spread farming southwards.
eastern-wu.e: After [[e:sun-quan|Sun Quan's]] death in 252, succession struggles weakened the state, and the last emperor, [[e:sun-hao|Sun Hao]], became notorious for cruelty. In 280 [[s:western-jin|Western Jin]] fleets descended the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] from [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] and Sun Hao surrendered, reuniting [[e:china|China]].

equinoctial-france.t: A short-lived French colony on the island of Maranhão whose fort, Saint-Louis, survives as the city of São Luís in northern Brazil.
equinoctial-france.o: In 1612 an expedition led by [[e:daniel-de-la-touche|Daniel de La Touche]], seigneur de La Ravardière, and François de Razilly, with [[e:capuchins|Capuchin]] friars, landed on the island of [[e:maranhao|Maranhão]] on [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] northern coast. They built [[e:sao-luis-maranhao|Fort Saint-Louis]], named after King [[e:louis-xiii-of-france|Louis XIII]], and allied with local [[e:tupinamba|Tupinambá]] groups.
equinoctial-france.r: The colony was a small trading and missionary outpost. The [[e:capuchins|Capuchins]] [[e:claude-dabbeville|Claude d'Abbeville]] and [[e:yves-devreux|Yves d'Évreux]] wrote detailed accounts of the [[e:tupinamba|Tupinambá]], and [[e:abbeville|Abbeville]] took several Tupinambá to [[e:paris|Paris]], where they were baptised before the court in 1613. French support from home was weak, and the settlers relied on indigenous allies for food and protection.
equinoctial-france.e: Portugal, then united with [[e:spain|Spain]], sent forces under [[e:jeronimo-de-albuquerque-maranhao|Jerónimo de Albuquerque]], who defeated the French at [[e:battle-of-guaxenduba|Guaxenduba]] in 1614. [[e:daniel-de-la-touche|La Ravardière]] surrendered [[e:sao-luis-maranhao|Saint-Louis]] in 1615. The Portuguese kept the town as [[e:sao-luis|São Luís]], later capital of the [[s:state-of-maranhao|State of Maranhão]].

earldom-of-ulster.t: The Anglo-Norman lordship of eastern Ulster founded by John de Courcy and held by the de Burghs, whose collapse in 1333 opened the way to Gaelic recovery.
earldom-of-ulster.o: [[e:john-de-courcy|John de Courcy]] invaded [[s:northern-ireland|Ulster]] in 1177 and ruled it from [[e:carrickfergus|Carrickfergus]] and [[e:downpatrick|Downpatrick]]. In 1205 [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] expelled him and created the earldom of Ulster for [[e:hugh-de-lacy-earl-of-ulster|Hugh de Lacy]]. After de Lacy's death the earldom passed in 1263 to [[e:walter-de-burgh-1st-earl-of-ulster|Walter de Burgh]].
earldom-of-ulster.r: The earls held coastal [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]] and Down with castles, towns such as [[e:carrickfergus|Carrickfergus]] and [[e:coleraine|Coleraine]], and manors worked by English settlers. [[e:richard-og-de-burgh-2nd-earl-of-ulster|Richard de Burgh]], the Red Earl, was the most powerful lord in Ireland around 1300, overlord of the [[e:o-neill-dynasty|O'Neills]] and lord of much of [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Connacht]]. [[e:edward-bruce|Edward Bruce's]] invasion of 1315 to 1318 devastated the earldom.
earldom-of-ulster.e: In 1333 [[e:william-donn-de-burgh-3rd-earl-of-ulster|William Donn de Burgh]], the Brown Earl, was murdered by his own [[e:vassal|vassals]] at a ford near [[e:belfast|Belfast]]. The earldom passed by marriage to the English royal family, but Gaelic lords such as the [[e:clandeboye-oneills|O'Neills of Clandeboye]] reoccupied most of its lands.

electorate-of-hesse.t: Hesse-Kassel as an electorate whose rulers kept the electoral title for sixty years after the Empire ended.
electorate-of-hesse.o: Landgrave [[e:william-i-elector-of-hesse|William IX of Hesse-Kassel]], enriched by hiring out soldiers to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], was made an elector in the [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Imperial Recess of 1803]] and took the title Elector William I. The [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] ended in 1806 before he could take part in an imperial election.
electorate-of-hesse.r: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] dispossessed William in 1806 and his lands became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]]. Restored in 1813, he cancelled the French reforms and kept the title of elector. A constitution was granted in 1831, but [[e:frederick-william-elector-of-hesse|Frederick William I]] quarrelled with his parliament, leading to a crisis in 1850 that nearly brought war between [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:austria|Austria]]. [[e:kassel|Kassel]], the capital, retained the [[e:bergpark-wilhelmshohe|Wilhelmshöhe]] palace park.
electorate-of-hesse.e: [[e:hesse|Hesse]] sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in the [[e:austro-prussian-war|Austro-Prussian War]] of 1866. [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] occupied it and annexed it, forming the [[e:province-of-hesse-nassau|Province of Hesse-Nassau]] with the [[s:duchy-of-nassau|Duchy of Nassau]] and [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]].

etiuni.t: A confederation of tribes around Lake Sevan and the Ararat plain, whose conquest by Urartu opened the way for the founding of Erebuni, the forerunner of Yerevan.
etiuni.o: Known only from Urartian royal inscriptions. In the 9th century BCE the name Etiuni covered a cluster of tribal lands north of the [[e:aras-river|Araxes]], around [[e:lake-sevan|Lake Sevan]] and the plain beneath [[e:mount-aragats|Mount Aragats]], which the expanding [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Kingdom of Urartu]] treated as one hostile country.
etiuni.r: The union was a loose alliance of local chiefdoms living from [[e:cattle|cattle]] herding, farming and bronze and iron working, with hill fortresses of the kind still visible around [[e:lake-sevan|Sevan]]. Urartian texts list captured people and livestock in the thousands, showing a populous region but saying little about its institutions.
etiuni.e: [[e:argishti-i|Argishti I]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Kingdom of Urartu]] conquered much of Etiuni in a series of campaigns in the early 8th century BCE, and his successor Sarduri II campaigned there again. Captives were resettled at the new fortress of [[e:erebuni|Erebuni]], founded in 782 BCE, and the region became an Urartian province.

emirate-of-transjordan.t: The British-protected emirate of Abdullah east of the Jordan, the forerunner of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.
emirate-of-transjordan.o: After the French expelled his brother Faisal from [[e:damascus|Damascus]], Abdullah, son of [[e:hussein-bin-ali-king-of-hejaz|Sharif Husayn]] of [[e:mecca|Mecca]], arrived at Ma'an with followers in late 1920. At the [[e:cairo|Cairo]] conference of March 1921 [[e:winston-churchill|Winston Churchill]] agreed that he would govern the land east of the [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Jordan]] under British mandate, separate from [[s:mandatory-palestine|Mandatory Palestine]].
emirate-of-transjordan.r: Abdullah built a state from [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] tribes and small towns, making [[e:amman|Amman]] his capital. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] controlled finance and foreign affairs and funded the Arab [[e:legion|Legion]], built up by [[e:frederick-peake|Frederick Peake]] and later [[e:john-glubb|John Glubb]]. The 1922 mandate memorandum excluded Transjordan from the provisions for a Jewish national home. A 1928 treaty and organic law established a legislative council.
emirate-of-transjordan.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] recognised the [[e:emirate|emirate]]'s independence by the Treaty of London of March 1946, and on 25 May Abdullah was proclaimed king of what became, from 1949, the [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan]].

east-hebei-autonomous-government.t: A Japanese-sponsored puppet administration in eastern Hebei that served as a channel for smuggling and as a step towards Japan's war on China.
east-hebei-autonomous-government.o: The [[e:tanggu-truce|Tanggu Truce]] of 1933 created a demilitarised zone south of the [[e:great-wall-of-china|Great Wall]]. In November 1935, as [[e:japan|Japan]] pressed for the separation of northern [[e:china|China]], the local administrator [[e:yin-rugeng|Yin Rugeng]] declared the twenty-two counties of eastern [[e:hebei|Hebei]] autonomous from the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]], with its seat at [[e:tongzhou-district|Tongzhou]] near [[e:beijing|Beijing]].
east-hebei-autonomous-government.r: The administration was dependent on the Japanese army. It charged its own low customs rates, which allowed Japanese goods, [[e:silver|silver]] and narcotics to flood into northern [[e:china|China]], undermining the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]]'s revenues. Its peace preservation corps provided local security.
east-hebei-autonomous-government.e: In July 1937, soon after the [[e:lugou-bridge|Marco Polo Bridge]] incident, its own Chinese security troops mutinied at [[e:tongzhou-district|Tongzhou]] and killed many Japanese and Korean residents. The regime was absorbed into the [[s:provisional-government-of-the-republic-of-china|Provisional Government of the Republic of China]] in February 1938.

electorate-of-hanover.t: The Brunswick-Lüneburg electorate whose rulers became kings of Great Britain, linking a north German state to a global empire.
electorate-of-hanover.o: Duke [[e:ernest-augustus-elector-of-hanover|Ernest Augustus]] of Brunswick-[[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]], ruling from [[e:hanover|Hanover]], was granted a ninth electoral dignity by [[e:leopold-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Leopold]] I in 1692 in return for military support, though it was recognised by the [[e:imperial-diet|Imperial Diet]] only in 1708. His wife [[e:sophia-of-hanover|Sophia]] was named heir to the British throne by the [[e:act-of-settlement-1701|Act of Settlement]] of 1701.
electorate-of-hanover.r: In 1714 [[e:sophia-of-hanover|Sophia]]'s son [[e:george-i-of-great-britain|George Louis]] became King George I of [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Great Britain]], and [[e:hanover|Hanover]] was governed by a privy council while the [[e:prince-elector|electors]] lived mostly in [[e:london|London]]. The state was Lutheran, agrarian and conservative, run by a nobility-dominated administration. [[e:george-ii-of-great-britain|George II]] founded the [[e:university-of-gottingen|University of Göttingen]] in 1734, which became a leading centre of learning. The [[e:herrenhausen-gardens|Herrenhausen]] gardens survive from Sophia's time.
electorate-of-hanover.e: [[e:hanover|Hanover]] was occupied by [[e:france|France]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in the Napoleonic wars and partly absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]]. In 1814 the restored state was raised to the [[s:kingdom-of-hanover|Kingdom of Hanover]] at the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]].

eastern-buyeo.t: A branch kingdom of Buyeo near the Korean east coast, remembered in Korean legend as the birthplace of Goguryeo's founder Jumong.
eastern-buyeo.o: The 12th-century [[e:samguk-sagi|Samguk sagi]] relates that King [[e:haeburu|Haeburu of Buyeo]] moved his court east to a place called Gaseopwon on divine advice, founding Eastern [[s:buyeo|Buyeo]], traditionally in 86 BCE. Its location is uncertain, perhaps in the [[e:tumen|Tumen]] river region. The story is legendary in detail and Chinese sources do not clearly distinguish it from Buyeo itself.
eastern-buyeo.r: Korean tradition names three kings, [[e:haeburu|Haeburu]], [[e:geumwa|Geumwa]] and [[e:daeso|Daeso]]. In the legend Geumwa took in [[e:yuhwa|Yuhwa]], mother of [[e:dongmyeong-of-goguryeo|Jumong]], who later fled south to found [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]]. Little else is known of its government or society, which presumably resembled that of [[s:buyeo|Buyeo]].
eastern-buyeo.e: Rivalry with [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] ended in war: [[e:daemusin-of-goguryeo|King Daemusin]] of Goguryeo invaded and King [[e:daeso|Daeso]] was killed in 22 CE, after which members of the royal house submitted to Goguryeo.

emirate-of-atsiz.t: The first Turkish state in southern Syria and Palestine, carved out by the Turkmen commander Atsiz at the expense of the Fatimids.
emirate-of-atsiz.o: [[e:atsiz-ibn-uvaq|Atsiz ibn Uvaq]] was a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] commander who entered Fatimid service as Turkish bands spread into [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] after the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuk]] victories. Around 1071 he took [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] and [[e:ramla|Ramla]] for himself, and in 1076 he captured [[e:damascus|Damascus]], proclaiming the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid]] [[e:caliphate|caliph]] and the Seljuk sultan in [[e:khutba|Friday prayers]].
emirate-of-atsiz.r: His rule rested on [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] warriors and was harsh: [[e:damascus|Damascus]] suffered famine and extortion, and when [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] rebelled in 1077 he retook it and massacred many inhabitants. In 1077 he invaded [[e:egypt|Egypt]] but was defeated near [[e:cairo|Cairo]]. His state was a military domain with little administration of its own.
emirate-of-atsiz.e: Threatened by a Fatimid counter-offensive, [[e:atsiz-ibn-uvaq|Atsiz]] asked [[e:malik-shah-i|Malik-Shah]] for help. The sultan sent his brother [[e:tutush-i|Tutush]], who had Atsiz killed in 1079 and took [[e:damascus|Damascus]], founding the [[s:seljuk-sultanate-of-syria|Seljuk Sultanate of Syria]].

electorate-of-salzburg.t: Short-lived electorate created from the secularised archbishopric of Salzburg for a Habsburg prince who had lost Tuscany.
electorate-of-salzburg.o: Archbishop [[e:hieronymus-von-colloredo|Hieronymus von Colloredo]] fled [[e:salzburg|Salzburg]] before French troops in 1800. Under the [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Imperial Recess of 1803]] the prince-archbishopric was secularised and given, together with [[e:berchtesgaden|Berchtesgaden]] and parts of [[e:passau|Passau]] and [[e:eichstatt|Eichstätt]], to [[e:ferdinand-iii-grand-duke-of-tuscany|Ferdinand III]], the former [[e:grand-duke-of-tuscany|Grand Duke of Tuscany]], who received an electoral title.
electorate-of-salzburg.r: Ferdinand's brief rule brought a reorganised administration and a secular government in place of the archbishops, though the population remained Catholic. The university was continued, and [[e:salzburg|Salzburg's]] economy still relied on salt mining at [[e:hallein|Hallein]] and trade. The electorate had little time to develop before war returned.
electorate-of-salzburg.e: After [[e:austria|Austria's]] defeat at [[e:battle-of-austerlitz|Austerlitz]], the [[e:peace-of-pressburg-1805|Peace of Pressburg]] in December 1805 gave [[e:salzburg|Salzburg]] to the [[s:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire]], and Ferdinand was compensated with [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]]. Salzburg later passed to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] from 1810 to 1816 before returning permanently to Austria.

early-cholas.t: The Sangam-age Chola kings of the Kaveri delta, remembered for the hero Karikala and the great port of Puhar.
early-cholas.o: The [[s:chola-empire|Cholas]] were one of the three crowned dynasties of ancient [[e:tamilakam|Tamilakam]], with the [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]] and the [[e:chera-dynasty|Cheras]]. [[e:ashoka|Ashoka's]] edicts in the 3rd century BCE name them among independent peoples to the south of his empire. Their [[e:bantustan|homeland]] was the fertile Kaveri delta, with an inland capital at [[e:uraiyur|Uraiyur]], near modern [[e:tiruchirappalli|Tiruchirappalli]], and a port at [[e:puhar|Puhar]], also called Kaveripattinam.
early-cholas.r: [[e:sangam-literature|Sangam]] poems celebrate [[e:karikala-chola|Karikala]], who defeated a coalition of [[e:chera-dynasty|Cheras]] and [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]] at [[e:battle-of-venni|Venni]] and is credited by tradition with the [[e:kallanai-dam|Kallanai]], an early dam across the Kaveri. The poem Pattinappalai describes [[e:puhar|Puhar]] as a bustling harbour where foreign merchants unloaded horses and goods. [[e:rice|Rice]] farming on the delta supported the kingdom, and [[e:chola-empire|Chola]] adventurers, such as [[e:ellalan|Elara]], at times ruled in [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]].
early-cholas.e: From around the 3rd century the [[s:chola-empire|Cholas]] lost power during the obscure age of the [[s:kalabhra-dynasty|Kalabhra dynasty]] and survived only as local chiefs, later under the [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallava dynasty]]. The line revived in 848, when [[e:vijayalaya-chola|Vijayalaya]] took [[e:thanjavur|Thanjavur]] and began the [[e:chola-empire|Chola Empire]].
early-cholas.re: Tamil folk religion, Vedic religion, Buddhism, Jainism

eblani.t: People of eastern Ireland named in Ptolemy's Geography, whose town Eblana has often, though doubtfully, been linked with Dublin.
eblani.o: The Eblani are known only from the [[e:geography-ptolemy|Geography of Ptolemy]], compiled around 150 from earlier sailors' reports. He places them on the east coast of Ireland, south of the [[s:voluntii|Voluntii]] and north of the [[s:cauci|Cauci]], roughly in the area of modern [[e:county-dublin|County Dublin]] and [[s:kingdom-of-mide|Meath]], with a town called [[e:eblana|Eblana]].
eblani.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers, society or customs. The resemblance of [[e:eblana|Eblana]] to [[e:dublin|Dublin]] led older writers to identify the two, but most scholars now doubt the link, since Dublin's name is Irish and Ptolemy's coordinates are imprecise. Archaeology shows Roman goods reaching the east coast at sites such as [[e:drumanagh|Drumanagh]].
eblani.e: The Eblani do not appear in any later source, and no Irish tradition preserves their name. Their area later fell within the territory of the [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Kingdom of Leinster]] and of the rising [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]] dynasties of [[s:kingdom-of-brega|Brega]].

east-breifne.t: The O'Reilly lordship of County Cavan, a Gaelic state with a town at Cavan whose 'O'Reilly money' circulated in the Pale, until the Plantation of Ulster.
east-breifne.o: East Breifne emerged when the [[s:kingdom-of-breifne|Kingdom of Breifne]] split in 1256 and the [[e:o-raghallaigh|O'Reillys]], Muintir Mhaoilmhordha, took the eastern part. They founded the town of Cavan beside their castle on Tullymongan hill and a Franciscan friary, and also held the island fortress of [[e:clough-oughter-castle|Clough Oughter]].
east-breifne.r: The [[e:o-raghallaigh|O'Reillys]] traded with the [[e:the-pale|Pale]], and their 'O'Reilly money', clipped coins circulating in the 15th century, was common enough to be banned by the [[e:parliament-of-ireland|Irish Parliament]] in 1447. The lordship was organised in Gaelic fashion, with tanistry, brehon law and a hereditary learned class.
east-breifne.e: Under the [[e:house-of-tudor|Tudors]] the area became County Cavan in 1584. After the Nine Years' War and the Flight of the Earls it was included in the [[e:plantation-of-ulster|Plantation of Ulster]] from 1609, with lands granted to English and Scottish settlers.

emirate-of-bukhara.t: The Manghit state of Bukhara, a conservative Islamic emirate that survived as a Russian protectorate until the Red Army stormed its capital in 1920.
emirate-of-bukhara.o: [[e:muhammad-rahim-of-bukhara|Muhammad Rahim]] of the [[e:manghit-dynasty|Manghit]] tribe took real power in the [[s:khanate-of-bukhara|Khanate of Bukhara]] in the 1740s under [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah's]] protection. In 1785 [[e:shah-murad|Shah Murad]], a pious ruler, set aside the [[e:janid-dynasty|Janid]] figurehead khans and took the title emir, founding the [[e:emirate|Emirate]] of [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]].
emirate-of-bukhara.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled through [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] tribal chiefs, a clerical elite and officials, enforcing Islamic law strictly. [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] had hundreds of mosques and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]] and was a centre of trade in [[e:cotton|cotton]], karakul and [[e:silk|silk]]. Emir [[e:nasrullah-khan-emir-of-bukhara|Nasrullah]] executed the British officers [[e:charles-stoddart|Stoddart]] and [[e:arthur-conolly|Conolly]] in 1842. Wars with the [[s:khanate-of-kokand|Khanate of Kokand]] and [[e:khiva|Khiva]] were frequent.
emirate-of-bukhara.e: [[e:russia|Russia]] defeated [[e:emir|Emir]] Muzaffar in 1868, taking [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]] and making [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]] a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]. In 1920 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] and the [[e:young-bukharans|Young Bukharans]] stormed Bukhara, the last emir, [[e:mohammed-alim-khan|Alim Khan]], fled to [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]], and the [[s:bukharan-peoples-soviet-republic|Bukharan People's Soviet Republic]] was founded.

english-tangier.t: Tangier under English rule after it came as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry, a costly garrison abandoned after twenty-two years.
english-tangier.o: In 1661 the [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]] ceded [[e:tangier|Tangier]] to [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]] as part of the dowry of [[e:catherine-of-braganza|Catherine of Braganza]]. English troops took over in January 1662, hoping to make it a naval base controlling the [[e:strait-of-gibraltar|Strait of Gibraltar]].
english-tangier.r: [[e:tangier|Tangier]] was governed by military governors such as the [[e:andrew-rutherford-1st-earl-of-teviot|Earl of Teviot]], who was killed in an ambush in 1664. The English built a great mole to create a harbour and granted the town a municipal charter in 1668. The garrison was under constant pressure from Moroccan forces, especially after [[e:moulay-ismail|Moulay Ismail]] of the [[s:alaouite-sultanate|Alaouite Sultanate]] came to power.
english-tangier.e: With costs rising and Parliament unwilling to pay, [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]] ordered the evacuation. In 1684 the English blew up the mole and fortifications, with [[e:samuel-pepys|Samuel Pepys]] among the officials present, and left the town to [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]].

eastern-guo.t: A Ji-clan state near Xingyang founded by a brother of King Wen of Zhou and swallowed by the newly arrived State of Zheng in 767 BCE.
eastern-guo.o: Eastern [[e:guo-state|Guo]] was established early in the [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] by Guo Shu or Guo Zhong, younger brothers of [[e:king-wen-of-zhou|King Wen]], whose descendants held two separate Guo states. The eastern one, centred at Zhi near modern [[e:xingyang|Xingyang]] in [[e:henan|Henan]], guarded the approaches to the eastern capital at [[e:luoyang|Luoyi]].
eastern-guo.r: Its rulers were close kin of the [[e:zhou-dynasty|Zhou]] kings, but little else is known of their government. The state controlled strategic ground near the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]] and the [[e:xingyang|Xingyang]] pass.
eastern-guo.e: When the [[e:zhou-dynasty|Zhou]] court moved east in 770 BCE, [[e:duke-huan-of-zheng|Duke Huan of Zheng]] had already deposited his family and treasure with Eastern [[e:guo-state|Guo]] and nearby Kuai. His son Duke Wu of [[s:state-of-zheng|Zheng]] conquered Eastern Guo in 767 BCE, and the State of Zheng built its power on its lands.

ecab.t: The Maya province at the north-eastern tip of Yucatán, the first part of mainland Mexico seen by a Spanish expedition in 1517.
ecab.o: Ecab (Ekab) emerged after the fall of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441 in the north-east corner of the peninsula, facing [[e:isla-mujeres|Isla Mujeres]] and [[s:cozumel|Cozumel]]. Its main town, Ecab, impressed [[e:francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-yucatan-conquistador|Francisco Hernández de Córdoba]] in 1517, who called it '[[e:esztergom|Gran]] [[e:cairo|Cairo]]'.
ecab.r: Ecab was a coastal province whose towns lived from fishing, salt and the seaborne trade that passed around the peninsula. Little is known of its rulers or internal organisation, which colonial records describe only briefly.
ecab.e: Ecab resisted early Spanish incursions but was conquered in the 1540s by [[e:francisco-de-montejo-the-nephew|Francisco de Montejo the Nephew]]. Its population declined sharply under colonial rule and the town was later abandoned.

eridu.t: One of the oldest settlements in southern Mesopotamia, remembered by the Sumerians as the first city to receive kingship and as the home of the water god Enki.
eridu.o: Eridu was settled around 5400 BCE on a sandy rise at the edge of the marshes near the ancient shore of the Gulf, in the [[e:ubaid-period|Ubaid period]]. Excavations by [[e:fuad-safar|Fuad Safar]] and [[e:seton-lloyd|Seton Lloyd]] in 1946 to 1949 uncovered a sequence of some eighteen superimposed temples, growing from a single mud-brick room into a monumental platform shrine.
eridu.r: The city was above all a sacred place, the seat of [[e:enki|Enki]] (Akkadian Ea), god of fresh water, crafts and wisdom, whose temple was called the [[e:e-abzu|E-abzu]]. The [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]] opens with the words that kingship first descended from heaven at Eridu, naming the legendary kings [[e:alulim|Alulim]] and Alalngar. Its population was small compared with nearby Ur, and little is known of its secular government.
eridu.e: By the [[e:early-dynastic-period|Early Dynastic period]] Eridu had lost political weight to Ur, though it remained a revered cult centre; [[e:ur-nammu|Ur-Nammu]] and his successors of the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]] built a [[e:ziggurat|ziggurat]] there. The site was largely abandoned by the mid-first millennium BCE, but its myths of [[e:enki|Enki]] and the first city endured in Mesopotamian literature.

emirate-of-bitlis.t: A Kurdish emirate that ruled Bitlis for centuries and produced Sharaf Khan Bidlisi, author of the Sharafnama, the first history of the Kurds.
emirate-of-bitlis.o: [[e:bitlis|Bitlis]], at a gorge south-west of [[e:lake-van|Lake Van]], came under the Rojiki, a Kurdish tribal confederation, whose [[e:emir|emirs]] claimed descent from ancient Kurdish lords. Their rule is traditionally dated from the late 12th century, though early details rest on the family's own later history.
emirate-of-bitlis.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled from [[e:bitlis|Bitlis]] castle over a mountain district controlling the road from [[e:iran|Iran]] to the [[e:tigris|Tigris]]. After 1514 they accepted Ottoman suzerainty with hereditary autonomy, alternating between Ottoman and Safavid sides. Emir [[e:sharaf-khan-bidlisi|Sharaf Khan Bidlisi]] completed the [[e:sharafnama|Sharafnama]] in Persian in 1597, a history of Kurdish dynasties. [[e:evliya-celebi|Evliya Celebi]] described the rich court of [[e:abdal-khan|Abdal Khan]] in 1655, shortly before an Ottoman army attacked him.
emirate-of-bitlis.e: In the 19th-century Ottoman centralisation the hereditary [[e:emir|emirs]] were removed, and [[e:bitlis|Bitlis]] was placed under appointed governors by 1849.

earldom-of-orkney.t: Norse earldom of the Orkney and Shetland islands, the heart of a sea-based power in northern Britain for six centuries, recorded in the Orkneyinga saga.
earldom-of-orkney.o: Norse settlers took over [[e:orkney|Orkney]] in the 9th century, displacing or absorbing the Pictish population. According to the [[e:orkneyinga-saga|Orkneyinga saga]], [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] granted the islands to Earl [[e:rognvald-eysteinsson|Rognvald of Møre]], who passed them to his brother [[e:sigurd-eysteinsson|Sigurd]], the first earl, in the late 9th century.
earldom-of-orkney.r: The earls owed allegiance to the kings of [[e:norway|Norway]], and later also to the kings of [[e:scotland|Scotland]] for [[e:caithness|Caithness]], but often acted independently. [[e:thorfinn-the-mighty|Thorfinn the Mighty]], in the 11th century, ruled much of northern Scotland and built a minster at [[e:birsay|Birsay]]. [[e:magnus-erlendsson|Earl Magnus]], murdered around 1117, was venerated as a saint, and his nephew [[e:rognvald-kali-kolsson|Rögnvald Kali Kolsson]] began [[e:st-magnus-cathedral|St Magnus Cathedral]] in [[e:kirkwall|Kirkwall]] in 1137.
earldom-of-orkney.e: After the Norse line died out in 1231, Scottish families held the earldom, ending with the [[e:clan-sinclair|Sinclairs]]. In 1468 Christian I of [[s:denmark-norway|Denmark-Norway]] pledged [[e:orkney|Orkney]] to [[e:james-iii-of-scotland|James III of Scotland]] as security for his daughter Margaret's dowry, and in 1472 the earldom was annexed to the Scottish crown. Norse law and the [[e:norn-language|Norn language]] lingered for centuries.
